chapters.title: Chapter 3996: Trembling! III
paragraphs: Many Dukes throughout the assembled forces looked toward the cluster of Paradoxes with gazes that carried undisguised animosity.

For many of them, the relationship with Living Paradoxes had been defined by warfare that stretched across eons...conflicts in which Diviticus and other Dukes present had killed uncountable numbers of their allies.
The idea of accepting such beings as partners rather than enemies required adjustments to thinking that had been refined through countless cycles of violence and retribution.
In this moment of heavy contemplation, Moiraine began to float back toward Noah’s position.
Yet Noah’s mental voice reached her consciousness with firm instructions that halted her advance before it could draw unwanted attention.
’Do not,’ he conveyed, ’Remain where you are and continue appearing as the source of enhancement that benefits all present.’
His expression grew heavy as he observed this unfolding situation with the seriousness it demanded.
Right now, he seemed to be nothing more than an Extra with very little apparent power while Diviticus commanded center stage.
But this was okay!
Noah released a sigh that carried the weight of choices, acknowledging that he had chosen this path when he made the Festival of War resonate from Moiraine’s position rather than his own.
Not being in the spotlight every now and then was okay.

At this moment of personal reflection, Noah found himself sympathetically understanding how all those discarded extras in his own fable must have felt when their contributions were overlooked in favor of more prominent characters.
The sensation of being reduced to irrelevance despite possessing capabilities that exceeded those who commanded attention was humbling!
It was in this moment of heavy contemplation that existence itself convulsed!
A blaring purple brilliance blazed from above as reality tore itself open to accommodate the passage of someone whose presence was heavy.

From the temporal rift emerged the visage of an extremely gorgeous woman. Her stellar purple hair flowed like liquid starlight given form and direction, while her dress seemed to contain within its fabric the compressed essence of temporal authority refined to its purest expression.

She smoked a pipe whose contents blazed with inner radiance, yet her attention focused immediately upon the figure of Duke Schrodinger with the kind of recognition that suggested their relationship stretched across eons of history.
"I thought I smelled a dirty beggar in my Transcendent Temporal Folds," she said. "How many millions of years has it been now, Schrodinger? Since when did you let children begin speaking for you?"

As she delivered this casual insult, she barely glanced toward Diviticus, yet that momentary attention carried within it the weight of assessment and dismissal that made the assembled Paradox Duke’s expression grow cold.
This...was Aion, the Temporal Watcher...a being whose authority over time itself had been legendary since epochs that predated current existence!
Toward her provocative words, the beggar-looking Schrodinger smiled with patient amusement that suggested he had been expecting exactly this development.
"Sometimes," he replied, "one has to sit back and let the younger generation lead. Age brings wisdom about when to act and when to observe."
Aion smoked her pipe with movements that seemed to slow time around her position, each inhalation drawing in possibilities while each exhalation released certainties into the surrounding space.
She nodded as if considering his response, then...
WAP!
She vanished from her position above the battlefield, reality bending around her passage until she materialized directly beside Moiraine!

"You have gotten rusty, old friend," she said to Schrodinger with voice that carried across impossible distances without losing any of its clarity. "I can see your gaze and the hungry attention of this loud Diviticus looking toward this Moiraine here with calculations..."
She gestured toward the Living Paradox whose position had become the center during this battle!

"She appears to have come before you other Paradoxes to lend aid against Dead Existences. If anyone should have a seat at the table of governance, should it not be her? Young, perhaps a bit weaker than established powers, certainly easier to manipulate into serving larger agendas..."
Schrodinger’s smile deepened at her provocative analysis.
"You are letting your true thoughts be heard out loud again, Aion," he observed with gentle reproach.
Aion nodded with calm acknowledgment of his criticism.

"Of course. I believe in being straightforward about intentions and motivations rather than hiding behind pretense and manufactured courtesy. And what I want most in this situation is the precise opposite of whatever you are seeking to achieve, you manipulative fucking beggar."
BOOM!
The exchange between these terrifying beings carried undertones that spoke to conflicts and competitions that stretched across eons of shared history!
Their true auras flared outward at this moment as... everything began to tremble.
They were called Dukes by those who required classifications and hierarchies to understand the scope of power they witnessed.

But truly, their accumulated authority exceeded any normal Duke by margins that rendered comparison meaningless. They were Existences at a stage of power that very few beings across the breadth of reality could claim to understand.

Some even speculated that they had reached heights of capability comparable to those achieved by beings who had walked the Earliest Folds when power flowed according to principles that current reality had forgotten.
Others whispered that they might be comparable in authority to young Early Creatures themselves!

But the signature manifestation that truly defined their transcendent nature was their capability for Existential Trembling...the ability to make all surrounding weavings of existence shake through their presence alone, their aura affecting the atmosphere and environment of the very fabric of Existence itself!
Standing before such beings, one would feel their very existence trembling!
As two terrifying existences looked at each other, the bodies of everyone and everything nearby vibrated in response!
Existential! Trembling!
Only a single being had felt his hands begin to shake before his eyes turned utterly livid and filled with tyranny as he told his own body...Don’t you fucking dare!
And right after, his glorious standing and distinction as an Early Creature flared as for him and him alone in this region... he did not tremble.
He would not tremble!

sentences.text: Many Dukes throughout the assembled forces looked toward the cluster of Paradoxes with gazes that carried undisguised animosity.

For many of them, the relationship with Living Paradoxes had been defined by warfare that stretched across eons...conflicts in which Diviticus and other Dukes present had killed uncountable numbers of their allies.
The idea of accepting such beings as partners rather than enemies required adjustments to thinking that had been refined through countless cycles of violence and retribution.
In this moment of heavy contemplation, Moiraine began to float back toward Noah’s position.
Yet Noah’s mental voice reached her consciousness with firm instructions that halted her advance before it could draw unwanted attention.
’Do not,’ he conveyed, ’Remain where you are and continue appearing as the source of enhancement that benefits all present.’
His expression grew heavy as he observed this unfolding situation with the seriousness it demanded.
Right now, he seemed to be nothing more than an Extra with very little apparent power while Diviticus commanded center stage.
But this was okay!
Noah released a sigh that carried the weight of choices, acknowledging that he had chosen this path when he made the Festival of War resonate from Moiraine’s position rather than his own.
Not being in the spotlight every now and then was okay.

At this moment of personal reflection, Noah found himself sympathetically understanding how all those discarded extras in his own fable must have felt when their contributions were overlooked in favor of more prominent characters.
The sensation of being reduced to irrelevance despite possessing capabilities that exceeded those who commanded attention was humbling!
It was in this moment of heavy contemplation that existence itself convulsed!
A blaring purple brilliance blazed from above as reality tore itself open to accommodate the passage of someone whose presence was heavy.
From the temporal rift emerged the visage of an extremely gorgeous woman.

Her stellar purple hair flowed like liquid starlight given form and direction, while her dress seemed to contain within its fabric the compressed essence of temporal authority refined to its purest expression.

She smoked a pipe whose contents blazed with inner radiance, yet her attention focused immediately upon the figure of Duke Schrodinger with the kind of recognition that suggested their relationship stretched across eons of history.
"I thought I smelled a dirty beggar in my Transcendent Temporal Folds," she said.
"How many millions of years has it been now, Schrodinger?
Since when did you let children begin speaking for you?"

As she delivered this casual insult, she barely glanced toward Diviticus, yet that momentary attention carried within it the weight of assessment and dismissal that made the assembled Paradox Duke’s expression grow cold.
This...was Aion, the Temporal Watcher...a being whose authority over time itself had been legendary since epochs that predated current existence!
Toward her provocative words, the beggar-looking Schrodinger smiled with patient amusement that suggested he had been expecting exactly this development.
"Sometimes," he replied, "one has to sit back and let the younger generation lead.
Age brings wisdom about when to act and when to observe."
Aion smoked her pipe with movements that seemed to slow time around her position, each inhalation drawing in possibilities while each exhalation released certainties into the surrounding space.
She nodded as if considering his response, then...
WAP!
She vanished from her position above the battlefield, reality bending around her passage until she materialized directly beside Moiraine!
"You have gotten rusty, old friend," she said to Schrodinger with voice that carried across impossible distances without losing any of its clarity.
"I can see your gaze and the hungry attention of this loud Diviticus looking toward this Moiraine here with calculations..."
She gestured toward the Living Paradox whose position had become the center during this battle!
"She appears to have come before you other Paradoxes to lend aid against Dead Existences.
If anyone should have a seat at the table of governance, should it not be her?
Young, perhaps a bit weaker than established powers, certainly easier to manipulate into serving larger agendas..."
Schrodinger’s smile deepened at her provocative analysis.
"You are letting your true thoughts be heard out loud again, Aion," he observed with gentle reproach.
Aion nodded with calm acknowledgment of his criticism.
"Of course.
I believe in being straightforward about intentions and motivations rather than hiding behind pretense and manufactured courtesy.
And what I want most in this situation is the precise opposite of whatever you are seeking to achieve, you manipulative fucking beggar."
BOOM!
The exchange between these terrifying beings carried undertones that spoke to conflicts and competitions that stretched across eons of shared history!
Their true auras flared outward at this moment as... everything began to tremble.
They were called Dukes by those who required classifications and hierarchies to understand the scope of power they witnessed.
But truly, their accumulated authority exceeded any normal Duke by margins that rendered comparison meaningless.
They were Existences at a stage of power that very few beings across the breadth of reality could claim to understand.

Some even speculated that they had reached heights of capability comparable to those achieved by beings who had walked the Earliest Folds when power flowed according to principles that current reality had forgotten.
Others whispered that they might be comparable in authority to young Early Creatures themselves!

But the signature manifestation that truly defined their transcendent nature was their capability for Existential Trembling...the ability to make all surrounding weavings of existence shake through their presence alone, their aura affecting the atmosphere and environment of the very fabric of Existence itself!
Standing before such beings, one would feel their very existence trembling!
As two terrifying existences looked at each other, the bodies of everyone and everything nearby vibrated in response!
Existential!
Trembling!
Only a single being had felt his hands begin to shake before his eyes turned utterly livid and filled with tyranny as he told his own body...Don’t you fucking dare!
And right after, his glorious standing and distinction as an Early Creature flared as for him and him alone in this region... he did not tremble.
He would not tremble!

chapters.title: Chapter 3997: An Instant! I
paragraphs: The air itself seemed to hold its breath as existence trembled at the mere confrontation of two ancient powers!

The fabric of reality rippled outward from where Aion and Schrodinger locked gazes, their accumulated authority creating waves of pressure that made the very foundations of the Transcendent Temporal Folds uncertain about their own nature.
Lesser beings found themselves frozen in place, their bodies betraying them as Existential Trembling coursed through every fiber of their being!
Noah observed this display of overwhelming might with eyes that remained steady behind his obsidian helm.
The trembling that seized others, that fundamental recognition of powers beyond comprehension, simply... did not touch him.
His form stood perfectly still within Yoshinami’s armor, not through effort or resistance, but through the simple truth of what he was.
He was an Early Creature.
The thought burned through his consciousness with tyrannical certainty. How dare entities lesser than himself attempt to make him experience fear through mere displays of accumulated authority?!

They commanded respect, certainly. Their power could reshape existence itself, undoubtedly. But trembling? That was the province of those who stood beneath, not one whose very nature predated the concepts they wielded.
His gaze swept across the battlefield with cold assessment, taking in the positions of every player in this grand game.

Some of his goals had been achieved...the Festival of War had shifted the battle’s momentum, resources had been gathered, connections forged. Others remained tantalizingly out of reach. But the arrival of these heavy hitters, these beings whose authority transcended normal categorization, had transformed an already complex situation into something far more interesting.
Aion stood wreathed in temporal authority that seemed to slow time itself around her presence, each draw from her pipe pulling in possibilities while exhaling certainties!

She represented power that exceeded normal Dukes by margins that made comparison meaningless. And Schrodinger...that deceptively mundane figure whose presence generated warning signals in Noah’s mind...remained apathetically calm.
Noah’s lips curved slightly behind his concealing helm. He was not at the center of attention. And that was okay as since now, he had deemed it that way!
When circumstances served his purposes, he would do whatever proved necessary to obtain what he desired.
Consequences could be calculated, reactions predicted, outcomes orchestrated through understanding rather than force.
And right now, he wanted a certain terrifying treasure to be triggered.
In that moment of absolute stillness, where existence itself seemed frozen between heartbeats as two transcendent beings measured each other across impossible distances, Noah began to move.
His form lifted from its position with fluid grace, the obsidian armor flowing around him like liquid darkness as he started floating across the twisted space of the battlefield.
Amidst an Existential Trembling where others were frozen, he moved!

His destination was unmistakable...the massive form of the Primordial Death that Diviticus had bound in her tendrils of paradoxical authority, its skeletal frame held in perfect stasis despite the tremendous power contained within.
The shock of his actions rippled through every consciousness present like stones thrown into still water.
Eyes that had been locked on the confrontation between Aion and Schrodinger suddenly swiveled toward this impossible sight.

Here, in the midst of Existential Trembling that should have rendered all movement theoretical rather than actual, a single figure glided through space as if the overwhelming pressure simply... didn’t exist!

The obsidian armor caught and reflected the chaotic energies of the battlefield, creating patterns of darkness that seemed to absorb light rather than merely block it. Yet it was not the armor that commanded attention...it was the complete absence of struggle in his movements.
His body showed no indication of effort, no tremor of resistance against forces that made reality itself uncertain.
He moved as naturally as one might walk through an empty room, unaffected by pressures that had frozen beings of tremendous power in place.
Schrodinger’s ancient eyes shifted toward Noah’s advancing form, the calm assessment in his gaze suddenly flashing with brilliant illumination!

The beggar-like Duke’s expression remained unchanged, yet there was something in that brief flash of light that suggested pieces falling into place on a board whose scope only he could fully perceive.
Aion drew deeply from her pipe, the smoke swirling around her in patterns that seemed to write equations in the air before dissolving into nothingness.
Her eyes, those windows to temporal authority refined beyond normal comprehension, flickered with genuine interest as they tracked Noah’s movement.
The Temporal Watcher’s attention carried weight that made causality bend around its focus.
The distance between Noah’s starting position and the bound Primordial Death seemed to stretch and compress simultaneously, space itself uncertain about how to accommodate his passage!
Yet he continued forward with unwavering purpose, each moment bringing him closer to the massive creature whose very existence challenged the supremacy of life over death.

When he finally arrived within immediate proximity of the bound horror, close enough that the deathly authority radiating from its form should have begun the process of systematic dissolution, Noah turned his concealed gaze toward Diviticus calmly!

"I had laid claim to this little skeleton before you arrived and so rudely interrupted." His voice carried across the battlefield with crystalline clarity, each word cutting through the oppressive atmosphere as if the existential trembling was merely background noise. "So... release it."
HUUM!
The words hung in the space between them.

They were not phrased as a request or suggestion. They emerged as command, delivered with the casual authority of one who expected immediate compliance regardless of the vast differential in apparent power!
Noah’s mind raced through calculations as the words left his lips. He had chosen them with deliberate precision, understanding exactly how Diviticus would process such audacious demand.

She was currently intoxicated with her newfound might, drunk on capabilities that had elevated her beyond every previous limitation. Her entire approach to this situation had been crafted to establish Living Paradoxes as essential partners, to entrench their position within the broader weavings of existence.
He knew with absolute certainty that even if he deliberately sought to enrage her, she would not make direct moves against him here, not with all these Living Existences here.

As an unknown existence who displayed no obvious waves of dangerous power, yet who could walk unaffected through the Existential Trembling of beings whose might transcended normal Dukes, he represented a puzzle. And when faced with such an enigma, when confronted by someone bold enough to issue commands despite showing no apparent capability to enforce them, there was only one action she would take...
BOOM!
The obsidian tendrils that had held the Primordial Death in perfect stasis suddenly loosened, their grip releasing with the sound of existential law being deliberately violated!
The massive skeletal creature, freed from its bonds, roared with renewed fervor that made the temporal rivers themselves flow backward in recognition of wrongness given voice!

chapters.title: Chapter 3998: An Instant! II
paragraphs: Noah’s smile deepened behind his helm!

He didn’t even turn to look at the Primordial Death as it stretched its massive limbs, testing its recovered freedom with movements that created tears in the surrounding space. His gaze remained locked on Diviticus, recognition burning between them of exactly what had just occurred.

Yes, the only action she would have taken...the only response that satisfied both her curiosity and her position...was precisely what she had done. She had tested him by releasing a creature that even Dukes struggled to contain.

If he proved to be somebody of significance, he might defend himself and reveal his true nature. If he was nobody, he would simply die, and when questioned about such a result, she could merely shrug and point out that he had specifically requested the creature’s release.
The scene that followed was one of tyrannical confidence and glorious indifference!

Noah stood perfectly still as the Primordial Death, driven by its fundamental nature to eliminate everything that dared exist in its presence, immediately focused its attention on the being closest to its position. A massive skeletal hand, each finger larger than ancient towers, descended toward him with the inexorable certainty of entropy given malicious intent.
And intent...oh, gloriously, intent and action was all he needed!

The descending appendage crushed through space itself, its approach creating zones where the very concept of existence became negotiable. Yet Noah made no moves to defend or attack. His form remained motionless, as if the approaching annihilation was of no more concern than a gentle breeze.
When the massive hand was mere inches from his armored form, close enough that the deathly authority should have begun unmaking him at the most fundamental level...
HUUM!
A flash of crimson obsidian light erupted from Noah’s position with such intensity that every consciousness present felt it like a physical impact!
From within that terrible radiance came a sensation that transcended fear...it was the primal recognition of predator so far beyond their comprehension that resistance became meaningless concept.
For an instant so brief that most Living Existences failed to register it consciously, a massive illusion of a spider flashed across the entirety of the Transcendent Temporal Folds!

The spider’s form defied scale, its presence seeming to exist in dimensions that normal perception could not fully process. Eight eyes blazed with crimson malevolence, each one containing depths of ancient intelligence that regarded the Primordial Death with absolute apathy.
Those terrible eyes flashed with brilliant authority, and in that moment of acknowledgment, fate was sealed.
Diviticus and many of the assembled Dukes showed immediate alarm, their enhanced perceptions recognizing threat that they couldn’t truly counter!
They moved backward with instinctive urgency, their bodies responding to danger before conscious thought could process what they had witnessed.
Only Schrodinger and Aion remained unmoved, though their expressions grew slightly more serious as they recognized...something.
Something!

The moment after the crimson light completed its manifestation, everything seemingly returned to normal. The overwhelming presence vanished as suddenly as it had appeared, leaving only the lingering sensation that something monumental had occurred beyond their ability to fully comprehend.
But the massive body of the Primordial Death... had disappeared entirely.
No trace remained...no scattered bones, no wisps of deathly authority, no evidence that such a creature had ever existed in this space!
Where it had been, only empty air remained.
The veiled armored figure of Noah stood exactly as he had before, his posture unchanged, as if he hadn’t moved a fraction since the creature’s attack began.
Yet subtle crimson obsidian brilliance now radiated from his form, speaking to power recently exercised but carefully contained.
His gaze remained fixed on Diviticus, coldness and tyranny burning in the depths of his concealed eyes!
"Be careful," he said, his voice carrying the weight of prophecy delivered with absolute certainty. "Who knows... one day that might just be you."
The threat was delivered with such casual precision that it struck like existential law being established!
The implication was clear...whatever had just eliminated a Primordial Death with such absolute authority could just as easily be turned upon her!
Without waiting for response or reaction, Noah began floating back toward his previous position.
As he moved through space that still trembled from the confrontation of ancient powers, his voice rang out with commanding clarity.
"Come."
The single word was directed at Moiraine, who had been observing everything with her characteristic serene intensity!
He had told her to wait before when strategic positioning demanded it. Now he commanded her presence as circumstances had shifted to accommodate their departure.

Moiraine floated away from Aion’s position with grace, her movement creating ripples in the temporal authority that surrounded the ancient being. She came to stand beside Noah with the natural precision of one whose loyalty transcended every other consideration.

Noah’s gaze swept across the assembled powers one final time. He looked toward Diviticus calmly. His attention shifted to Aion with acknowledgment. Finally, his eyes settled on Schrodinger with the particular weight of one mystery recognizing another.
"Till next time," he said.

His attention turned to Duke Gwendolyn, and when he spoke again, his voice carried deliberate weight. "Thanks for the invite to this event. If there are to be any seats at any tables, you know how to reach me."
The implications hung in the air like existential contracts waiting to be signed.
He...was establishing himself as a player in games that shaped existence itself, one whose participation came with costs and benefits!

He didn’t remain to observe the reactions to his declarations. Sharp light erupted around both him and Moiraine, reality bending to accommodate their departure through methods that bypassed many Living Existences.
The two figures simply ceased to exist in that location, leaving behind only the weight of tyranny and glory.
As the light of transportation wrapped around him, Noah’s consciousness blazed with the fervor of prompts materializing within his mind!

|Yoshinami has successfully executed the Crown of Inevitable Retribution against a target whose power was deemed to be equivalent to or exceeded the distinction of an average Duke. True Death has been delivered to the Primordial Death, Kar’theta the Hungerer, through methods that bypass every form of resistance, protection, or existential anchoring.|

|The eliminated entity possessed authority equivalent to 1.7 times that of standard Duke-level capabilities, with additional enhancements from the Curse of the Infinite Paradox of Unmaking. Complete annihilation achieved across all dimensions, timelines, and possibilities. No resurrection, restoration, or reconstitution possible through any known or unknown methods.|

|Yoshinami has directly transported the True Death-eliminated corpse of Primordial Death Kar’theta to the Early Veiled Shore for comprehensive analysis. The corpse retains 94% of its original existential mass despite True Death elimination, a unique preservation effect of Yoshinami’s particular methodology.|
|Estimated processing timeline: Initial breakdown - 1 hour. Complete resource extraction - 24 hours.|

|Additional Note: Yoshinami expresses satisfaction with the quality of the eliminated target and requests permission to retain 50% of the processed materials for her own recovery and grown. Such enhancement would potentially allow for two uses of Crown of Inevitable Retribution per 24-hour period rather than the current single application.]
The cascade of information painted a picture of triumph that exceeded his most optimistic projections!

chapters.title: Chapter 3999: Be The Scariest Monster! I
paragraphs: The sharp light of transportation dissolved around them like morning mist, revealing the familiar golden expanse of the Early Veiled Shore.

Noah’s feet touched the warm sands with the satisfaction of one returning home after a journey through existential chaos, but what greeted his eyes made even his enhanced perception pause in appreciation.
The massive corpse of the Primordial Death lay compressed upon the golden shore like a monument to impossible victory!
Its skeletal form, which had towered over armies of Living Existences mere moments ago, now rested in defeated stillness.

The bones themselves seemed to pulse with residual deathly authority, creating distortions in the air above them where existence itself remained uncertain about accommodating such concentrated ending.
But it was not alone in its repose. Scattered across the pristine sands lay thousands of bone fragments, pieces of otherworldly flesh, and crystallized segments of what had once been Dead Existences.
They gleamed under the Shore’s light like macabre treasures, each piece radiating the particular wrongness that marked beings who had existed in states of perpetual termination.
These were the fruits of his Festival of War, the one percent that had been automatically claimed from every elimination enhanced by his orchestrated blessing!

Moiraine stood beside him, her eyes sweeping across the grotesque bounty with an expression that shifted from amazement to concern. The golden light caught the worry lines forming around her eyes as she turned to face him.

"Sir," she began, the honorific carrying its usual warmth despite the seriousness in her tone, "was it... truly okay to reveal yourself in such a manner? Entities like Schrodinger..." She paused, seeming to search for words adequate to convey the magnitude of what concerned her. "They are extremely terrifying. Beyond what most can comprehend."
HUUM!
Noah’s lips curved into a smile as he began walking toward the massive corpse, his bare feet leaving glowing impressions in the sand.
Each step felt like a declaration of intent, a refusal to be cowed by the scope of powers that existed beyond his current reach.

"I stopped living in fear many, many months ago," he said. "Fear is a luxury I can no longer afford, not when every moment of hesitation could mean countless possible futures lost." He paused beside a particularly large fragment of Dead Existence bone, nudging it thoughtfully with his foot. "But I am curious about this Schrodinger. What makes him so particularly terrifying among beings who can already reshape existence with their thoughts?"
Moiraine’s expression grew serious, her gaze drifting toward the vibrant waters that lapped at the Shore’s edge.
In the distance, she could see Ruination seated in deep meditation, her form wreathed in crimson-gold radiance as she processed the gifts Noah had bestowed.
The Infiniverse floated nearby, multicolored jewels across her skin pulsing in harmonious patterns.
The Sacred Totems rose like monuments to achievement, their crystalline surfaces catching and reflecting light in ways that created new colors with each observation.
She took in all of this...this sanctuary of power and potential, before beginning to speak, her voice taking on the cadence of someone sharing secrets that few were privileged to know.

"Schrodinger," she began, "is not merely powerful in the way other Dukes are powerful. His connection to Living Paradoxes runs so deep that some theorize he predates the current understanding of what Paradox even means. There are whispers...never confirmed, always denied when asked directly, that he used to live as an attendant of an Early Creature inside an Early Veiled Shore." She paused, letting the weight of that possibility settle. "Not visit, not observe, but actually lived within the Shore of an Early Creature."
The wind picked up slightly, carrying with it the scent of the sacred herbs growing in their plots, and Moiraine continued, her voice growing more animated as she warmed to her subject.

"His habits make no sense to anyone who tries to understand him through normal logic. He frequently takes on the visage of a beggar...not as disguise or infiltration, but seemingly because he genuinely enjoys it. He’ll go to mortal worlds, worlds so insignificant they don’t even register on most maps of existence, and simply... live there. Sometimes for years, sometimes for centuries, just existing as a homeless wanderer beside muddy roads."

She shook her head, hair catching the light as it moved. "Most think he’s insane, or playing games beyond their comprehension. He rarely makes moves...eons can pass without him taking any action that others can perceive. But when he does act..." Her voice dropped to barely above a whisper. "Every time Schrodinger has made a deliberate move, it has resulted in profound changes across existence itself. Entire Folds have been restructured. The balance of power between Living Existences has shifted. Things that were thought impossible suddenly become inevitable."
Noah absorbed this information with the careful attention it deserved, nodding slowly as pieces of a vast puzzle began arranging themselves in his mind.

"In existence," he said after a moment of contemplation, "there can indeed be some scary monsters. Beings whose power and understanding transcend every category we use to measure capability." His eyes blazed with inner fire as he continued. "All that I have to do... is become scarier than them. And slowly, gradually, I’m gathering the resources to accomplish exactly that."
Yes!
There were many monsters out there. He simply...had to be the bigger monster!
He turned toward the massive corpse of the Primordial Death, reaching out to tap its crystallized bone with casual familiarity.
"Yoshinami," he called out, his voice carrying the authority of one addressing a bound companion, "you can have your half."
The response was immediate and dramatic. The air beside him shimmered with crimson-black radiance before Yoshinami materialized in her human form.
Her pale features were transformed by an expression of genuine joy, her crimson eyes blazing with happiness that made her usual cold demeanor seem like a distant memory.
With grace that spoke to eons of practiced ceremony, she dropped to one knee and took his hand, pressing her lips to it in a gesture of gratitude.
"Master’s generosity exceeds all expectation," she murmured against his skin, her voice carrying vibrations that seemed to resonate with the spider-essence of her true nature.

Then, without warning, her form exploded outward. The transformation was both beautiful and terrifying to witness. Her human shape dissolved into expanding darkness that reformed as the massive spider, her true form standing taller than the Sacred Totems themselves.
Eight legs, each one thick as ancient trees, positioned themselves around the Primordial Death’s corpse with surgical precision.

One of her forelegs, sharp enough to cut through dimensions themselves, descended with deliberate care. The limb sliced through the massive corpse with a sound like reality tearing, dividing it perfectly in half!
No resistance met her blade-like appendage...even in death, the Primordial seemed to recognize a predator of superior nature.
Webs began flowing from her spinnerets, wrapping her portion of the corpse in silk that gleamed with otherworldly properties.

Each strand contained within it preservation techniques that would maintain the corpse’s potency while she processed its essence. With movements that made the ground tremble, she lifted her wrapped prize and began moving toward the distant trees where she could consume it in privacy.
A prompt materialized in Noah’s consciousness as she departed!

|Yoshinami has begun devouring half of the Primordial Death’s corpse. The profound nutrients contained within this Duke-level Dead Existence will elevate her capabilities significantly. Upon completion of consumption and digestion, the Crown of Inevitable Retribution will be available for use twice within any 24-hour period rather than the current single application.]
Noah watched her massive form disappear among the trees, each step making the Shore tremble slightly, before releasing a long breath.
The casual brutality of her efficiency, the eager joy in her service...it was simultaneously comforting and unsettling to witness.
"Quantify all remaining corpses to equivalent nutrients," he commanded the Shore itself, his voice carrying the weight of authority that expected immediate compliance.
The response came as cascading prompts that made his eyes widen with each successive revelation.

|Analysis complete. All scattered pieces of Dead Existences obtained through the Festival of War boon have been evaluated. Total nutritional value equivalent to: 1,250 corpses of Eminent Early Living Marine Lifeforms. This represents concentrated essence of ending that, when properly processed, can be converted to nutrients through the Shore’s unique digestive capabilities.|

|Additional analysis: Half of the Primordial Death’s corpse (portion retained for Shore processing) has been re-evaluated. Nutritional value equivalent to: 1 complete Kleos Early Living Marine Lifeform. This represents the highest grade of nutrients ever introduced to your Early Veiled Shore.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4000: Be The Scariest Monster! II
paragraphs: Noah’s eyes burned with brilliant intensity as understanding crystallized into ambition. The numbers were staggering, representing advancement potential that would have taken others eons to accumulate through conventional methods. His voice carried tyrannical certainty as he spoke his realization aloud.
"It seems...I need to focus on hunting Duke-level entities."
The statement buzzed in the air like a declaration of war against the established order of existence itself!

He knew that currently, his power remained far below that of an Honored Living Existence, let alone a Duke. But if he could continue eliminating such beings through strategic positioning and clever use of his unique resources, if he could keep converting their deaths into nutrients for his advancement... he would catch up soon enough.

The golden sands beneath the corpses began to shift and churn, drawing the massive remains and scattered pieces into their depths with the patient hunger of something that knew how to wait for its meals.
The Shore itself was consuming them, breaking them down into components that could fuel advancement.
Another prompt materialized, this one requiring his direct input.

|Due to the overabundance of nutrients currently being processed, allocation distribution is required. The Early Veiled Shore requests guidance on nutrient distribution across multiple possible development priorities. Proposed allocation:
- 15% toward Plot Enhancement: Accelerate maturation of currently planted Sacred Herbs (Transcendent Veilmoss, Chronos Petrichor, Void-Heart Chrysanthemums, Echo Sage, Infinity’s Breath Orchids.. )
- 15% toward Tree Awakening: Enable the nine Early Sacred Trees to begin producing their first fruits
- 20% toward Shore Expansion: Further increase the territory of the Early Veiled Shore by an additional 200%

- 15% toward Leviathan’s Eternum Cage construction: Build an ancient early aquarium designed to automatically draw in and capture Early Living Marine Lifeforms. Once caught, no entity below Early Creature status can escape

- 35% toward Personal Enhancement: Accelerate forging of Towers of Osmont, advance completion of the second part of your Heart (Oruvian Shardveil - The Arterial Convergence Core), and finalize the Early Atlas of the Folds
Confirm allocation?]
Noah gazed at the breakdown with calm and tyrannical excitement, his mind already calculating how each investment would compound into future advantages.
The Leviathan’s Eternum Cage particularly caught his attention...an automatic harvesting system for Marine Lifeforms would provide consistent nutrients without requiring his direct involvement.
"Proceed," he commanded.
HUUM!
The eruption of brilliance that followed made reality itself take notice. The entire Early Veiled Shore pulsed with white-gold radiance that seemed to emerge from every grain of sand simultaneously.
Waves of concentrated authority rippled outward from the points where nutrients were being processed, each pulse carrying with it fundamental changes to the Shore’s nature.
Heidrun, who had been maintaining her vigil over the sacred herb plots with characteristic arrogance, suddenly rose to her feet with unprecedented excitement.

Her crystalline eyes widened as she witnessed golden light of impossible density bathing the plots she had been guarding. The herbs, which had been growing at their natural pace, suddenly began flourishing with explosive vitality. Leaves unfurled, stems thickened, and the very air around them began to shimmer with the potency of their accelerated maturation.
Noah began walking across the golden sands toward the shoreline, each step feeling like a ceremony of advancement.

Moiraine followed behind him, and he could hear her release a soft sigh as the worry finally left her expression. When he glanced back, she was smiling...not the careful, respectful smile she usually wore, but something genuine and warm.
She would simply trust that he knew what he was doing.
As he walked, prompts began cascading through his consciousness, each one marking another milestone in his impossible progression!
|Heart Component Progress - Oruvian Shardveil (The Arterial Convergence Core): 67% complete. Crystalline arterial networks forming. Blood production capacity increasing exponentially.|
|Current Blood of Early Creature reserves: 10,847 drops. Production rate has increased to 500 drops per hour due to enhanced Heart development.|
|Tower Advancement Notifications:
- Tower of Kuklos has achieved Second Stage: Temporal Architectonics
- Tower of Veritarch has achieved Second Stage: Truth’s Observatory
- Tower of Relativity has achieved Second Stage: Dimensional Anchor
- Tower of Ordo Ab Chao has achieved Second Stage: Pattern Manifestation
- Tower of Megalos has achieved Second Stage: Magnitude Amplification
- Tower of Conceptual has achieved Second Stage: Abstract Fortress
- Tower of Ingeniare has achieved Second Stage: Creative Matrix
- Tower of Outerversal has achieved Second Stage: Boundary Transcendence
- Tower of Eldritch Expanse has achieved Second Stage: Impossible Geometries
- Tower of Prana has achieved Second Stage: Life Force Citadel...
-Tower of Plot...]
Noah almost laughed as he saw the Early Veiled Shore going all out to even give unique names to the Towers of Osmont experiencing their advancement to the Second Stage.
When Noah closed his eyes, the sensation that washed over him defied description.
He could feel the golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore infusing him with tremendous glory, each grain seemingly connected to his existence through threads of pure authority.

Every step he took sent waves of gold surging through his being...into every cell, every atom, every synapse. It was as if the Shore itself had become an extension of his body, or perhaps his body had become an extension of the Shore!
The feeling was utterly indescribable, a symphony of advancement playing through his very existence. Power became him, each pulse of nutrients reshaping fundamental aspects of his nature.

His muscles densed with strength that transcended the physical, his bones crystallized with durability that mocked conventional limits, his mind expanded to accommodate understanding that would have shattered lesser consciousness.

When he opened his eyes again, he stood near the waters of the Shore. The crystalline waves lapped at the sand with gentle insistence, each surge carrying whispers of the Marine Lifeforms that dwelt in their depths.
To his right, he could see the construction beginning...massive pillars of crystallized authority rising from the sands as the Leviathan’s Eternum Cage began taking shape.

The structure was magnificent even in its earliest stages. Archways of compressed space curved impossibly, creating passages that existed in more dimensions than the eye could properly follow. The foundation gleamed with runes and Glyphs that seemed to write themselves into existence, each symbol a law that would govern the Cage’s operation.
It would be beautiful and terrible...a trap that offered no escape, a prison that Marine Lifeforms would swim into willingly, drawn by currents they couldn’t resist.
Alongside all of this...
[Current Complexity Quotient: 897,442,318]
[Current Purity Quotient: 901,765,429]
The numbers blazed across his consciousness with the weight of achievement.
It was...maddening if others ever knew how quickly he was doing all this!
He was approaching one billion in both measurements...the threshold where he could form his first Kleos Glyph, that ultimate expression of power that transcended normal limitations.
Noah stood watching the Leviathan’s Eternum Cage take shape, its emerging form promising automated harvest of resources that would fuel endless advancement.
He was savoring these moments, enjoying the boons that came after heavy war, knowing full well that the landscape of existence was about to change dramatically.
The ramifications of what had occurred in the Temporal Folds would ripple outward.

The emergence of Dead Existences, the intervention of Living Paradoxes, his own display of power and Moiraine....all of it would reshape how the great powers viewed each other and their positions in the hierarchy of existence.
And he would be a participant in whatever came next. His eyes gazed into the distance as his mind reached out to his other body, still maintaining his merchant persona in Aeternitas Concordia.
He expected Duke Gwendolyn to approach that body very soon, drawn by questions and possibilities that his display had created.
Through that interaction, he might be able to observe the reshaping of Living Existence hierarchy in real time, positioning himself to take advantage of whatever opportunities emerged.
The Shore pulsed around him with renewed vitality, each breath he took filled with the scent of advancement and possibility!

The sacred herbs reached toward maturity, the trees prepared to bear fruit, and in the depths of the expanding waters, new Marine Lifeforms began to spawn, drawn by the irresistible authority of an Early Creature’s domain.
He had transformed a battlefield into a harvest, converted death into life, turned endings into new beginnings. And this...was only the glorious and magisterial beginning of what he would accomplish!

chapters.title: Chapter 4001: The 10 Living Existences! I
paragraphs: Life could change so rapidly that one found themselves in places they never imagined they would be just days or months ago.

The whims of existence possessed a particularly cruel sense of humor...one could be a grand teacher of existential philosophy one day, revered across multiple Wheels and Dwellings for their wisdom, and find themselves shaking their body for cash at a seedy establishment the next, simply because existence had decided to restructure itself overnight!
The mighty could fall, the fallen could rise, and sometimes, if existence was feeling particularly creative, both could happen simultaneously to the same being.
Existence could truly change too fast!
In a certain Law Fold, removed from the chaos of the Nullvein Gravewake Folds, such rapid change had become the defining characteristic of one particular being’s recent experiences.

Bob... who had managed to lock away Thauron, the Null Monarch, inside an Inevitability...walked through corridors of crystallized authority with movements that suggested he was still adjusting to his transformed state!

His form had evolved into an obsidian-white humanoid figure with skin that seemed to shift between solid and liquid states, crowned by a perfectly round, bald head that gleamed under the ambient light of Law itself.
He was now...a glorious Living Origin!

He followed in the wake of two beings whose presence made the very air taste of structured power. Altheon moved ahead with the distracted air of someone whose mind wrestled with problems far removed from their current location, his luminous form occasionally flickering as if his consciousness kept trying to be elsewhere.
Beside him bounced...there was no other word for her manner of movement- a Prime Living Law whose very existence seemed to radiate barely contained enthusiasm.
Her pink hair defied gravity, while her matching pink eyes sparkled with the kind of vivacious energy that made others simultaneously exhausted and energized just from proximity!
She wore robes that should have been formal, authoritative, befitting her status as a Prime Living Law, but somehow she made them look like party attire through sheer force of personality.

Living Law Authority wrapped around them in spiraling patterns, the silver-white energy creating tunnels through space that compressed distance into meaningless concepts. When the authority finally scattered, releasing them at their destination, the Prime Living Law threw her arms wide with theatrical flair.
"Welcome," she announced with a smile that could have powered small civilizations, "to the Juridical Sanctum of Law Litigation!"
HUUM!
The name boomed in the air with all the warmth of a death sentence delivered with a smile.
Bob’s enhanced perception took in their surroundings, and what he saw was glorious!

Seas of white banners and scales stretched in every direction, each one carved from what appeared to be crystallized justice itself. Between these scales, shrines dotted the landscape like monuments to crimes committed and sentences served.

"Isn’t it magnificent?" the Prime Living Law continued, practically vibrating with enthusiasm. "Here we house all types of Living Existences who broke Living Laws in some manner or another. Some are locked away for a mere dozen years...barely a slap on the wrist, really. Others..." Her smile grew sharper, "Others have been here for millions of years, and they’ll be here for millions more."

She began walking, or rather bouncing, forward, gesturing at various features with the pride of a homeowner showing off renovations. "We have sections organized by type of violation, severity of offense, and my personal favorite...likelihood of repeat offense. You’ll find many, many Living Paradoxes here, actually. They have such trouble following rules, the poor dears."
Her eyes twinkled with something that might have been sympathy if it hadn’t been accompanied by such obvious glee.
She spun to face Bob, her pink hair creating a halo effect that somehow made her look both angelic and slightly unhinged.
"The Royal Law Tristesse can have you stay here for, oh, what was your name again?" She tapped her chin thoughtfully. "Bobby?"
Bob’s entire form went rigid, his obsidian-white skin rippling with barely contained emotions.
Bobby. He fucking hated that name!
His voice, when it emerged, carried the weight of someone who had fought for far too long.
"Bob," he said with deliberate precision. "My name is Bob."

The Prime Living Law’s smile never wavered, though something in her eyes suggested she was filing away his reaction for future reference. "Of course! Bob it is. Well, Bob, the Royal Law Tristesse has reached a consensus with other interested parties. Nothing born from those special Nullvein Gravewake Folds is to be released into general circulation just yet...too many variables, too many unknowns. So instead, you get to temporarily learn how to be an Origin here!"
She gestured toward Altheon with a flourish. "With your assigned babysitter, the ever-boring Altheon, to guide you through the process!"

Her attention shifted to the Prime Living Origin, and her expression grew slightly more serious, though the effect was somewhat undermined by the way she was still bouncing on her toes. "Though you seem rather preoccupied, old friend. Some thoughts? Existential crisis?"
WAA!

Altheon seemed to surface from whatever depths his consciousness had been exploring, his ancient eyes focusing on the present with visible effort. He shook his head with the patient exhaustion of someone who had too many things in his mind- after all, his other body was with the Young Miss and the now seemingly terrifting Noah Osmont in a Doorway!
"I don’t have time to be a babysitter," he said, his voice carrying notes of genuine regret mixed with impatience. His gaze settled on Bob with something that might have been sympathy.
"Just bear with it and stay here for a bit. After things cool down...you’ll be allowed to enter the Transcendent Origin Folds properly."
Before Bob could formulate a response, before he could ask any of the thousand questions burning in his consciousness, Altheon simply... ceased.
One moment he stood there, luminous and present, and the next, only the faint afterimage of his authority remained, already fading like smoke in wind.
The Prime Living Law harrumphed with the exaggerated disappointment of a performer who’d lost half their audience!
She shook her head, pink hair swaying with the motion, before turning back to Bob with renewed enthusiasm.

"Well then, Bobby...sorry, Bob, looks like it’s just you and me! Would you like the grand tour? I especially enjoy visiting the sections where we keep the little Paradoxes who’ve been locked away for eons. They get so wonderfully bitter after the first few millennia." Her eyes gleamed with an excitement that bordered on disturbing. "And if you’re interested, if you really want to test yourself, you can even battle against them! Kill them if you achieve victory...it’s perfectly fine here. They’re prisoners, after all, and rehabilitation through combat is an accepted form of correction."
Bob’s eyes blazed with sudden intensity at these words. The prospect of combat, of devouring beings of significant power, struck a chord deep within his transformed existence.
In the depths of his consciousness, an image burned bright and constant...his daughter, his light, the one pure thing he had managed to create in his existence of conflict and struggle.

He would do whatever it took to gain enough power to see her again. If that meant fighting imprisoned Paradoxes in this realm of crystallized justice, if it meant learning to be an Origin through methods that others might find distasteful, then so be it!
He had already crossed lines that most beings wouldn’t even approach. What were a few more in service of a goal that transcended his own existence?
Bob looked at the Prime Living Law, and when he spoke, his voice burned with glory!
"Let’s go see these vile Paradoxes."

In Aeternitas Concordia, at the junction where the ambitious stalls of Originus Venerant Fold Dwellers gave way to the towering establishments of Living Existences, another of Noah’s bodies maintained his merchant persona with practiced ease.

The Glass Woks floated before him like captured stars, their contents sending waves of intoxicating aroma across the golden plaza. Stacks of golden bowls waited beside his purple throne, ready to be filled with treasures that would make even Honored existences weep with envy.

He was in the midst of examining a peculiar object...something that resembled a crystallized moment of time that a Living Concept had retrieved from a particularly treacherous Doorway, when reality suddenly compressed around him.
HUUM!
Nine figures materialized from thin air.
They appeared on the golden path in formation, their combined presence creating waves of pressure that made nearby Fold Dwellers stumble backward in instinctive recognition of overwhelming power.

The figure at their forefront commanded immediate attention. Golden hair that seemed to capture and reflect every photon of light in the plaza, features carved with the kind of perfection that transcended natural beauty, and an aura that made even the other Honored Living Existences seem diminished by comparison!
This was a Royal Living Existence!
Yet when he looked at Noah, his expression carried the kind of difficulty that suggested he was dealing with variables beyond his comfort zone.
"Sir," the Royal Living Existence said dubiously, "the Lady invites you for a discussion of utmost importance."
WAA!
The plaza erupted in barely contained chaos.

Whispers flew faster than thought itself as hundreds of consciousnesses tried to process what they were witnessing. Nine Honored Living Existences and a Royal had come to formally invite a supposed Fold Dweller to meet with ’the Lady’....
Many did not know, but this was a title that could only refer to Duke Gwendolyn herself!
Noah raised his head slowly, his eyes sharp as they took in the careful positioning of his escorts.

Nine Honored beings for a simple invitation was not courtesy....it was preparation. Duke Gwendolyn and the other Living Existences no longer knew how to accurately categorize him after his display in the Temporal Folds.
To them, he was an enigma who had somehow eliminated a Duke-level Dead Existence through means they couldn’t comprehend.
They were probing, testing, trying to gauge whether he would come willingly or require... persuasion.
Part of him wanted to decline. The merchant business had been surprisingly profitable, and there were still treasures from the Doorways he wanted to acquire here...

But the matter of Living Paradoxes seeking their seat at the table, the reshaping of power structures that was undoubtedly occurring in the wake of recent events...these things demanded his attention.
Noah rose from his throne with deliberate grace, each movement calculated to project confidence without threat.
The throne, woks, and bowls vanished into his spatial storage with practiced ease. His voice carried across the plaza with clear authority as he addressed the gathered crowd.
"I will return to continue our business in a little while."
Then, turning to the Royal Living Existence with a slight nod that acknowledged rank without surrendering dignity, he spoke two words that set events in motion.
"Let’s go."

chapters.title: Chapter 4002: The 10 Living Existences! II
paragraphs: The light of the Royal Living Origin wrapped around them like liquid starlight, compressing space and distance into meaningless concepts as it carried Noah and his escort through layers of Aeternitas Concordia that most beings would never witness.
When the radiance finally released them, Noah found himself standing in a place filled with glory...a garden!

The garden stretched before him in terraced levels that seemed to exist in multiple dimensions simultaneously. Crystalline pathways wound between beds of vegetation that pulsed with inner light, each plant more impossible than the last.

Here, roses bloomed with petals made from compressed temporal energy, their thorns capable of cutting through causality itself. There, trees rose with bark of crystallized law, their branches heavy with fruit that defied comprehension.
The fruits were Wheels of Existence.

Each wheel hung from its branch like a ripe apple, yet contained within its spinning form entire realities. He could see civilizations rising and falling within each fruit, billions of lives playing out their destinies in accelerated time, only to begin again when the wheel completed its rotation!
The sight was simultaneously beautiful and horrifying...entire existences reduced to decorative produce in someone’s garden.
Above it all, a massive golden dome crowned the space, its surface inscribed with patterns of runes.

This was clearly the apex of some vast structure in Concordia’s heart, a place where only the most powerful could tread without invitation. The dome itself seemed alive, breathing with a rhythm that made the garden’s impossibilities feel natural by comparison.
Yet Noah’s fascination with the surroundings was quickly displaced by what his senses detected within this miraculous space.
The auras that pressed against his consciousness were unmistakable...Duke-level entities, multiple ones, their presence making the very air dense with accumulated authority.

The Royal Living Origin who had escorted him here suddenly bowed with profound respect, as did all the Honored Living Existences who had accompanied them. Without a word of explanation or farewell, they simply vanished, leaving Noah alone with beings whose power could reshape existence itself.
Four Dukes. He counted them with the careful precision of someone observing potential threats and allies.

Duke Gwendolyn stood nearest, her stellar dark hair catching light that seemed to originate from within rather than from any external source. Beside her stood a figure that made Noah do a subtle double-take...a man in pristine white robes who leaned slightly on an ornate cane, his eyes... impossibly, incomprehensibly blind.
Milky white orbs gazed at nothing and everything simultaneously. How could a Duke, a being whose perception should transcend every limitation, be blind?
Further into the garden, surrounded by flames that danced between red and gold like Origin authority given pyroclastic form, stood a woman whose presence commanded attention through sheer intensity.

Her desert garb seemed out of place in this garden of impossibilities, yet somehow perfect for her bearing...layers of flowing fabric that shifted between states of matter with each movement. Her skin gleamed with an inner radiance that suggested she didn’t merely wield Origin, but had become it!
And lastly...
Noah had to look twice to confirm what his senses were telling him.
Floating at eye level, no more than a few inches in total size, was...a mouse.

Its fur was lustrous white that seemed to contain constellations within each strand, and its eyes....those stellar white orbs held the weight of eons, the kind of gaze that suggested this being had witnessed the rise and fall of entire Folds!
When the mouse spoke, its voice emerged with bass tones that belonged to something mountain-sized rather than palm-sized. Meaning its voice was fucking heavy!

"Duke Gwendolyn has filled us in on the... things she deemed we should know." The mouse’s tiny hands clasped behind its back in a gesture that would have been comical if not for the overwhelming authority radiating from its diminutive form.
"What I want to ascertain first, before anything else, is this... do you wish the Living Origins any harm?"
The question buzzed in the garden. Noah felt the weight of four Duke-level consciousnesses focused entirely upon him, their combined attention making reality itself hold its breath.
Purple text materialized above each of their heads as his distinction as the Weaver of Existence identified them.
Duke Gwendolyn he knew as thr others were foreign!
|Duke Valen - The Blind Oracle|:: He who traded sight for true vision.
|Duke Pyralis - The Desert Phoenix|:: She who burns away impurity with Origin’s flame.
|Duke Whisker - The Primordial Sage|:: He who remembers existence.
Noah’s lips curved into a smile as he met each of their gazes in turn, his voice carrying the kind of calm that came from either supreme confidence or supreme ignorance.
"Does it only matter for the Living Origins?" He let the question hang for a moment before continuing. "What if I wished to harm other Living Existences?"

Duke Whisker’s tiny features arranged themselves into what might have been amusement. "Realistically and honestly, the main determinant is your intent toward Living Origins. The politics between different types of Living Existences are... complex. But Origins are special. We are, after all, beginnings incarnate."

Noah nodded slowly, as if considering his words carefully. "I have no intention to harm Living Origins, though..." He paused, letting them lean into his hesitation. "There was one Living Origin who crossed me. I’m still deciding whether I will kill them or not."
The tension in the garden shifted, becoming sharper, more focused. Duke Whisker’s whiskers twitched with what might have been curiosity.
"What type of Living Origin are they?"
"Prime."

The mouse’s expression relaxed visibly. "Ah, that would be nothing major then. Primes die all the time in the grand scheme of things." He turned to the other Dukes, his stellar eyes gleaming with certainty. "He’s telling the truth. He does not wish Living Origins any harm...at least, not as a general principle."
The atmosphere in the garden shifted palpably. Duke Gwendolyn’s shoulders relaxed minutely, while Duke Pyralis’s flames dimmed from aggressive brilliance to merely impressive radiance.

Duke Whisker floated forward slightly, his tiny form somehow managing to project gravitas. "Allow me to make proper introductions, since we’re apparently going to be having a civilized discussion rather than an existential confrontation. I am Duke Whisker, sometimes called the Primordial Sage, though I find titles tedious after the first few eons."

He gestured to each Duke in turn. "Duke Valen here traded his physical sight for the ability to see truth itself. Duke Pyralis burns with the pure essence of Origin from the Desert of First Thoughts. And Duke Gwendolyn you’ve already had the pleasure of meeting."
Gwendolyn stepped forward, her expression all business now that the immediate question of Noah’s threat level had been addressed. "Very well, let’s get down to business then... the Living Paradoxes."
The name fell into the garden’s atmosphere like a stone into still water, creating ripples of tension that each Duke felt.

"They stole the corpse of an Early Creature," Duke Pyralis said, her voice carrying the heat of barely contained anger. "The audacity of such an action transcends everything. That corpse was being studied, preserved, protected for good reason."

"And they likely did something desecrated with it," Duke Whisker added, his tiny form radiating disgust. "The appearance of Dead Existences is almost certainly linked to whatever unholy ritual they performed. The timing is too convenient, the methodology too specific."

He gestured to each Duke in turn.
"Duke Valen here traded his physical sight for the ability to see truth itself.
Duke Pyralis burns with the pure essence of Origin from the Desert of First Thoughts.
And Duke Gwendolyn you’ve already had the pleasure of meeting."
Gwendolyn stepped forward, her expression all business now that the immediate question of Noah’s threat level had been addressed.
"Very well, let’s get down to business then... the Living Paradoxes."
The name fell into the garden’s atmosphere like a stone into still water, creating ripples of tension that each Duke felt.
"They stole the corpse of an Early Creature," Duke Pyralis said, her voice carrying the heat of barely contained anger.
"The audacity of such an action transcends everything.
That corpse was being studied, preserved, protected for good reason."
"And they likely did something desecrated with it," Duke Whisker added, his tiny form radiating disgust.
"The appearance of Dead Existences is almost certainly linked to whatever unholy ritual they performed.
The timing is too convenient, the methodology too specific."

chapters.title: Chapter 4003: The 10 Living Existences! III
paragraphs: Duke Valen’s blind eyes seemed to focus on something none of them could see. "And now they wish to use the very crisis they created as pretense to assert themselves among the Living Existences again. It’s brilliant in its simplicity...create a problem only you can solve, then demand recognition for solving it."

"The threat of Dead Existences is very real," Gwendolyn continued, her voice heavy with the weight of recent memory. "If we deny the Paradoxes their seat at the table, they’ll likely open more tears in existence, make the situation increasingly dire until we’re forced to call upon them. Since Paradoxes..." she paused, seeming to taste something bitter, "are mainly the ones effective against Dead Existences."
Duke Whisker’s whiskers twitched in what might have been amusement. "But then... another party has appeared that seems to also be effective against Dead Existences."
All four Dukes turned their attention to Noah with synchronized precision that spoke to planning or instinct honed over eons.
Duke Valen’s blind eyes seemed to pierce through him despite their lack of function. "You aren’t a Paradox, are you?"
Noah’s smile deepened as he turned toward Duke Whisker, recognizing the mouse’s apparent ability to discern truth from falsehood. "I am not truly a Paradox."
The words were carefully chosen.
He wasn’t truly a Paradox...he was many things beyond Paradox, and fundamentally, he was an Early Creature. The statement was true from a certain perspective, which was all that mattered.
Duke Gwendolyn leaned forward slightly, her ancient eyes searching his face for clues. "Are you someone stemming all the way back from the Earliest Folds? Someone who served... Early Creatures?"
Noah turned to her with that same enigmatic smile. "No."
Duke Pyralis’s flames flickered with increased intensity as she voiced her own theory. "Are you a Mutated Living Existence affected by a Lost Forgotten Principle?"
He shifted his attention to her, finding her theory particularly interesting even as he denied it. "While that would be fascinating, no."
The silence that followed was dense with calculation as four of the most powerful beings in existence tried to categorize something that refused to fit their understanding.
Finally, Duke Whisker floated forward, his tiny hands still clasped behind his back, and asked the question that made the other Dukes visibly tense.
"Are you...an Early Creature?"
BOOM!

The question seemed to make reality itself pause, as if Existence was holding its breath waiting for the answer. Even the other Dukes showed alarm at such a direct inquiry...the implications of a positive answer would shatter every assumption about the current order of existence!
Noah laughed, the sound genuine and amused. "If I was a genuine, full-fledged Early Creature, would I be here playing along with all these games?"

The question carried its own weight of logic. An Early Creature wouldn’t need to trade in marketplaces or attend meetings. They would simply take what they wanted, reshape reality according to their whims.
So he said...he was not a genuine and full fledged early creature!
And well...it was true.
After all, he had not even finished forming his heart!
Duke Whisker’s eyes gleamed with that truth-detecting light. "This... is not false."
The visible relief that washed through the other Dukes was almost comical. Even beings of their power found the prospect of dealing with an Early Creature overwhelming.

Duke Gwendolyn recovered first, her practical nature reasserting itself. "Existence is vast and there are many types of beings out there. What matters is that you hold an alternative to the hungry Living Paradoxes. You have Moiraine, who can empower everyone to fight against Dead Existences, and yourself, of course, who can kill a Duke-level Dead Existence in an instant, right?"
Noah blinked at her words, then responded with casual air that suggested he’d almost forgotten. "Oh, yes, right!"
The confusion that flashed across the Dukes’ faces would have been amusing if the situation weren’t so serious. How did someone forget they had just eliminated a Duke-level threat?

Gwendolyn sighed with the weight of someone trying to herd weavings made of pure chaos. "We can hold Living Paradoxes at length and not give them much recognition with you in the picture. If you were aligned with us. If you let us know what it is you want."

Duke Whisker floated forward. "Everyone wants something. Some seek power, others knowledge, still others simple comfort. But there are those rare beings who are not driven by wants but by purpose, by destiny, by forces greater than personal desire. Some are driven by existence itself as they look over the masses and seek to simply help without anything in return. Which type are you?"
Noah’s smile carried genuine amusement as he looked at the profound little mouse. "I am very much one who wants and takes."

Duke Whisker blinked, his whiskers drooping slightly as his philosophical moment was thoroughly deflated. He shook his tiny head with what might have been exasperation. "Okay then. Straightforward. We can work with straightforward."

The mouse’s demeanor shifted to something more businesslike. "If a cooperation agreement can be reached between us...you providing your strength when needed, we can give you what you want. Because due to recent events, representatives from all ten types of Living Existences will now gather to discuss the threat of Dead Existences. Living Paradoxes will be included in these discussions for the first time since the Earliest Folds."

His tiny form seemed to swell with the importance of what he was about to say. "The Kleos Concordat will convene within a day. Every Duke who can be spared, select Royal Living Existences, and certain other parties of interest will gather to determine how existence itself will respond to these threats."
The name carried weight that pressed against consciousness itself!
The Kleos Concordat...a gathering that transcended normal meetings, where decisions would be made that could reshape the fundamental nature of how existence operated!

"It would be good," Duke Whisker continued, his stellar eyes boring into Noah’s with intensity that belied his small size, "to know who are enemies and who are friends when that time comes. The lines are being drawn as we speak. Where will you stand when the moment arrives?"
The question buzzed in the garden air between the impossible plants and their Wheel-fruits, waiting for an answer that would echo across existence itself!
