chapters.title: Chapter 4004: The 10 Living Existences! IV
paragraphs: Where would he stand when the time came?
The question hung in the garden’s impossible air, weighted with implications that stretched across existence itself.
Noah let the tension flow through the space, feeling how each Duke leaned into his eventual answer, when Duke Gwendolyn’s voice cut through the moment with surgical precision.
"When it comes to this, I have to mention something else." She turned to face the other Dukes, her stellar dark hair catching light.
"Something that makes his alignment with us..." she pointed directly at Noah, "clear."
The words fell into the garden like stones into still water, creating ripples of anticipation that made even the Wheels of Existence hanging from their branches slow their eternal rotations.

Something that made his alignment with them clear? Noah’s mind raced through possibilities, his enhanced perception catching the subtle shift in Gwendolyn’s posture that suggested she was about to cross a line they had agreed upon.
Duke Whisker’s stellar eyes flashed with sharp intensity, his tiny form radiating sudden wariness. "You seemed hesitant before, Gwendolyn. Why say it now?"

Noah’s expression hardened as understanding crystallized with cold certainty. He knew exactly what she planned to reveal, and his voice emerged with an almost rebuking edge that made the temperature in the garden drop perceptibly.
"You agreed not to share anything regarding that."
The words were delivered with the kind of controlled coldness that was more dangerous than any explosion!
Duke Gwendolyn met his gaze steadily, though something in her expression suggested she recognized the magnitude of what she was about to do.

"I did," she acknowledged with a slow nod. "But too much is now at stake. The balance of existence itself teeters on the edge of fundamental change." She paused, seeming to gather her resolve. "I have a body of mine actively protecting her, and you are beside her as well, so I have even less worry regarding her protection. All the Dukes here are those I would give my very existence to protect. I cannot be the only Duke who knows such critical information when the fate of all Living Origins might depend upon it."
Noah’s eyes pulsed!
This fucker.

The blind Duke Valen straightened, his sightless eyes somehow managing to convey stern intensity despite their lack of function. His cane tapped once against the crystalline path, the sound reverberating through dimensions. "What do you mean, Gwendolyn? What information carries such weight that you would break a promise to reveal it?"
Duke Whisker, surprisingly, seemed to be lost in contemplation for a moment before his tiny features arranged themselves into an expression of concern.
When he spoke, his deep voice carried the weight of wisdom earned through witnessing the rise and fall of concepts themselves.
"Gwendolyn," he said, siding with Noah in a way that clearly surprised Duke Gwendolyn, "at times, some things are best left unsaid. The fewer who know certain truths, the safer those truths remain."
Duke Gwendolyn looked at each of them in turn...Noah’s stern disapproval, Whisker’s unexpected caution, Valen’s demanding curiosity, and Pyralis’s burning intensity.

She saw the weight of their combined attention, felt the pressure of secrets that wanted to remain hidden, and shook her head with the resignation of someone who had already crossed the point of no return in their mind.

"No," she said firmly. "The stakes are far too high. She needs to be protected by more than just us. Given resources by more than just us." Her voice grew heavy with the magnitude of what she was about to reveal. "She was the hope of Living Origins. She is."
HUUM!
The moment those words left her lips, Duke Whisker’s eyes blazed with sudden understanding while the other two Dukes showed expressions of pure shock that they struggled to contain.
Duke Valen’s voice emerged as barely more than a whisper, though it carried through the garden with perfect clarity. "You don’t mean..."

Duke Gwendolyn nodded solemnly, sealing their fate with words that could never be taken back. "The Young Miss. THE Living Order has been found. Secured. Protected." Her gaze turned to Noah with something that might have been apology. "She is closely entangled with him, and he with her. That is why I have no doubt he sides with us."
This fucker.
The silence that followed was deafening.

Noah’s expression, as he looked at Duke Gwendolyn, transformed into something that showed coldness. It was immense disappointment, the kind that came from watching someone you had begun to respect shatter that respect through a single action.
He had told her not to say it. She had been explicitly instructed not to share this information. And yet, at this crucial moment, she had freely revealed it because she trusted those present!
Trust. Such a fragile thing, so easily given and so catastrophically misplaced.
His eyes moved across the assembled Dukes, gauging their reactions with the careful precision of someone cataloging potential threats.

Duke Whisker looked down contemplatively, his tiny hands clasped behind his back as he processed implications that stretched across eons. The other two Dukes showed surprise they quickly tried to reign in, but their eyes had already sharpened with new interest, new calculation.

Duke Pyralis’s flames flared with sudden intensity, her voice cutting through the silence with demands that made Noah’s disappointment deepen. "THE Living Order was one of the biggest projects of the Living Origins. How is she entangled with him? Where is she right now? We need to..."

Noah shook his head sharply, cutting off her questions as his gaze returned to Duke Gwendolyn. The disappointment in his eyes was palpable, a weight that seemed to press against her consciousness with more force than any physical blow could have achieved.

Duke Gwendolyn sighed, recognizing his displeasure but pressing forward with the conviction of someone who believed they were right despite all evidence to the contrary. "All those here are to be trusted. We are the ones who analyze other Dukes of Origin to ensure we are all aligned...Duke Whisker sees to that personally. I understand the fear of betrayal, but you will not find it among us. If we have no trust, we have no strength."

chapters.title: Chapter 4005: The 10 Living Existences! V
paragraphs: Noah simply shook his head at this. In that moment, watching her justify her breach of confidence with platitudes about trust and strength, he lost all respect for her.
Trust was not something to be assumed or demanded...it was earned through consistent action, through keeping one’s word even when circumstances made it difficult.

Gwendolyn turned toward the other Dukes, continuing despite his obvious disapproval. "Knowing of her survival, also know that she shattered her Realm and is now reestablishing it...rebuilding her purpose. To allow her to become an Honored Existence and then grant her the power of a Duke and even higher will need the resources of all Living Origins. That is why I told you. As for where she is now..."
"Don’t fucking say that too." Noah’s voice cut through her words like a blade through silk, the profanity carrying more weight for its rarity!
Simultaneously, Duke Whisker’s voice joined his in urgent warning. "Don’t... reveal that."
Noah’s eyes met Duke Whisker’s, a moment of unexpected alliance passing between them. This mouse was much better to his liking than the Duke he thought would be a decent ally!
The ancient mouse spoke toward Gwendolyn with his wizened stellar eyes carrying gentle but firm reproach.

"It is enough for us to know she lives," Whisker said carefully. "Even though we are powerful, there may always be those stronger. Even though we believe nobody is listening, someone could always be listening. The walls of existence have ears we cannot perceive, memories we cannot erase. The return of THE Living Order is a momentous occasion that we must approach delicately, not with the blunt instrument of full disclosure."
Duke Gwendolyn appeared surprised by Whisker’s words, perhaps expecting support from the being who verified truth for their circle.

But she nodded, seeming to finally understand that she had already said too much. Her attention returned to Noah, and when she spoke, her voice carried a mixture of authority and something that might have been plea.
"All is known between us now. Can we continue counting on your support? With THE Living Order? Against the schemes of the Living Paradoxes?"
Noah looked at her with that same stern gaze of disappointment, his voice emerging cold as winter’s final breath. "You can count on my support."
The words were delivered without warmth, without the earlier ease of their interaction!
His displeasure at her revealing information about Sigrid, THE Living Order...radiated from him in waves that made the impossible plants in the garden lean away from his presence.
Because the more beings that knew such secrets, the more possible variables entered the equation!
And things were already messy enough without adding unnecessary complications. Who needed more variables when the board was already so complex that a single misplaced piece could topple everything?!

Across the folds of existence, through layers of reality that most beings would never perceive, through the Transcendent Temporal Folds where time flowed like rivers, through the Transcendent Origin Folds where beginnings were born, and through multiple other domains of impossibility, there existed... the Transcendent Conceptual Folds.

In the depths of these Folds, where abstract thought had been given form and substance, rose the Ethereal Summit of Unspoken Truths...a hazy silver mountain surrounded by thousands of swirling multicolored Wheels of Existence.
Each wheel contained within it concepts that had shaped reality itself: Love, Hatred, Justice, Mercy, and thousands of others that most minds couldn’t even name.

Deep inside the mountain’s hollowed core, in a domain protected by immense waves of Living Conceptual Authority where silver and white seas mixed in patterns that resembled thoughts becoming real, there existed a plain that defied every expectation of what power could create.

The vegetation here burst with waves of complexity that would make Honored Living Existences mad with greed. Flowers bloomed with petals of crystallized inspiration, their scent carrying enlightenment that could advance understanding by eons.
Trees grew with bark of compressed wisdom, their leaves whispering secrets that predated current existence!
Grasses swayed in breezes that carried the fragmentary thoughts of existence itself, each blade worth more than entire civilizations.
Yet what made this place truly remarkable were not the impossible plants, but the auras that permeated it.
Ten different terrifying Living Existences had gathered here, each one eclipsing the power of normal Dukes by margins that rendered comparison meaningless.

A Living Temporal lounged beside a fountain where past and future flowed as separate streams. A Living Spirit floated in meditation, their form shifting between states of consciousness. A Living Emotive sat surrounded by crystals that captured and reflected every feeling that had ever been felt.
A Living Law stood rigid as justice itself, while a Living Elemental swirled between states of matter with each breath.

A Living Quantum existed in multiple positions simultaneously until observed. A Living Dimensional folded space around themselves like origami. A Living Concept pondered thoughts that could reshape reality if spoken aloud!
And shockingly, horrifically, impossibly...a Living Paradox was among them.
The Living Paradox was none other than the beggar-looking being known as...Schrodinger.

He sat cross-legged on a simple mat, his tattered robes pooling around him as he focused on a board game with pieces that seemed to exist in multiple states simultaneously. His opponent, the Living Concept, moved pieces that represented ideas rather than armies, each placement changing the nature of the game itself.
In the middle of moving a piece that might have been Hope or Despair depending on the angle of observation, Schrodinger looked up with a smile that carried too much knowledge.
His gaze found the Living Origin among their gathering, and his voice emerged with casual curiosity that belied the weight of his words.
"I sense you have found something critical. What is it, O Valen?"
BOOM!
The shocking revelation settled into the space...among these terrifying beings, Duke Valen actually maintained one of his bodies here!
The Blind Oracle who had traded his sight for true vision seemed troubled as he rose from his seated position, his white robes flowing around him like liquid truth.
"THE Living Order," he said slowly, each word carrying the weight of impossible discovery, "has been found once more."
Schrodinger’s hand froze above the game board, a piece that was simultaneously Victory and Defeat hovering in his grip.
"Oh?" The single syllable carried more interest than entire speeches might have contained.
The game was forgotten as he turned his full attention to this revelation, his beggar’s appearance doing nothing to diminish the terrible intelligence that blazed in his ancient eyes!

This mouse was much better to his liking than the Duke he thought would be a decent ally!
The ancient mouse spoke toward Gwendolyn with his wizened stellar eyes carrying gentle but firm reproach.
"It is enough for us to know she lives," Whisker said carefully.
"Even though we are powerful, there may always be those stronger.
Even though we believe nobody is listening, someone could always be listening.
The walls of existence have ears we cannot perceive, memories we cannot erase.
The return of THE Living Order is a momentous occasion that we must approach delicately, not with the blunt instrument of full disclosure."
Duke Gwendolyn appeared surprised by Whisker’s words, perhaps expecting support from the being who verified truth for their circle.
But she nodded, seeming to finally understand that she had already said too much.
Her attention returned to Noah, and when she spoke, her voice carried a mixture of authority and something that might have been plea.
"All is known between us now.
Can we continue counting on your support?
With THE Living Order?
Against the schemes of the Living Paradoxes?"
Noah looked at her with that same stern gaze of disappointment, his voice emerging cold as winter’s final breath.
"You can count on my support."
The words were delivered without warmth, without the earlier ease of their interaction!
His displeasure at her revealing information about Sigrid, THE Living Order...radiated from him in waves that made the impossible plants in the garden lean away from his presence.
Because the more beings that knew such secrets, the more possible variables entered the equation!
And things were already messy enough without adding unnecessary complications.
Who needed more variables when the board was already so complex that a single misplaced piece could topple everything?!

Across the folds of existence, through layers of reality that most beings would never perceive, through the Transcendent Temporal Folds where time flowed like rivers, through the Transcendent Origin Folds where beginnings were born, and through multiple other domains of impossibility, there existed... the Transcendent Conceptual Folds.

In the depths of these Folds, where abstract thought had been given form and substance, rose the Ethereal Summit of Unspoken Truths...a hazy silver mountain surrounded by thousands of swirling multicolored Wheels of Existence.
Each wheel contained within it concepts that had shaped reality itself: Love, Hatred, Justice, Mercy, and thousands of others that most minds couldn’t even name.

Deep inside the mountain’s hollowed core, in a domain protected by immense waves of Living Conceptual Authority where silver and white seas mixed in patterns that resembled thoughts becoming real, there existed a plain that defied every expectation of what power could create.
The vegetation here burst with waves of complexity that would make Honored Living Existences mad with greed.
Flowers bloomed with petals of crystallized inspiration, their scent carrying enlightenment that could advance understanding by eons.
Trees grew with bark of compressed wisdom, their leaves whispering secrets that predated current existence!
Grasses swayed in breezes that carried the fragmentary thoughts of existence itself, each blade worth more than entire civilizations.
Yet what made this place truly remarkable were not the impossible plants, but the auras that permeated it.
Ten different terrifying Living Existences had gathered here, each one eclipsing the power of normal Dukes by margins that rendered comparison meaningless.
A Living Temporal lounged beside a fountain where past and future flowed as separate streams.
A Living Spirit floated in meditation, their form shifting between states of consciousness.
A Living Emotive sat surrounded by crystals that captured and reflected every feeling that had ever been felt.
A Living Law stood rigid as justice itself, while a Living Elemental swirled between states of matter with each breath.
A Living Quantum existed in multiple positions simultaneously until observed.
A Living Dimensional folded space around themselves like origami.
A Living Concept pondered thoughts that could reshape reality if spoken aloud!
And shockingly, horrifically, impossibly...a Living Paradox was among them.
The Living Paradox was none other than the beggar-looking being known as...Schrodinger.
He sat cross-legged on a simple mat, his tattered robes pooling around him as he focused on a board game with pieces that seemed to exist in multiple states simultaneously.
His opponent, the Living Concept, moved pieces that represented ideas rather than armies, each placement changing the nature of the game itself.
In the middle of moving a piece that might have been Hope or Despair depending on the angle of observation, Schrodinger looked up with a smile that carried too much knowledge.
His gaze found the Living Origin among their gathering, and his voice emerged with casual curiosity that belied the weight of his words.
"I sense you have found something critical.
What is it, O Valen?"
BOOM!
The shocking revelation settled into the space...among these terrifying beings, Duke Valen actually maintained one of his bodies here!
The Blind Oracle who had traded his sight for true vision seemed troubled as he rose from his seated position, his white robes flowing around him like liquid truth.
"THE Living Order," he said slowly, each word carrying the weight of impossible discovery, "has been found once more."
Schrodinger’s hand froze above the game board, a piece that was simultaneously Victory and Defeat hovering in his grip.
"Oh?" The single syllable carried more interest than entire speeches might have contained.
The game was forgotten as he turned his full attention to this revelation, his beggar’s appearance doing nothing to diminish the terrible intelligence that blazed in his ancient eyes!

chapters.title: Chapter 4006: The 10 Living Existences! VI
paragraphs: The revelation hung in the mountain’s hollowed depths like a bell that had just been struck, its resonance making even these ancient beings pause in their contemplations!
Duke Valen’s words about THE Living Order’s return had transformed the atmosphere from one of casual gathering to something far more consequential.

The blind Duke moved with deliberate grace across the crystalline floor, each tap of his cane sending ripples through the silver-white seas of Conceptual Authority that flowed beneath their feet. When he stopped before the board game, his sightless eyes somehow managed to convey the weight of his concern as he addressed both players.
"The return of THE Living Order," he said, his voice carrying the particular timbre of someone who had witnessed too many returns that ended in tragedy. "What do you think about it?"

Schrodinger’s smile deepened, though something in his expression suggested memories being carefully examined and weighed. He moved a piece on the board...something that might have been Doubt transforming into Certainty, before responding.

"Order," he began, savoring the word as if tasting something exotic and long-forbidden, "was something I never had the chance of coming across. Not properly, at least. Not in its pure, original form."

His fingers drummed against his tattered robes in a rhythm that seemed to echo through dimensions. "THE Living Law was the only one of those original beings I had the pleasure, if we can call it that, to encounter directly. And even that thing terrified me."

The admission sent subtle waves through the gathered entities. For Schrodinger to admit fear was not weakness but rather an acknowledgment of forces that transcended even their elevated understanding.

"Consider what THE Living Law represented," Schrodinger continued. "Not just rules or structure, but the fundamental assertion that existence should operate according to comprehensible patterns. That chaos should have boundaries. That actions should have predictable consequences. When I stood before her...I felt my very nature rebel against her presence. Every paradox within me screamed at the wrongness of such absolute certainty."
He paused, letting his words settle into the consciousness of his audience before continuing with calculated precision.

"If that girl...the one whose entire lineage you Origins systematically eliminated to create the proper conditions for Order’s awakening...truly does become THE Living Order..." He trailed off, his expression growing contemplative. "It will be a good thing. Existence needs its anchor, its foundation stone. Without Order, we’re all just... possibilities floating in an ocean of maybe."
HUUM!
Duke Valen snorted, the sound carrying more meaning than entire speeches might have contained.
His blind gaze fixed on Schrodinger with the particular intensity of someone who could see through deceptions that eyes might miss.

"You speak as if you weren’t the one who advised me on how to possibly awaken the Order within her. Your cryptic hints, your careful nudges in specific directions." The Duke’s cane tapped once against the floor, the sound sharp as accusation. "Whatever. Her reentry is good for stability, but it does muddy the waters somewhat."

Valen turned slightly, as if observing something beyond the mountain’s confines. "Oh, and there’s another matter. The same being who moved across your Existential Trembling against Aion completely unaffected, the one who took your little Paradox Moiraine... he is somehow entangled with THE Living Order. I cannot fully gauge what his actual power is."
The reaction was immediate and palpable.

Several of the terrifying beings who had been maintaining distance from the conversation suddenly drew closer. A Living Temporal materialized from what had been a shadow, while the Living Emotive’s crystalline arrangements chimed with sudden interest.
Schrodinger’s hand paused above the board, a piece that existed in multiple states simultaneously hovering in his grip. His smile grew wider, though his eyes remained calculating.

"That is certainly interesting," he mused, finally placing the piece with deliberate care. "Moiraine was traveling with someone that little Diviticus swallowed a bit. Someone who should have something relating to Early Creatures. Possibly blessed with a corpse of another Early Creature, or perhaps an Inheritor of a Sleeping Shore." His gaze sharpened, cutting through the philosophical veneer to something more immediate. "Could he be one and the same?"

The Living Quantum, who had been existing in seventeen different positions simultaneously, suddenly collapsed into a single location beside them. When it spoke, its voice carried the weight of calculated probabilities!
"What happened with the corpse of the Early Creature we decided to let the Paradoxes have for the first time? Did that Diviticus use whatever she obtained to..."

"Little Diviticus managed to innervate the corpse of the Early Creature," Schrodinger interrupted, his tone carrying a mixture of pride and concern that suggested complicated feelings about his fellow Paradox. "She’s a shooting star now, burning bright across the darkness of our current predicament. Who knows?" He looked over the others with an expression of gentle mockery. "She might become more powerful than any of you."
The harrumphs and dismissive gestures that followed would have been comical if not for the fact that each being present could reshape reality with their displeasure.
Duke Valen’s eyes flashed with particular sharpness, his voice cutting through the protests.
"So through your actions, we are tearing the veil between the Living and the Dead early. Earlier than when the veil should have begun to come down naturally."

Schrodinger waved his hands dismissively, the gesture somehow managing to convey both acknowledgment and indifference. "Just a few years earlier. The veil was bound to be torn eventually...at least now, we can control where the tears appear, how wide they grow. Everything has a price, my friends. We have been preparing for the Dead Existences for eons, developing countermeasures, training forces. But even they..."
He paused, letting the weight of anticipation build before delivering his next words with careful precision.
"Even they are not our final enemies."
HUUM!
The atmosphere in the mountain’s depths grew heavy with implications that pressed against consciousness itself.
The entities present exchanged glances...or whatever equivalent their forms allowed, each one processing this statement through their own vast understanding.

Schrodinger looked at each of them in turn, his beggar’s appearance doing nothing to diminish the ancient intelligence that blazed in his eyes. When he smiled this time, it carried the particular quality of someone about to share a secret they’d been holding for far too long.
"Do you want to hear a Story from the Earliest Folds that nobody else knows?"

chapters.title: Chapter 4007: True Enemies!
paragraphs: Schrodinger had asked if they wanted to hear a story from the Earliest Folds!
But...
The collective eye-roll that followed was almost synchronized, as if they’d performed this routine countless times before. The Living Concept actually sighed, the sound like ideas deflating.
“Not another one of your possibly-true, possibly-invented parables,” someone muttered.
Schrodinger laughed, the sound genuine and warm despite the weight of their discussion. “Listen, this one is particularly relevant. I promise.”
He settled back slightly, his posture shifting into the comfortable stance of a storyteller who knew his audience couldn’t resist despite their protests.

“At a time when chaos was most rampant in the Earliest Folds...when Early Creatures hunted for sport and Inevitabilities bloomed like flowers after rain...there was an Early Creature who happened to overhear a conversation. This creature, whose name has been deliberately forgotten, witnessed THE Living Law visiting the locked Paradox in its prison of contradictions.”
HUUM!
The mountain seemed to grow quieter, even the flow of Conceptual Authority beneath their feet stilling to better hear the tale.

“THE Living Law stood before the chains of impossibility that bound THE Living Paradox, and she asked a question that had been burning in her consciousness since the first Inevitability emerged. ‘Are Inevitabilities the true enemies of all Existences?'”
Schrodinger’s voice took on different tones as he embodied each character, his talent for storytelling evident despite the tattered appearance he maintained.

“At such a question, THE Living Paradox laughed...an eerie sound that existed simultaneously as mirth and despair. ‘What,’ it said, ‘just because even before THE Creature, the Inevitabilities were there? Just because they predate understanding, and the very conception of what should and shouldn’t be?'”
The storyteller paused, letting tension build before continuing in a voice that captured the bound Paradox’s terrifying certainty.

“‘No,’ THE Living Paradox said, its voice carrying that particular quality of statements that were simultaneously true and false. ‘Even Inevitabilities are not the true enemies of all Existences. No, the biggest enemy of Existences... is existence itself.'”
HUUM!
Several of the listeners shifted uncomfortably at this pronouncement, recognizing philosophical depths that threatened to drown rational thought.

“‘Existence is feeble,’ the Paradox continued. ‘Undecided. Uncertain. It doesn’t know whether it wants to be or not to be, whether it should expand or contract, whether consciousness is blessing or curse. That was why I sought to put it under my control...to give it the direction it so desperately lacks.'”
Schrodinger’s voice grew lighter, more mocking as he continued channeling the bound Paradox.

“‘The true enemy of Existences?’ THE Living Paradox laughed again. ‘Who knows? I could be the true enemy...after all, I’m talking to you right now, aren’t I? Or perhaps it’s you, THE Living Law, with your rigid insistence that everything follow rules. Maybe it’s any of the others, or all of them together. Perhaps it’s THE Creature itself.’ A pause, then with something almost like fondness: ‘How is that kid doing nowadays anyway? Without my guidance, he may be getting lost. You all haven’t done anything crazy without me, right?'”
The silence that followed in the story was mirrored by the silence in the mountain’s depths. Schrodinger continued, his voice now embodying THE Living Law’s heavy response.
“‘Out of all of us, you could have been so great.'”
The statement hung between the characters in the story like an accusation and a lament combined.

“This caused an immense silence to descend before THE Living Paradox laughed once more and began what would become its most famous monologue...though famous only to the Early Creature who overhead it.”
Schrodinger’s voice took on a philosophical depth that made even these ancient beings lean in slightly.

“‘What is greatness?’ the Paradox asked. ‘Is it power accumulated until reality bends to acknowledge your supremacy? Is it understanding gathered until the mysteries of existence lay bare before your perception? Or is it something more... paradoxical?'”
The beggar-Duke’s delivery grew more animated, his hands moving to emphasize points that existed in multiple interpretations simultaneously.

“‘Consider: I am locked here, chains of impossibility binding me in ways that should prevent even thought. Yet I think. I speak. I influence. My very imprisonment has become legendary, a cautionary tale that shapes how billions of consciousnesses will understand reality. In my cage, I... am more present in existence than I ever was while free.'”
He paused, his voice dropping to barely above a whisper that somehow carried perfectly through the space.

“‘Me, locked up right now, could be a grandiose form of greatness. The greatest teacher is the one whose lessons are learned without their presence. The greatest warrior is the one whose battles are won without fighting. The greatest paradox is the one that resolves itself by remaining unresolved. Maybe I’m locked here... maybe I’m actually free. Who knows?'”

Schrodinger ended the story there, his eyes moving across the assembled beings with an expression that suggested layers of meaning they might never fully unpack. The silence that followed was dense with contemplation, each entity processing the parable through their own vast understanding.
Did this actually happen? Was it true? Was it false? None could say!

“When it comes to true enemies,” Schrodinger said, returning to his normal voice with its mixture of wisdom and whimsy, “there are few, and yet many. We simply have to do what we can to ensure that Existence keeps chugging along, keeps asking whether it should be rather than surrendering to shouldn’t.”
He smiled with something approaching genuine warmth as he looked at each of them.

“My friends...and yes, I do consider you friends despite your constant skepticism of my stories, we have much to do. Oh, and in a day’s time, at the Kleos Concordat, we might see each other under the gazes of others for the first time in a while. Don’t treat me too coldly, okay? You all are, after all, the closest I have to...friends in existence.”

Duke Valen snorted at this sentiment, though something in his expression suggested the dismissal was more habit than genuine feeling. “So, what shall be done about THE Living Order? Moiraine? And the Enigma entangled with both of them who possibly has links to an inheritance of an Early Creature?”
Schrodinger’s smile deepened as he moved another piece on the board...Victory becoming Defeat becoming Something Else Entirely.
“What to do indeed,” he mused, the words carrying the weight of plans within plans, possibilities within paradoxes. “What to do indeed...”

chapters.title: Chapter 4008: The Difference of Everything!
paragraphs: In the time before time was measured, when existence still questioned whether it should continue existing, there lived an Early Creature whose ambition exceeded its understanding.
This creature, whose name has been deliberately erased from all records, watched THE Creature with the kind of devotion that bordered on obsession.

THE Creature moved through the Earliest Folds with purpose that defied comprehension, each action reshaping Existence in ways that wouldn’t be understood for eons. And at a certain period, invariably, THE Living Concept came and stayed at its side...the manifestation of thought itself given form and consciousness.

The Early Creature studied these interactions with desperate intensity. It saw how THE Creature would pose questions that THE Living Concept would transform into realities. It witnessed conversations that birthed entire categories of existence.
And in its limited understanding, it believed that proximity to THE Living Concept was one of the keys to THE Creature’s transcendent nature.
At a certain time, THE Creature disappeared.
And the Early Creature...thought its chance had come!
So it began to follow.

At first, THE Living Concept ignored the Early Creature’s presence, treating it with the same indifference it showed to the countless other beings that populated the Earliest Folds. But as days became years, and years stretched toward epochs, the persistence grew impossible to overlook.
“You are not like your predecessor,” THE Living Concept finally said, its voice carrying the weight of absolute truth. “You should not try to be like him.”
The Early Creature’s response blazed with the particular arrogance of youth convinced of its own destiny. “But I can become like him! If I understand what you teach, if I learn what you know...”
“Knowledge without foundation is merely sophisticated ignorance,” THE Living Concept interrupted. “You chase shadows while ignoring the light that casts them.”

But the Early Creature would not be deterred. It continued its pursuit with the single-minded determination that marked its kind, following THE Living Concept through domains where thought became substance, through regions where ideas went to die and be reborn.
Then came the day when Inevitabilities found it.
They emerged from the spaces between certainty, those paradoxical entities that existed because they shouldn’t, that thrived on the contradiction of their own nature.
The Early Creature found itself surrounded, its considerable power...power that could reshape entire Folds...suddenly, terrifyingly insufficient.
“Help me!” it pleaded to THE Living Concept, who observed from a position just beyond the ring of Inevitabilities. “I have followed you faithfully! I have learned your teachings!”

THE Living Concept’s response carried neither cruelty nor compassion, merely the weight of truth acknowledged. “I did warn you. Sometimes, one will never measure up to be like someone else. You should have been trying to forge your own existence, not attempting to replicate another’s.”
Defiance blazed through the Early Creature’s form as Inevitabilities pressed closer, their paradoxical presence beginning to unravel its carefully maintained existence.
“I will give you my Everything to be saved! Everything I am, everything I could become...take it all!”

THE Living Concept regarded it with the particular attention reserved for moments that would echo through eternity. When it spoke, each word fell like judgment rendered in the court of existence itself.

“Your Everything and THE Creature’s Everything are incomparable. The difference is so vast, so fundamentally insignificant, that even now it does not motivate me to take it.” THE Living Concept paused, allowing the weight of this truth to settle. “I could find an ant...a simple, momentary creature barely aware of its own existence...and its Everything might be larger than yours.”
HUUM!
The Early Creature’s defiance crumbled into confusion, then horror, as understanding began to dawn.

“Across Existence,” THE Living Concept continued, its voice carrying the finality of lessons that would never be repeated, “every creature has their Everything. Their worth. Their fundamental value in the grand equation of what is and what might be. But the worth of some...their Everything...is unfathomably more prized than others.”
The Inevitabilities closed in, their paradoxical nature beginning to dissolve the Early Creature’s form into component possibilities.

“And more often than not,” THE Living Concept concluded, already turning away from the scene, “very few can accurately gauge worth. You spent eternity trying to become something you could never be, when you might have become something unprecedented. The tragedy is not in your ending, but in your never truly beginning.”
The lesson echoed through the Earliest Folds.
Worth...cannot be claimed or demanded. It simply is, or isn’t, and the ability to recognize it remains one of existence’s rarest gifts.
In the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds.
The Doorway to the Loom stretched before them in all its paradoxical glory, each step forward somehow also being a step in directions that had no names.
They had been traversing for what felt like hours but could have been moments or centuries...time held little meaning in spaces where Paradox itself had carved the pathways!

Noah’s enhanced perception took in their current location with careful assessment. They stood at the edge of a region that challenged every assumption about what landscape could be. A mountain of pure red black flame rose before them, its surface not merely burning but existing in a state of perpetual conflagration that seemed to feed on space itself.
The flames didn’t produce smoke...they produced concepts that dissolved before they could be understood.

At the mountain’s peak, visible through the dancing conflagration and the storms that raged around it, a single flower bloomed. Its petals caught light that shouldn’t exist, reflecting colors that had no names, existing in defiance of every force that sought to destroy it.
And those forces were considerable. Storms of pure Paradox raged around the peak, each gust carrying contradictions sharp enough to shred an Honored Living Existence into component possibilities!
The very air seemed to war with itself, being and not-being in rapid succession that created visible tears in reality that sealed themselves only to tear again.

They had paused here after their encounter with the multiplying Inevitability, the one that Titano had so enthusiastically crushed into submission before gifting to Noah. The aftermath of that exchange had left the atmosphere charged with unspoken questions.
Altheon and Thessaly regarded Noah with expressions that mixed wariness with calculation.
Whatever he had given to Titano and Sigrid had transformed them in ways they could not fathom!

The glass woks that Titano had consumed...both their contents and the sacred waters they contained, had elevated the simple giant’s already terrifying physical might to levels that made Honored beings wary.

But it was Sigrid’s transformation that truly commanded attention. Her aura blazed with the intensity of a Prime Living Existence approaching breakthrough, her Tower of Origin reconstructing itself with each passing moment. The very air around her hummed with nascent authority, as if reality itself was preparing to acknowledge her ascension to Honored status.
What could possibly cause such dramatic advancement? What treasures did this mysterious figure possess that could reforge a Tower of Origin to such a terrifying extent?

Titano’s massive form vibrated with barely contained energy as he gazed up at the flower atop the burning mountain. His expression...that mixture of childlike enthusiasm and simple determination that marked all his actions, brightened with sudden purpose.
He beat his chest with enough force to create thunderclaps in the paradoxical atmosphere, the sound somehow both deafening and silent.
“Brother!” he exclaimed, his deep voice carrying the particular cadence of someone who had never quite mastered the language they spoke. “Titano get that little flower for you!”

chapters.title: Chapter 4009: Loyalty! I
paragraphs: The declaration carried such earnest sincerity that it transcended its grammatical imperfection.

This was not a question or a request for permission...it was simply Titano stating what would happen with the certainty of someone who had never encountered a problem that couldn’t be solved through sufficient application of physical force.
Noah nodded, a slight smile playing at his lips as he observed the giant’s enthusiasm. “Be careful with it when you retrieve it.”
“Titano very careful! Titano bring Brother best flower!”
Beside them, Thessaly hovered with the rigid posture of someone struggling to maintain professional composure in the face of increasingly unusual circumstances.
Her fairy-like form radiated disapproval that she couldn’t quite voice, while Altheon gazed ahead with the thousand-yard stare of someone processing too much information simultaneously.

It was at this moment that Noah turned to Sigrid, his movement carrying the glory of decision already made. His hand found her waist with casual certainty, drawing her against his side with a possessiveness that asked for no argument!

She blinked at the sudden proximity, though no embarrassment colored her features. Her sterling smiling eyes met his with the direct gaze of someone who had long since passed beyond such simple emotions. “Why did you do that?”
Her question carried genuine curiosity rather than objection, the kind of inquiry that sought understanding.

Noah’s expression darkened slightly, his gaze shifting to track Titano’s enthusiastic charge toward the mountain. The giant moved through the storms of Paradox as if they were gentle breezes, his massive frame somehow refusing to acknowledge dangers that should have unmade him at the conceptual level.
“I have to keep you closer to me now,” Noah said, his voice carrying weight that made even the paradoxical air grow still. “Duke Gwendolyn decided to inform other Dukes regarding your existence.”
BOOM!
The words fell into the space between them like stones into still water, each one creating ripples of implication that spread outward in waves.
“What?!” Sigrid’s voice cracked with shock that quickly transformed into anger. Her aura flared, Origin authority leaking from her form in patterns that made reality itself step back in recognition!

Noah sighed, his gaze still tracking Titano’s progress as the giant literally punched his way through conceptual storms. “She decided to disclose it to three other Dukes...Whisker, Pyralis, and Valen. She knows they are to be trusted, apparently.” His voice carried a particular bitterness on the last word. “She seems to not understand what trust truly stands for.”
Sigrid’s expression shifted through several emotions in rapid succession...betrayal, anger, understanding, and finally a kind of resigned acceptance.
She grit her teeth hard enough that Noah could hear them grinding like the shattering of Wheels, then shook her head with the weariness of someone recognizing their own culpability.

“No,” she said quietly. “This is my mistake. I knew she was on my side, knew her nature, but I didn’t consider... I didn’t think she would...” She trailed off, then straightened with the kind of resolve that had allowed her to survive the destruction of her original form. “This is on me.”

Noah’s response was immediate and firm, his hand tightening slightly on her waist. “You cannot put the stupid decisions of others on your shoulders. Their choices are their own, and the consequences...”

He was interrupted by the sharp intake of breath from both Altheon and Thessaly. The casual way he referred to Duke Gwendolyn’s decision as ‘stupid’ seemed to challenge their fundamental understanding of hierarchy and respect.

Thessaly rose higher in the air, her tiny form radiating indignation that seemed too large for her fairy-like frame. “Duke Gwendolyn only wants the best for the Young Miss! Anything she does is for...”
“You can shut all the way up.”
WAA!
Noah’s voice cut through her protests with booming words!
His eyes, though showing no obvious manifestation of power, carried something that made even an Honored Living Origin pause.
Thessaly actually felt trepidation crawl up her spine...not from any display of overwhelming might, but from something more fundamental.
The certainty in his gaze suggested consequences she couldn’t quite comprehend!
Her expression soured as words died in her throat, the unsaid protests creating a tension that made the paradoxical atmosphere grow thick.

It was at this moment that Titano descended from the mountain’s peak, his entire form glowing with the residual energy of his passage through impossible storms. His skin had taken on a lustrous quality, as if the paradoxes had polished rather than torn him.
And yet...no Living Existential Authority surrounded him!
In his massive hand, held with the delicate care of someone handling spun glass, was a flower torn from its impossible perch.
“Brother!” Titano’s voice boomed with pride and excitement. “I have gotten it for you! Can I continue to grow my wealth with this?!”
He offered the flower with the enthusiasm of a child presenting a found treasure, his simple face bright with anticipation of approval.
Noah accepted the flower with careful movements, his enhanced perception immediately cataloging its properties.
|Paradox Lotus of Singular Purity|:: A flower that blooms only where impossibility becomes so dense it achieves physical form.
Primary Effect: Grants 5,000,000 Purity Quotient units upon consumption
Growth Requirements: Can bloom where at least three types of Inevitabilities have died, or inside an Early Veiled Shore.
Note: The flower exists in a state of constant dissolution and reformation. Consumption must occur within one hour of picking or it ceases to exist entirely...

Noah nodded appreciatively, recognizing the treasure for what it was as he sent it to his Early Veiled Shore for planting right away. “This will indeed make you richer, Titano. Well done.” He paused, his expression growing thoughtful. “But tell me...what is your relationship to Duke Gwendolyn?”

The question seemed to come from nowhere, yet it landed with the weight of careful calculation. Both Thessaly and Altheon’s expressions grew even more unsightly, recognizing the probe for what it was.

Titano scratched his bald head with one massive finger, his expression growing uncharacteristically serious. “The Duke helped Titano come out of a dark place and into the Folds. Titano owes Duke Gwendolyn everything. Without her...” He trailed off, seeming to struggle with concepts his simple vocabulary couldn’t quite express.
Noah’s expression grew stern as he processed this information. His next words were delivered with careful precision, each one a test of loyalty and possibility.
“What if Gwendolyn did something I did not like, and I told you to leave her and join me? I would give you all the riches you could want. Treasures beyond imagination, power beyond everything. ”
Titano’s eyes, usually bright with simple joy, dimmed noticeably. The giant’s massive frame seemed to shrink slightly, as if the weight of the decision was physically pressing down upon him!
For several long moments, he was silent, his face cycling through expressions as thoughts too complex for his usual demeanor warred within.

Finally, he shook his head with obvious reluctance. “Titano likes Brother. Titano want riches, want to be strong, want many things Brother could give.” His voice grew firmer, more certain. “But Titano owes Duke Gwendolyn. Titano... cannot.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4010: Loyalty! II
paragraphs: The simple declaration of loyalty carried more weight than any elaborate oath might have!
This was not calculated allegiance...it was the fundamental honesty of someone who understood debt and honor in their most basic forms!

Noah frowned at this response, though something in his expression suggested respect for the giant’s stance. He could push here, could probably find ways to manipulate or coerce, but there were other methods. Better methods.

He reached up...a considerable stretch given their height difference, and patted Titano’s massive frame with something approaching fondness. “Do not worry about it. I will talk to Duke Gwendolyn to release you from your debt to her. Would that be acceptable? If she agrees to release you?”

Titano’s face transformed with sudden hope, his eyes brightening like stars emerging from clouds. “If Duke Gwendolyn agrees, Titano would like to go with Brother! Brother makes Titano rich! Brother treats Titano good!”

Noah smiled, filing away this information for future use. “Good. Then that’s what we’ll do.” He looked ahead into the depths of the Doorway where reality continued its war with itself. “For now, let’s see if we can find a few more Inevitabilities, and then we’ll get out of here.”
“Yes!” Titano’s enthusiasm returned in full force, his massive form practically vibrating with excitement. “Titano will clear the way! Titano will find many Inevitabilities for Brother!”

The giant charged ahead with renewed vigor, his terrifying power creating a wake through the paradoxical space that actually made traversal easier for those following. Each step he took seemed to temporarily force reality to choose a single state, creating brief islands of stability in the chaos.
Noah and Sigrid followed at a more measured pace. Sigrid’s expression remained troubled, her mind clearly wrestling with the implications of Gwendolyn’s betrayal of trust.
Noah didn’t even spare a glance for Altheon and Thessaly as they moved forward, his dismissal of their presence more cutting than any direct confrontation could have been!
A tremendous distance away, in the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds, another group made their way through their own Doorway to the Loom.

These doorways were numerous throughout the Battlefront, most leading nowhere, and those that did lead somewhere invariably filled with boundless Inevitabilities or other hazards that prevented advancement toward the ultimate prize.
Alexander Asmodeus moved through this particular Doorway with his characteristic measured grace, each step calculated and precise!
The environment around them defied conventional description...a landscape of shattered white clocks and broken wheels that might have once measured something beyond time.

The fragments floated in air that had the consistency of liquid crystal, each piece reflecting moments that had never occurred, might be occurring, or had already occurred in futures that no longer existed.
The moment their party fully entered the Doorway, prompts materialized before each of them.
|You have entered the Doorway: Origin Graveyard of Forgotten Measurements|
|Special Conditions: Death in this Doorway may retroactively prevent birth. Memories formed here exist in quantum superposition until observed. Success and failure are not mutually exclusive states.|
|Warning: Your perception of entering this Doorway may itself be an echo of a future that won’t occur|
Alexander read through the information with his characteristic calm, his mind already calculating probabilities and possibilities!
Beside him, Seraphina Valorheart gripped her weapon tighter, while Royal Law Tristesse had finally stopped fuming about Noah’s earlier displays, her expression now carved from focused concern.
“This is worse than the report suggested,” Kaedric muttered, his usual confidence shaken by the sheer wrongness of their surroundings.

Tristesse voiced her thoughts as they moved deeper into the Doorway, her attention split between the environment and her companions. “That friend of yours is not ordinary.” She fixed Alexander with a gaze that demanded answers. “If he stems from the same Folds as you...”
Alexander’s frown deepened, clearly wanting to deflect or stop her line of inquiry. But before he could speak, before he could redirect the conversation, something unprecedented occurred!
HUUM!
His Enneagram...that dazzling stellar nine-pointed star that resided on his chest, suddenly blazed with purple-gold light so intense it made reality step back.
Simultaneously, Seraphina Valorheart gasped as her own hidden Enneagram erupted in white-blue brilliance, the light pouring from her form in waves that shouldn’t exist.

The two Enneagrams began to spin in perfect synchronization, their rotation creating weavings that made the shattered clocks and wheels around them resonate. The sound built from whisper to roar to something beyond sound...a fundamental frequency that existence itself recognized!
Then, with the distinctive sound of bronze being torn, space ruptured before them.
The tear that formed was unlike any spatial distortion they had encountered. It didn’t lead to another place...it led to another time, another state of being entirely.
The smell that poured from it defied description: archaic oldness mixed with wonder, the scent of possibilities that had been sealed away since before the current age began!
Prompts cascaded before Alexander’s vision, each one more impossible than the last!
|Desiccated Sleeping Shore of an Early Creature Located|
|The fragments of the Early Tool of THE Living Law have resonated in a domain that THE Living Law’s authority covered in the Earliest Folds|
|Following the paths taken since the Earliest Folds will allow for the recovery of the Early Tool of THE Living Law|
|Warning: This Shore has been dead and sleeping for an unknown number of years|
Alexander stared at the prompts with an expression that cycled through shock, understanding, and grim determination.
Behind him, Royal Law Tristesse’s authority blazed to life, silver-white power creating defensive barriers as her voice cracked with barely controlled alarm.
“What is it?! What happened?” Her usual musical tones had given way to sharp demand, her attention fixed on the archaic tear that promised either unprecedented opportunity or complete annihilation.

Seraphina looked toward Alexander with shock that transformed into something deeper....a recognition that whatever came next would fundamentally change the nature of their journey. “Alexander, what...”
Without explanation, without hesitation, without even acknowledging the questions and concerns of his companions, Alexander Asmodeus stepped into the crack in space.

The bronze tear seemed to welcome him, reality parting like curtains to admit one who carried the keys to doors that had been locked since the Earliest Folds. His form disappeared into that archaic light, leaving his companions to make their own choices about whether to follow into the unknown.
Behind him, Tristesse cursed with the creative eloquence of someone who had lived long enough to know when situations had spiraled completely beyond control!
Yet even as profanity flowed from her lips, she was already moving forward, because some opportunities...and some dangers, were too significant to let pride or caution prevent action!

The Doorway to the Loom suddenly seemed mundane compared to what lay beyond that bronze tear. What slept in that Desiccated Shore? What remnants of THE Living Law’s authority might still linger there? And perhaps most importantly...what would wake when they entered if everything was dead?
The only way to know was to follow Alexander into the archaic unknown, into a Shore that had been sleeping since before the current configuration of existence had been established!

sentences.text: The simple declaration of loyalty carried more weight than any elaborate oath might have!
This was not calculated allegiance...it was the fundamental honesty of someone who understood debt and honor in their most basic forms!
Noah frowned at this response, though something in his expression suggested respect for the giant’s stance.
He could push here, could probably find ways to manipulate or coerce, but there were other methods.
Better methods.
He reached up...a considerable stretch given their height difference, and patted Titano’s massive frame with something approaching fondness.
“Do not worry about it.
I will talk to Duke Gwendolyn to release you from your debt to her.
Would that be acceptable?
If she agrees to release you?”
Titano’s face transformed with sudden hope, his eyes brightening like stars emerging from clouds.
“If Duke Gwendolyn agrees, Titano would like to go with Brother!
Brother makes Titano rich!
Brother treats Titano good!”
Noah smiled, filing away this information for future use.
“Good.
Then that’s what we’ll do.” He looked ahead into the depths of the Doorway where reality continued its war with itself.
“For now, let’s see if we can find a few more Inevitabilities, and then we’ll get out of here.”
“Yes!” Titano’s enthusiasm returned in full force, his massive form practically vibrating with excitement.
“Titano will clear the way!
Titano will find many Inevitabilities for Brother!”
The giant charged ahead with renewed vigor, his terrifying power creating a wake through the paradoxical space that actually made traversal easier for those following.
Each step he took seemed to temporarily force reality to choose a single state, creating brief islands of stability in the chaos.
Noah and Sigrid followed at a more measured pace.
Sigrid’s expression remained troubled, her mind clearly wrestling with the implications of Gwendolyn’s betrayal of trust.
Noah didn’t even spare a glance for Altheon and Thessaly as they moved forward, his dismissal of their presence more cutting than any direct confrontation could have been!
A tremendous distance away, in the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds, another group made their way through their own Doorway to the Loom.

These doorways were numerous throughout the Battlefront, most leading nowhere, and those that did lead somewhere invariably filled with boundless Inevitabilities or other hazards that prevented advancement toward the ultimate prize.
Alexander Asmodeus moved through this particular Doorway with his characteristic measured grace, each step calculated and precise!
The environment around them defied conventional description...a landscape of shattered white clocks and broken wheels that might have once measured something beyond time.

The fragments floated in air that had the consistency of liquid crystal, each piece reflecting moments that had never occurred, might be occurring, or had already occurred in futures that no longer existed.
The moment their party fully entered the Doorway, prompts materialized before each of them.
|You have entered the Doorway: Origin Graveyard of Forgotten Measurements|
|Special Conditions: Death in this Doorway may retroactively prevent birth.
Memories formed here exist in quantum superposition until observed.
Success and failure are not mutually exclusive states.|
|Warning: Your perception of entering this Doorway may itself be an echo of a future that won’t occur|
Alexander read through the information with his characteristic calm, his mind already calculating probabilities and possibilities!
Beside him, Seraphina Valorheart gripped her weapon tighter, while Royal Law Tristesse had finally stopped fuming about Noah’s earlier displays, her expression now carved from focused concern.
“This is worse than the report suggested,” Kaedric muttered, his usual confidence shaken by the sheer wrongness of their surroundings.
Tristesse voiced her thoughts as they moved deeper into the Doorway, her attention split between the environment and her companions.
“That friend of yours is not ordinary.” She fixed Alexander with a gaze that demanded answers.
“If he stems from the same Folds as you...”
Alexander’s frown deepened, clearly wanting to deflect or stop her line of inquiry.
But before he could speak, before he could redirect the conversation, something unprecedented occurred!
HUUM!
His Enneagram...that dazzling stellar nine-pointed star that resided on his chest, suddenly blazed with purple-gold light so intense it made reality step back.
Simultaneously, Seraphina Valorheart gasped as her own hidden Enneagram erupted in white-blue brilliance, the light pouring from her form in waves that shouldn’t exist.
The two Enneagrams began to spin in perfect synchronization, their rotation creating weavings that made the shattered clocks and wheels around them resonate.
The sound built from whisper to roar to something beyond sound...a fundamental frequency that existence itself recognized!
Then, with the distinctive sound of bronze being torn, space ruptured before them.
The tear that formed was unlike any spatial distortion they had encountered.
It didn’t lead to another place...it led to another time, another state of being entirely.
The smell that poured from it defied description: archaic oldness mixed with wonder, the scent of possibilities that had been sealed away since before the current age began!
Prompts cascaded before Alexander’s vision, each one more impossible than the last!
|Desiccated Sleeping Shore of an Early Creature Located|
|The fragments of the Early Tool of THE Living Law have resonated in a domain that THE Living Law’s authority covered in the Earliest Folds|
|Following the paths taken since the Earliest Folds will allow for the recovery of the Early Tool of THE Living Law|
|Warning: This Shore has been dead and sleeping for an unknown number of years|
Alexander stared at the prompts with an expression that cycled through shock, understanding, and grim determination.
Behind him, Royal Law Tristesse’s authority blazed to life, silver-white power creating defensive barriers as her voice cracked with barely controlled alarm.
“What is it?!
What happened?” Her usual musical tones had given way to sharp demand, her attention fixed on the archaic tear that promised either unprecedented opportunity or complete annihilation.
Seraphina looked toward Alexander with shock that transformed into something deeper....a recognition that whatever came next would fundamentally change the nature of their journey.
“Alexander, what...”
Without explanation, without hesitation, without even acknowledging the questions and concerns of his companions, Alexander Asmodeus stepped into the crack in space.
The bronze tear seemed to welcome him, reality parting like curtains to admit one who carried the keys to doors that had been locked since the Earliest Folds.
His form disappeared into that archaic light, leaving his companions to make their own choices about whether to follow into the unknown.
Behind him, Tristesse cursed with the creative eloquence of someone who had lived long enough to know when situations had spiraled completely beyond control!

chapters.title: Chapter 4011: Integrity! I
paragraphs: The garden of impossible fruits seemed to hold its breath as the last of the Dukes departed through their various methods...Duke Whisker simply ceasing to be present, Duke Pyralis leaving in a conflagration that somehow froze the air, and Duke Valen tapping his way through a door that hadn’t existed until he needed it.
Now only Duke Gwendolyn remained, her stellar dark hair catching light that originated from the Wheels of Existence hanging overhead.
Her expression carried a type of particular calmness!

“It seems like you had something to say,” she began, her voice maintaining that diplomatic steadiness that had served her through eons of maneuvering. “I did what I did for the sake of the Young Miss. To help her. To ensure she has everything she needs-”
“Yeah, yeah.”
Noah’s interruption cut through her justification with the casual dismissal of someone who simply didnt care!
His voice emerged coldly.
“Titano. Release him from the debt he owes you. I will take him under my wing.”
The demand fell into the garden’s atmosphere like a stone through still water.
Her expression shifted from calm certainty to genuine surprise, her head tilting slightly as if the angle might help her understand why Titano would suddenly be relevant to their discussion.
But understanding dawned quickly...too quickly for someone of her intelligence to miss the implications!
Her eyes widened as pieces fell into place, her entire bearing shifting from diplomatic to intensely focused.
“Did you...” she began, her voice carrying newfound wariness, “already grasp his nature? Did you find out what he really is?”
His nature.

It might not have mattered to Noah under different circumstances, but his distinction as the Weaver of Existence...that ever-evolving capability that grew more complex with each passing moment, had revealed Titano’s true nature some time ago.
The moment he had first laid eyes on the giant while they went through the doorway, purple text had materialized above his head, revealing truths that most would never perceive!
Noah’s eyes flickered as he recalled the information, the information materializing in his vision with perfect clarity.
|Titano - The Unbreaking Fist|
Classification: Mutated Living Existence affected by Lost Forgotten Principle
Lost Forgotten Principle Influence: The Principle of Absolute Physicality- One of the earliest principles established when existence first wondered if thought or substance held primacy.
-Grants the ability to impose physical reality over conceptual authority
-Current Integration: 1% (Unconscious)
Living Existential Mutation: Corporeal Supremacy- Physical form exists in a state of fundamental priority over energy-based attacks
-Body naturally negates up to 99% of Living Existential Authority from beings below Duke level
-Strength operates on pre-existence parameters, allowing interaction with concepts as if they were physical
-Limitation: Cannot consciously control or understand his own nature
-Side Effect: Drastically reduced intellectual capacity in exchange for absolute physical dominance

Combat Rating: Can physically overcome any Honored Living Existence through brute force alone. Can wrestle Royal Living Existences to stalemate. Duke-level entities require a bit of effort to damage him.
Hidden Potential: If consciousness could be elevated while maintaining mutation, would become one of the most terrifying existences in current reality...
He could obtain waves of lengthy information if he wanted to!

And he now gave the information a dismissive glance before returning his attention to Gwendolyn. “It matters not what being he is. He is too simple and earnest to be under someone like you, so release him.”
The implication was clear...Titano’s honest nature was wasted on someone who treated trust as currency.

Duke Gwendolyn’s expression hardened, her diplomatic mask reasserting itself as she shook her head with practiced regret. “There is nothing you can offer me that would make me release him to you. He is a unique being that will benefit the Living-...!”

Before she could complete her justification, Noah raised his hand with casual certainty. On his palm, reality seemed to condense and crystallize, forming a single droplet that blazed with inner radiance.
A milky droplet of the Sacred Mead of Existence.
The moment it manifested, the garden itself seemed to inhale with desperate want. Every plant, every Wheel of Existence fruit, every mote of dust in the air suddenly oriented toward that single drop!

The vegetation grew more vibrant, colors deepening beyond their already impossible saturation. The crystalline pathways hummed with resonance, and even the golden dome overhead seemed to pulse with renewed vitality!

Duke Gwendolyn herself felt her existence buzz with unprecedented intensity. Every cell, every particle of her being suddenly understood that it was incomplete, that this single droplet contained something that could elevate her beyond current limitations. Her enhanced perception, refined through eons of advancement, could barely process the concentrated potential contained in that small amount of liquid.
She stood frozen, her ancient composure cracking as she looked ahead!
Noah’s voice cut through her shock with simple directness. “Release Titano, and you can have this.”
The offer hung between them like a contract written in starlight. A single drop of Sacred Mead of Existence for the freedom of one Mutated Living Existence.
The exchange rate was absurd as the Duke did not even know what it was! Nor that it was a drop amidst...thousands more that remained!

Duke Gwendolyn’s expression cycled through several complex emotions in rapid succession. Calculation warred with desire, propriety battled against pragmatism. For several seconds that felt like small eternities, she stood perfectly still, her mind racing through implications and possibilities.
Finally, she grit her teeth with the sound of stones grinding together and spoke the word that sealed the bargain.
“Okay!”
HUUM!
The concession erupted from her with more force than intended, her usual control cracking under the weight of what she was accepting.

“Titano is released from all debt to me and is now under your supervision.” She seemed to gather herself, majesty reasserting itself as she continued. “We are all on the same side anyway. Whether Titano is bound to you or me is inconsequential...if this is what you wish for, it is granted.”

Noah looked toward Duke Gwendolyn with even greater disappointment than before. The ease with which she had capitulated, the ready justifications that followed...they painted a picture of someone for whom everything was negotiable, everything had a price!
