chapters.title: Chapter 4012: Integrity! II
paragraphs: Noah flicked his finger with casual precision, sending the milky white-gold droplet through the air.

Duke Gwendolyn caught it with both hands, cradling it like she had received the most profound treasure imaginable. Her fingers trembled slightly as she secured it within her spatial storage, the action performed with the reverence typically reserved for religious artifacts.
When she looked back at Noah, her eyes blazed with newfound hunger that she didn’t even attempt to hide.

"If you have resources like this," she said, her voice carrying barely contained excitement, "you could give it to more Dukes and allow for the rapid increase in power across our entire structure. You could give even more to me."
She leaned forward slightly, her experience making her next words sound reasonable despite their audacity. "Apart from Titano, what else do you want? Anything can be exchanged."
Exchanged. Anything.
The words settled into Noah’s consciousness. Was that all Titano was to her? Something to be exchanged? A resource to be traded when better options presented themselves?
His dislike toward this Duke crystallized into something colder. His voice emerged with dangerous calm. "Anything can be exchanged, is that right?"
Duke Gwendolyn nodded seriously, missing the warning in his tone. "Yes, anything."

Noah’s eyes flashed with cold brilliance as another droplet materialized in his palm. The garden once again responded to its presence, reality itself leaning toward that concentrated potential. Duke Gwendolyn’s body actually trembled with barely suppressed need.
"Okay," Noah said, his voice carrying the weight of test and judgment combined. "Here is another drop. I will exchange this... for you to be on your knees when you receive it."
HUUM!
The words fell into the space between them.
A Duke. On her knees.
Her expression flashed with lividity, the calm diplomatic mask shattering as the full implications of his demand registered!
This was not about resources or power...this was about dignity, about the fundamental respect that her position commanded.
Noah remained cold, his gaze unwavering as he continued. "What? Is that not for exchange? I thought anything could be exchanged?"

Duke Gwendolyn’s glorious visage turned to ice. Her mind raced through what she represented, what she had achieved. Who was she? She was a Duke...one of the eighty-one who stood at the pinnacle of Living Origin hierarchy. She had Royal Living Origins under her command, multiple Honored Living Existences who would die at her word. She was power incarnate! She was accumulated wisdom! She was...!
"Kneel."
BOOM!
The single word carried more weight than entire speeches, more command than armies could enforce!
She looked toward Noah coldly, her expression cycling through emotions too complex for simple classification. Then she nodded, her voice emerging with bitter recognition.
"So this is your true self."
Without further hesitation, without dramatic pause, she took a decisive step forward and dropped to her knees.
A Duke...a being whose authority could reshape portions of existence itself...fell to her knees on the crystalline pathway of the garden.
The sight was wrong in ways that transcended simple power dynamics. This was hierarchy inverted, dignity discarded for gain!

Noah looked at her with even greater distaste as he tossed the droplet toward her kneeling form. She caught it with steady hands despite her position, her expression serious as she secured this second treasure.
As she remained on her knees, Noah’s voice emerged with the kind of measured intensity that commanded absolute attention.
"Out of everything a being can possess...power, wisdom, resources beyond measure...integrity is the one thing that should never be compromised." His words carried the weight of fundamental truth.
"Somewhere, in the vast expanse of our existence, everyone must have a line they will not cross. A boundary that defines not what they can do, but what they won’t do, regardless of the gain."
He paused, letting the words settle into her consciousness before continuing with increased intensity.

"You are such a detestable being that you would likely compromise your integrity for anything deemed sufficient. I could continue pushing you now, tell you to do obscene things...degrade yourself in ways that would haunt your consciousness for eons, and you would likely do them if it meant getting what you want."
His voice dropped to barely above a whisper, yet it carried perfectly through the garden’s stillness.
"You...have no integrity."

The condemnation rang through the space with the finality of judgment rendered. Duke Gwendolyn rose from her knees with mechanical precision, brushing off her robes with movements that seemed more habit than necessity.
She looked toward Noah with eyes that had shed any pretense of warmth, her voice emerging with cold certainty.

"You can call it integrity. I call it doing whatever is necessary to ensure survival and prosperity for the Living Origins." She straightened to her full height, authority radiating from her form despite what had just transpired.
"Because what did I lose just now by getting on my knees? My face? My pride? These are ephemeral concerns that matter only to those who value appearance over result."
Her voice grew stronger, more certain, as if she was convincing herself as much as him.

"I will put them aside every time. For her, for the Young Miss, I will put aside everything. For Order to be restored, for balance to return to existence, I will do everything." Her eyes blazed with terrible certainty. "I will give up everything."
Everything.
Once more, someone stood ready to give up their Everything for a cause they deemed greater than themselves.
The only question that remained was whether her Everything was worth anything at all.

As Noah gazed coldly at Duke Gwendolyn, feeling the weight of her absolute yet somehow hollow commitment, he found himself wondering about a more personal question: What was the worth of his own Everything?
In the Early Veiled Shore, as Noah contemplated the nature of worth and sacrifice across his many bodies, brilliance suddenly erupted near his primary form.
He turned to witness a sight that drew his attention completely...the Leviathan’s Eternum Cage had reached completion.

The structure defied conventional architecture, existing as something between temple and trap, between sanctuary and prison. Its walls rose from the golden sands in sweeping curves that seemed to follow mathematical principles that hadn’t been discovered yet.
The frame was composed of crystallized authority so pure it appeared to be carved from solid light, yet shadows danced within its depths, suggesting spaces that existed beyond normal dimensions.
Most remarkable were the waters that filled it...Early Sacred Waters that blazed with their own inner radiance!

The liquid was so clear that looking through it was like gazing through crystallized time, yet it pulsed with vitality that made ordinary water seem like dust by comparison. These waters seemed to breathe within the cage.
Prompts materialized before Noah’s vision at that moment.
|The Leviathan’s Eternum Cage has been completed|
Structural Integrity: Perfect
Dimensional Anchoring: Stable
Capacity: Can hold up to 10,000 Basic, 1,000 Refined, 100 Eminent, or 10 Kleos Early Living Marine Lifeforms simultaneously
Activation Requirements: Early Creature blood can be used as bait to attract Marine Lifeforms. Different blood quantities attract different grades:
1 drop: Basic Marine Lifeforms
10 drops: Refined Marine Lifeforms
100 drops: Eminent Marine Lifeforms across current Fold
1,000 drops: Kleos Marine Lifeforms across adjacent Folds
A glorious aquarium!
He looked at its brilliantly as it shone clesr blue and emanated waves of glory!
Without hesitation, Noah leaped into the Cage itself, his body cutting through the air with perfect grace before plunging into those impossible waters.
The sensation that followed defied description...it was like being embraced by liquid starlight, each molecule of water carrying within it the compressed essence of life itself.
He submerged completely, allowing the Early Sacred Waters to flow over and through him.
The liquid was welcoming him like a long-lost element returning to its proper place. He could feel it seeping into his pores, each drop carrying potential that would have overwhelmed lesser beings!
Another prompt appeared soon after.
|Your entry into the Leviathan’s Eternum Cage is recognized as supreme bait|
|Your aura as an Early Creature surpasses blood as attraction, but be careful|
|The Cage will now begin seeking Early Living Marine Lifeforms across dimensional boundaries|
|Estimated time to first capture: 3-7 minutes|
As if responding to the prompt’s declaration, brilliant golden lines erupted from the Cage’s crystalline frame.
They looked like fishing lines spun from captured sunlight, each one disappearing into the vibrant waves of the Shore with purpose that transcended simple hunting!
These lines were reaching across dimensions, through spaces that existed between spaces, hunting for creatures that most beings didn’t even know existed.

Noah floated in the sacred waters, feeling their vitality seeping into every fiber of his being. His eyes remained closed as he contemplated his Everything...what it meant, what it was worth, whether it could be measured against the Everything of others.
A new prompt suddenly blazed across his consciousness as he did so.
|Complexity Quotient has reached: 1,000,473,891|
|Purity Quotient has reached: 1,000,892,734|
|You have crossed the 1 Billion threshold|
|Current power classification: Equivalent to Prime Living Existence|

Duke Gwendolyn rose from her knees with mechanical precision, brushing off her robes with movements that seemed more habit than necessity.
She looked toward Noah with eyes that had shed any pretense of warmth, her voice emerging with cold certainty.
"You can call it integrity.

I call it doing whatever is necessary to ensure survival and prosperity for the Living Origins." She straightened to her full height, authority radiating from her form despite what had just transpired.
"Because what did I lose just now by getting on my knees?
My face?
My pride?
These are ephemeral concerns that matter only to those who value appearance over result."
Her voice grew stronger, more certain, as if she was convincing herself as much as him.
"I will put them aside every time.
For her, for the Young Miss, I will put aside everything.
For Order to be restored, for balance to return to existence, I will do everything." Her eyes blazed with terrible certainty.
"I will give up everything."
Everything.
Once more, someone stood ready to give up their Everything for a cause they deemed greater than themselves.
The only question that remained was whether her Everything was worth anything at all.

As Noah gazed coldly at Duke Gwendolyn, feeling the weight of her absolute yet somehow hollow commitment, he found himself wondering about a more personal question: What was the worth of his own Everything?
In the Early Veiled Shore, as Noah contemplated the nature of worth and sacrifice across his many bodies, brilliance suddenly erupted near his primary form.
He turned to witness a sight that drew his attention completely...the Leviathan’s Eternum Cage had reached completion.
The structure defied conventional architecture, existing as something between temple and trap, between sanctuary and prison.
Its walls rose from the golden sands in sweeping curves that seemed to follow mathematical principles that hadn’t been discovered yet.
The frame was composed of crystallized authority so pure it appeared to be carved from solid light, yet shadows danced within its depths, suggesting spaces that existed beyond normal dimensions.
Most remarkable were the waters that filled it...Early Sacred Waters that blazed with their own inner radiance!
The liquid was so clear that looking through it was like gazing through crystallized time, yet it pulsed with vitality that made ordinary water seem like dust by comparison.
These waters seemed to breathe within the cage.
Prompts materialized before Noah’s vision at that moment.
|The Leviathan’s Eternum Cage has been completed|
Structural Integrity: Perfect
Dimensional Anchoring: Stable
Capacity: Can hold up to 10,000 Basic, 1,000 Refined, 100 Eminent, or 10 Kleos Early Living Marine Lifeforms simultaneously
Activation Requirements: Early Creature blood can be used as bait to attract Marine Lifeforms.
Different blood quantities attract different grades:
1 drop: Basic Marine Lifeforms
10 drops: Refined Marine Lifeforms
100 drops: Eminent Marine Lifeforms across current Fold
1,000 drops: Kleos Marine Lifeforms across adjacent Folds
A glorious aquarium!
He looked at its brilliantly as it shone clesr blue and emanated waves of glory!
Without hesitation, Noah leaped into the Cage itself, his body cutting through the air with perfect grace before plunging into those impossible waters.
The sensation that followed defied description...it was like being embraced by liquid starlight, each molecule of water carrying within it the compressed essence of life itself.
He submerged completely, allowing the Early Sacred Waters to flow over and through him.
The liquid was welcoming him like a long-lost element returning to its proper place.
He could feel it seeping into his pores, each drop carrying potential that would have overwhelmed lesser beings!
Another prompt appeared soon after.
|Your entry into the Leviathan’s Eternum Cage is recognized as supreme bait|
|Your aura as an Early Creature surpasses blood as attraction, but be careful|
|The Cage will now begin seeking Early Living Marine Lifeforms across dimensional boundaries|
|Estimated time to first capture: 3-7 minutes|
As if responding to the prompt’s declaration, brilliant golden lines erupted from the Cage’s crystalline frame.
They looked like fishing lines spun from captured sunlight, each one disappearing into the vibrant waves of the Shore with purpose that transcended simple hunting!
These lines were reaching across dimensions, through spaces that existed between spaces, hunting for creatures that most beings didn’t even know existed.
Noah floated in the sacred waters, feeling their vitality seeping into every fiber of his being.
His eyes remained closed as he contemplated his Everything...what it meant, what it was worth, whether it could be measured against the Everything of others.
A new prompt suddenly blazed across his consciousness as he did so.
|Complexity Quotient has reached: 1,000,473,891|
|Purity Quotient has reached: 1,000,892,734|
|You have crossed the 1 Billion threshold|
|Current power classification: Equivalent to Prime Living Existence|

chapters.title: Chapter 4013: A Stick! I
paragraphs: He smiled calmly at this notification, the expression carrying satisfaction rather than surprise.

Just like that, within a single day, he had progressed from exceeding Originus Venerant to achieving power that matched Prime Living Existences. His progression was so gloriously fast that others would find it maddening to witness...eons of advancement compressed into hours.
But the resources he had, even with his ridiculous foundation that should have made his path slower...still meant he was faster than many could even imagine!

He drew in a deep breath, actually drinking the Early Sacred Waters that surrounded him, feeling them flow down his throat like liquid advancement itself. The sensation was intoxicating, each swallow adding to his ever-growing power.
"Since one billion has been reached," he said, his voice resonating through the waters with crystalline clarity, "let the first Kleos Glyph be formed!"
HUUM!
The declaration rang through the Early Veiled Shore with the weight of existential law being established.

His eyes blazed with brilliant anticipation as he recalled how Moiraine had formed her Kleos Glyphs...those ultimate expressions of power that contained both Origin and Paradox. She could achieve this because she existed as both states simultaneously, an Arch Living Existence that transcended normal categories.

But he was something far beyond even that. Within his existence, he contained aspects of all types of Living Existences, not just two or three, but all ten fundamental forces that shaped reality itself.
Barring one he had not yet attained as it had not bloomed fully within Sigrid.
"My first Glyph," he declared with terrible certainty, "shall incorporate all ten."
The words erupted from him with force that made the Early Veiled Shore itself pause!

His body began to vibrate with frequencies that shouldn’t exist. His completing Early Atlas trembled within his existence, its structures groaning under the strain of what he was attempting. Every Tower of Osmont resonated with vibration, their crystalline structures singing notes that had never been heard together. Glorious Hymns!

He was attempting something that should have been impossible...forming a Kleos Early Living Existential Glyph that incorporated Paradox, Origin, Dimensional, Elemental, Law, Spirit, Emotive, Concept, Temporal, and Quantum authorities simultaneously.

The process was immediately grueling. Reality itself seemed to rebel against the attempt, as if the fundamental forces he was trying to unite had never been meant to coexist within a single expression!
His body convulsed as contradictions tore through him...Origin and Paradox warring for dominance, Temporal and Quantum refusing to synchronize, Elemental and Concept finding no common ground.

With desperate certainty, Noah waved his hand and summoned the bucket containing all remaining Sacred Mead of Existence. Without hesitation, he upended it above his head, swallowing every drop that remained!
Magisterially!
Tyrannically!
Quintessentially!
|Sacred Mead of Existence Consumed: 3,847 drops|
|Warning: Consumption rate exceeds recommended parameters|
|Early Creature physiology adapting to extreme intake|
One by one, the prompts came.
And one by one, they continued!
|Your distinction as an Early Creature is the only factor enabling this attempt|
|Probability of success without Early Creature nature: 0.0000000001%|
|Current probability of success: 12.7%...|
|Sacred Totems, Realm, Nutrients from the Early Veiled Shore, Sacred Mead, and other facotrs are increasing the probability... 34.2%... 51.8%... 77.3%...|
DUM! DUM! DUM!
His body became a battlefield where fundamental forces waged war for dominance.
His skin cracked and reformed, each fissure leaking light of different colors...silver white for Law, gold white for Origin, obsidian gold for Paradox, crimson for Elemental!
The Early Sacred Waters around him began to boil from the energy being released, creating steam that itself carried enough authority to reshape lesser realities.
Throughout the Shore, his Sacred Totems began to resonate in response to his attempt.

Each tower blazed with its own light, their combined radiance creating pillars that stretched toward infinity. The lights converged above the Aquarium, forming something unprecedented...an archaic lighthouse that seemed to exist in all times simultaneously!
From this lighthouse, reality itself seemed to focus into a single point of impossible density.

Noah’s lesser Glyphs...all the Basic and Refined Early Living Existential Glyphs he had painstakingly formed began dissolving, their essence being drawn into the forming creation. They didn’t resist; they seemed to understand that they were becoming part of something greater.
|Basic Early Living Existential Glyphs Consumed|
|Refined Early Living Existential Glyphs Consumed|
|Kleos Glyph Formation: 94% complete|
The process reached a crescendo that made existence itself hold its breath. Then, with the sound of reality sighing and accepting something that shouldn’t exist, the Glyph completed its formation.
|Kleos Glyph Successfully Formed: The Creature’s First Lesson|
HUUM!
The Glyph that inscribed itself upon Noah’s forehead was unlike anything that had existed since the Earliest Folds!

It appeared as a circular pattern that somehow contained ten distinct yet unified symbols, each one representing a different type of Living Existence. They rotated around a central point that seemed to be simultaneously empty and containing everything...a paradox that Origin accepted, that Law defined, that Concept understood.
|The Creature’s First Lesson|
The first lesson THE Creature learned: All forces can be one force if properly understood
Primary Effect: Grants access to Early Creature’s Authority, the ability to treat all Living Existential Authorities as aspects of a single, unified force.
Secondary Effect: All attacks carry traces of all ten authorities, making immunity impossible.
Tertiary Effect: Can temporarily impose "lessons" upon reality, forcing it to accept contradictions.
Unique Feature: Grants access to a Goad, a tool of education and discipline.
Current Mastery: 0.1% (Increasing with complexity, purity, usage and understanding)
As the Glyph settled into its place upon his forehead, it pulsed with brilliant white-gold radiance.
He was not given any rest!
From within that light, something began to emerge...something that seemed almost insultingly simple given the magnitude of what had just occurred.
It was...
A stick.

It was perhaps three feet in length, carved from what appeared to be simple white wood. There were no ornate decorations, no obvious signs of power. It looked like something a shepherd might use to guide sheep, or a teacher might use to point at lessons written on air.
|From the newly formed Kleos Glyph, the Rearing Stick of the Early Creature, the Goad, has been obtained|
Noah grasped the simple stick, and immediately, information flooded his consciousness!

|The Goad - Rearing Stick of Existential Education|:: In the Earliest Folds, THE Creature used a tool similar to this to discipline Early Creatures and unruly Living Existences. Not through pain. Instead through understanding forcibly imparted.
Physical Properties: Appears as simple wood. Cannot be broken, burned, or destroyed by any force below Early Creature level.
Activation Requirement: Can only be wielded by one who possesses The Creature’s First Lesson Glyph.
Primary Function: Educational Discipline- a single tap forces the target to understand one fundamental truth about their nature
Secondary Function: Existential Correction- can temporarily "correct" flaws in a being’s existence.

Combat Rating: At current 1% access, can rear weak Honored Living Existences and entities of equivalent complexity. Each tap reduces their combat effectiveness by 10% as they are forced to confront truths about themselves.
Growth Potential: As complexity, purity, and mastery increases, can eventually discipline Duke-level entities and even other Early Creatures.
Warning: The truths revealed are always accurate but not always survivable. Some beings shatter when forced to truly understand themselves.
Noah held the simple stick, feeling its weight...not physical weight, but the weight of responsibility, of power that transcended simple destruction!
This was not a weapon in the traditional sense.
It was something far more terrifying: a tool that could force beings to confront the truth of their own existence.
In his hand, he held the power to educate existence itself.
And sometimes, education was the most terrifying force of all!

chapters.title: Chapter 4014: A Stick! II
paragraphs: The weight of the simple stick in Noah’s hands carried more significance than any weapon he had ever held.

It wasn’t its physical properties...the smooth white wood felt no different from any branch one might find beside a country road. It was the potential within it, the terrible authority to force understanding upon those who might prefer ignorance.
His contemplation was interrupted by a sudden surge of movement in the Leviathan’s Eternum Cage.
|Alert: Eminent Early Living Marine Lifeform Successfully Captured!|

|Species: Crimson-Eyed Depth Tyrant|:: Classification: Apex Predator of Abyssal Trenches. Threat Level: Can overwhelm standard Prime Living Existences. Nutritional Value: Equivalent to 127 Refined Marine Lifeforms.

One of the golden fishing lines suddenly went taut, its crystalline structure humming with strain as something massive fought against its pull. The line blazed brighter, reality bending around it as it hauled its catch across dimensional boundaries with inexorable force.
The Early Sacred Waters in the Cage began to churn, whirlpools forming as space itself was forced to accommodate what was being dragged through.
Then it breached.

The creature that erupted into the Cage was magnificence and terror combined. Its scales were obsidian plates that seemed to absorb light, each one inscribed with natural Glyphs that pulsed with Eminent authority!

Its body was serpentine yet muscled, suggesting both fluidity and devastating power. But it was the eyes that commanded attention...crimson orbs that burned with intelligence far exceeding what one expected from a "mere" Marine Lifeform.

The Crimson-Eyed Depth Tyrant took one look at Noah floating in its new prison and immediately recognized what he was. Not the specifics, perhaps, but the fundamental truth that here was something that existed at the apex of all food chains. Its response was instant and decisive...attack before being attacked, establish dominance before becoming prey.

It rushed toward him with speed that compressed the Sacred Waters into visible shock waves, its maw opening to reveal rows of teeth that existed in several dimensions simultaneously. Hundreds of Refined and Eminent Glyphs blazed along its form, each one adding layers of authority to its assault!

Noah blinked at the approaching devastation with the calm of someone watching a particularly aggressive puppy charge. His hand tightened slightly on the Goad, and he made a simple motion...a casual swipe through the water, the kind of gesture one might use to brush away a fly.
PAH!

The sound that resulted shouldn’t have been possible underwater, yet it rang with crystalline clarity. The stick connected with the Tyrant’s scales with force that had nothing to do with physical impact. Its accumulated authority, those hundreds of Glyphs that should have made it nearly invulnerable, simply... didn’t matter!
They might as well have been decorative paintings for all the protection they provided.
The Marine Lifeform’s charge reversed instantly, its massive form driven backward through the water with such force that it created a temporary vacuum.
But more than the physical repulsion, it was the expression in those crimson eyes that told the true story. Shock gave way to horror, horror transformed into primal fear.
Because in that moment of contact, the Goad had done what it was designed to do...it had educated.
Above the trembling creature’s head, words materialized in the water itself, visible only to it and Noah.

|Truth of Existence Revealed: You exist to become nourishment for an Early Creature. Your entire evolutionary line, millions of years of development, all led to this moment where you would provide sustenance to one who stands above the food chain itself. This is not tragedy...this is purpose fulfilled.|
HUUM!

The Tyrant’s trembling intensified as this fundamental truth settled into its consciousness. It had always known it was predator, had defined itself by what it consumed. To suddenly understand that it had always been prey, just prey for something so far above it that the concept hadn’t existed in its limited worldview... the revelation was shattering.

Noah observed its fearful form with something approaching sympathy. He beckoned toward it with his free hand, a simple gesture that somehow carried more command than any roar or threat could have achieved.

The Marine Lifeform approached with the tentative movements of something that had just learned its place in existence. When it reached him, Noah patted its massive head with genuine fondness, his laughter echoing through the Sacred Waters.
"Don’t look so terrified," he said, though he knew it couldn’t understand his words, only his intent. "Purpose fulfilled is better than purpose unknown."
The Rearing Stick hummed in his hand with satisfaction at a lesson properly delivered. This tool... it needed to be used more. The possibilities were intoxicating!

Noah launched himself from the Cage with a powerful stroke, his body breaking through the surface in a spray of Sacred Water that caught the glorious light of the Shore like liquid diamonds. He landed on the golden sands with practiced grace, water running from his form in streams that seemed reluctant to leave his presence.

Moiraine approached immediately, her expression carrying that mixture of deference and determination that had become her signature. "Sir," she said, her voice steady despite what she was about to reveal, "here are those I defeated before things turned crazy."

With a wave of her hand, space distorted to release her stored prizes. Six corpses materialized on the golden sands...the Dead Existences she had systematically destroyed during the chaos in the Temporal Folds. Each one radiated residual wrongness, their forms caught between states of being even in death.
But what happened next drew Noah’s complete attention.
The Kleos Glyphs adorning Moiraine’s body...those ultimate expressions of power that she had painstakingly formed, began to crack. Not from damage or degradation, instead from deliberate sacrifice!
One by one, they shattered like crystalline sculptures struck by hammers of pure will, their essence condensing into something far more precious.
Light erupted from each breaking Glyph. The fragments condensed, compressed, and transformed into perfect shards that blazed with potential beyond normal classification.
|Ten Kleos Glyphs of Paradoxical Genesis have been sacrificed|
|Ten Shards of the Seed of the Lost Forgotten Principle: The Principle of Existential Duality have been created|
|Current Shard Count: 11/100|

Moiraine gathered the shards with reverent care, each one pulsing with the compressed essence of what she had given up. She offered them to Noah with both hands, her eyes meeting his with unwavering certainty.

"Sir," she said, and the way she spoke that single word carried more meaning than entire speeches might convey. It was acknowledgment and devotion, respect and something deeper that defied simple classification. "For you, I will continue to form more and sacrifice."
The earnestness in her expression, the absolute certainty with which she offered up power that others would kill to possess... it was something else entirely.
Her ’Sirs’ were intoxicating!
Noah looked at her devoted figure as his eyes burned brightly. He leaned closer, his voice dropping to a whisper meant only for her. "I really need to find a place of privacy for the two of us..."
A whisper.
Yet before he could complete the thought, reality responded to his barely voiced desire.
|Construction Option Available: Early Abode of the Early Creature|
|Resource Requirements: Option 1: 500 Drops of Early Creature Blood. Option 2: Nutrients from currently processing corpses.|
|Note: Construction requires manual assembly. Materials and building blocks will be provided, but the Abode must be built by hand to properly attune to its creator’s essence.|

But what happened next drew Noah’s complete attention.
The Kleos Glyphs adorning Moiraine’s body...those ultimate expressions of power that she had painstakingly formed, began to crack.
Not from damage or degradation, instead from deliberate sacrifice!
One by one, they shattered like crystalline sculptures struck by hammers of pure will, their essence condensing into something far more precious.
Light erupted from each breaking Glyph.
The fragments condensed, compressed, and transformed into perfect shards that blazed with potential beyond normal classification.
|Ten Kleos Glyphs of Paradoxical Genesis have been sacrificed|
|Ten Shards of the Seed of the Lost Forgotten Principle: The Principle of Existential Duality have been created|
|Current Shard Count: 11/100|
Moiraine gathered the shards with reverent care, each one pulsing with the compressed essence of what she had given up.
She offered them to Noah with both hands, her eyes meeting his with unwavering certainty.
"Sir," she said, and the way she spoke that single word carried more meaning than entire speeches might convey.
It was acknowledgment and devotion, respect and something deeper that defied simple classification.
"For you, I will continue to form more and sacrifice."
The earnestness in her expression, the absolute certainty with which she offered up power that others would kill to possess... it was something else entirely.
Her ’Sirs’ were intoxicating!
Noah looked at her devoted figure as his eyes burned brightly.
He leaned closer, his voice dropping to a whisper meant only for her.
"I really need to find a place of privacy for the two of us..."
A whisper.
Yet before he could complete the thought, reality responded to his barely voiced desire.
|Construction Option Available: Early Abode of the Early Creature|
|Resource Requirements: Option 1: 500 Drops of Early Creature Blood.
Option 2: Nutrients from currently processing corpses.|
|Note: Construction requires manual assembly.
Materials and building blocks will be provided, but the Abode must be built by hand to properly attune to its creator’s essence.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4015: A Stick! III
paragraphs: Noah’s eyes lit up with interest as he considered the possibilities. An abode...a private space within his Shore where certain activities could occur without observation.
Yes, this was necessary!
He looked down at the six corpses of Honored Dead Existences that Moiraine had provided, his mind already calculating distributions. "Evaluate and devour," he commanded the Shore itself.
The response was immediate:
|Six Honored Dead Existence Corpses Evaluated|
|Total Nutritional Value: Equivalent to 1500 Eminent Early Living Marine Lifeforms|
|Distribution Parameters Set: 35% to Moiraine for Kleos Glyph formation, 25% to Early Abode construction materials, 40% to personal advancement|
|Distribution Commencing...|

The golden sands beneath the corpses began to shift and churn, drawing them down with the patient hunger of something that knew how to savor its meals. As they disappeared, Noah turned his attention to the broader Shore.
"Henry! Kazuhiko! Emperor Penguin! Liora!..." His voice carried across the expanded territory with crystalline clarity. "Come here and help me build something..."

The named individuals emerged from their meditative positions, their bodies still buzzing with the complexity and purity they had been absorbing. Henry’s features had taken on an almost crystalline quality, while Kazuhiko’s hand rested on a katana that now hummed with barely contained authority.

The Emperor Penguin waddled forward with dignity that transcended his somewhat ridiculous form, and Liora moved with the fluid grace of someone whose connection to primal forces had deepened, her eyes filled with purpose as she thought of her father!
They converged toward the center of the Early Veiled Shore, where something unprecedented was beginning to manifest.

Stone-like materials began to materialize from thin air, emerging gradually like thoughts becoming solid. Each block was unique yet clearly part of a greater whole, inscribed with patterns that suggested function beyond mere structure.
"We can always use more people," Noah mused, his gaze turning toward the mist that marked the Shore’s boundaries.

As if responding to his unvoiced invitation, the mist began to part, revealing something like a doorway...a threshold between the Shore and the greater Infiniverse that contained it. The first figure to emerge made Noah simultaneously smile and question his decision.

The Queen of Matter burst through the opening in an explosion of enthusiasm that seemed to reshape reality around her presence. Her white dress was adorned with jewels that weren’t merely decorative...each one was a crystallized concept, a thought given form.
Books and grimoires orbited her form in complex patterns, their pages fluttering with winds that carried whispers of Fables.
"I HAVE BEEN MADE RELEVANT AGAIN!" she screamed with joy that could have powered small civilizations.

Her eyes locked onto Noah with the intensity of someone viewing their personal idol. "Sir! Thank you for putting me in the main story once more! Even though I was having ridiculous fun observing the transforming Infiniverse Wheel of Existence...did you know how crazy its becoming?!"
She spun in place, taking in the Early Veiled Shore with eyes that seemed to catalogue every impossible detail simultaneously.
"By the way," she continued without pause for breath, "do you know what-...oh my word, is that an aquarium?!"
Noah shook his head with exasperation, wondering if bringing her here was brilliant or catastrophic.

Behind the Queen of Matter, more figures began to emerge through the doorway. Dr. Hall stepped through with his white coat. Erikson followed, his massive frame having to duck through the opening. Ayame, Romulus, the Great Beyonder, the Great Mother, Lilith...and dozens of other beings who had been part of his journey but had faded into the background as powers escalated beyond their ability to participate.
Now they entered the Early Veiled Shore with expressions of wonder that reminded Noah why he had brought them. They deserved to be part of this, to witness and participate in the glory!
"Everyone," he called out, his voice carrying warm authority, "energize yourselves by drinking droplets of the Early Sacred Water from the shores, then come help build an Abode."

The assembled beings nodded with various expressions of amazement. The Queen of Matter, predictably, was the first to act. She bounded toward the crystalline waters with the enthusiasm of someone who had just been offered unlimited access to a library of forbidden knowledge. She cupped the Sacred Water in her hands, drinking deeply, and the transformation was immediate...her entire form began to pulse with newfound vitality.

She returned with her mouth still full of Sacred Water, her cheeks puffed out like a chipmunk’s as she tried to speak around the liquid. Her eyes were wide with excitement, practically vibrating with readiness for whatever came next.
Noah reached out and ruffled her hair with genuine affection. "Let’s get started."
As his primary body organized construction in the Early Veiled Shore, another version of himself navigated the twisted passages of the Doorway to the Loom in the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds.

The crimson obsidian halls stretched in different directions, their surfaces reflecting possibilities rather than images. In a relatively stable pocket of space, Noah faced the massive form of Titano.
"I have something to show you," he said, raising his hand to project an illusory scene into the air between them.

The memory played out with perfect clarity...Duke Gwendolyn in her garden, her voice carrying that diplomatic certainty as she spoke the words: "Titano is released from all debt to me and is now under your supervision."

Altheon and Thessaly watched the projection with expressions of shock that bordered on horror. Their enhanced perceptions were calculating furiously, trying to determine what Noah could possibly have offered to make Duke Gwendolyn release such a valuable asset.
The Duke never gave up anything without receiving something of greater value in return...it was fundamental to her nature.
Titano watched the scene with eyes that dimmed noticeably. His massive frame seemed to shrink slightly, the hurt visible in every line of his simple, honest face!
He had genuinely believed Duke Gwendolyn cared about him beyond his utility, that their relationship transcended mere debt and service!
After several long seconds of silence, he looked at Noah with those dimmed eyes and asked, "Does this mean Titano is okay to come work under Brother?"

Noah shook his head firmly, reaching up to pat the giant’s massive arm. "You won’t work under me. You’re my brother, right? We’ll simply move together, and as your Older Brother, I’ll help you out and make you rich just like me."
The transformation in Titano’s expression was immediate and complete. Joy erupted across his features like sunrise over mountains.
"Brother!" he boomed, sweeping Noah up in a bear hug that would have crushed anyone below Honored Living Existence level to paste.
Noah’s body creaked audibly under the embrace, his enhanced durability the only thing preventing immediate structural failure.
When Titano finally released him, the giant’s expression had shifted to thoughtful confusion.
"Brother," he said with unexpected seriousness, "I might be older than you, though?"

Noah waved his hands with equal seriousness, his expression suggesting this was a matter of grave importance. "Being richer and more experienced makes me older. Age is not just time, Brother. It’s about wisdom, wealth, and the ability to provide guidance."

Titano’s eyes widened as if he had just received profound enlightenment. He nodded slowly, filing this information away with the same care he applied to all of Noah’s teachings. "Titano understands! Brother Noah is older because Brother Noah is richer!"

chapters.title: Chapter 4016: A Stick! IV
paragraphs: Off to the side, Sigrid smiled and shook her head at the exchange between Noah and Titano.
Yet her amusement faded as her thoughts turned to Duke Gwendolyn and her recent actions. The betrayal of trust, the casual trading of loyalties...it left a bitter taste that wouldn’t fade.
Her contemplation was shattered by a sound that made reality itself step back in recognition.
"ROAAAAR!"

The bellow echoed through the winding halls with force that created visible distortions in the paradoxical space. But more terrifying than the volume was how that single voice immediately multiplied, becoming five distinct roars that harmonized into something that challenged sanity itself.
The aura that followed made the air thick with wrongness...five Inevitabilities, each one radiating power equivalent to an Honored Living Existence, were rushing toward their position.

Thessaly and Altheon immediately shifted into combat readiness, their accumulated authority beginning to manifest. Titano cracked his knuckles with sounds like mountains breaking, his expression brightening with anticipation.
"Brother," he said cheerfully, "I will take care of these and gift them to you as well!"
But Noah raised his hand in a stopping gesture. "No... let me try these ones."

The silence that followed was deafening. Even Sigrid turned to look at him with barely concealed concern. She opened her mouth as if to question his decision, then closed it with visible effort. He was an Early Creature...he could probably do things that defied comprehension. She had to trust that.
Titano, however, had no such restraint. He blinked his massive eyes and said with blunt honesty, "Brother, you have no muscles like Titano and your figure is scrawny. Will you be okay?"

Noah turned to face the giant with an expression of patient instruction. "Brother, sometimes those who are truly rich can look scrawny, but they could buy a weapon that makes them more powerful than anyone else. And what I will use today is a truly terrifying weapon."
As he spoke, something materialized in his hand.
A stick.
Just... a stick.

The Rearing Stick of the Early Creature, the Goad, appeared with no fanfare, no blazing light, no reality-warping presence. To everyone watching, it looked like Noah had just summoned a piece of white wood, the kind of thing one might use to poke a campfire.
Yet Noah carried it forward with the bearing of a knight carrying a legendary blade!

He stepped ahead of Titano, Sigrid, and the others, positioning himself as the vanguard against the approaching horror. The image was simultaneously glorious and absurd...a man with a stick preparing to face five Inevitabilities.
They emerged from the twisted space like nightmares given form and purpose:
|One Inevitability turned to Five Inevitabilities Detected: The Writhing Paradox of Unending Reach|
|Classification: Each entity possesses power equivalent to Honored Living Existence|
|Form: Roiling masses of tentacles that exist in multiple states simultaneously|
|Warning: Paradoxical nature allows them to be everywhere and nowhere until observed|

The creatures that approached defied rational observation. They were masses of tentacles, but the tentacles weren’t quite physical...they existed in states of possibility until the moment they chose to strike. Each one possessed thousands of writhing appendages that phased in and out of reality, their surfaces inscribed with paradoxes that blazed!
Noah moved forward with his stick raised, and the battle that followed would be carved into the memories of all who witnessed it.

The first Inevitability struck with tentacles that existed in seventeen different possible positions simultaneously. Normal defense would have been impossible...how could one block an attack that came from every direction including some that didn’t exist?
But the Goad didn’t operate according to normal principles.
PAH!

Noah’s stick swept through the air with casual precision, and somehow, impossibly, it connected with all seventeen possibilities at once. The tentacles recoiled with visible shock, their paradoxical nature momentarily forced into a single, painful reality.
|The Goad’s Authority is forcing a singular truth upon paradoxical existence|

The second and third Inevitabilities attacked in coordination, their tentacles weaving through space in patterns that created tears in causality itself. Noah’s body, despite his enhanced capabilities, simply wasn’t fast enough to dodge everything. Several tentacles struck him, their touch carrying paradoxes that should have unmade him at the conceptual level.
Should have.
|Passive Defense Activated: The Kleos Glyph of the Creature’s First Lesson shines brightly.|
|Paradoxical attacks recognized and rejected. Your existence refuses to acknowledge contradictions.|
HUUUM!
The Kleos Glyph on his forehead blazed with white-gold light, and the paradoxes simply... didn’t take.
They struck his form and dissolved, their contradictions unable to take root in someone who carried the unified authority of all ten Living Existences in the form of a single glyph!
A single...Glyph!
Noah pressed forward, his stick moving in patterns that looked almost casual but carried devastating purpose. Each strike forced understanding upon the Inevitabilities.
PAH! - "You exist because you shouldn’t, but that’s not strength, it’s confusion"
PAH! - "Your paradoxes are questions, not answers"
PAH! - "You fear definition because definition would reveal your emptiness"

The fourth and fifth Inevitabilities tried to overwhelm him through sheer mass, thousands of tentacles converging from every possible angle. Noah’s defensive capabilities were tested to their limits...he took hits that sent him flying, tentacles that wrapped around his limbs, attacks that would have torn apart Prime Living Existences and injured weak Honored Ones!
But he endured because a single Kleos Glyph shone again and again. And more than endured...he educated.

His stick never stopped moving, each contact delivering truths that the Inevitabilities couldn’t reject or ignore. The battle wasn’t about physical dominance but about forcing these paradoxical beings to confront the fundamental nature of their existence.
The observers watched in shocked silence as Noah, armed with nothing but a stick, systematically broke down five Honored-level threats!

Altheon’s ancient eyes were wide with disbelief. Thessaly had actually stopped hovering, her fairy form dropping to the ground in shock. Sigrid watched with a mixture of awe and something deeper...a recognition that she was witnessing something unprecedented.

But it was Titano’s reaction that was most profound. The giant watched his scrawny brother beat cosmic horrors with a stick, and his simple mind reached a profound conclusion: being rich meant having the best tools!
The battle reached its climax as all five Inevitabilities, educated beyond their ability to maintain paradoxical existence, collapsed into quivering masses.
They didn’t die...death would have been mercy. Instead, they lay there, tentacles twitching weakly, trembling from the beating delivered by a simple stick.

Noah floated above them grandly, the Goad still held in his hand like a teacher’s pointer after a particularly effective lesson. He had given his first true combat lesson, and the Inevitabilities had been thoroughly educated.
The silence that followed was broken only by the weak whimpering of existential horrors that had just learned truths they would have preferred to remain ignorant of.
Noah looked down at them with satisfaction. The Rearing Stick had proven its worth beyond question. And this was only at one percent of its true power!
He couldn’t help but wonder...what would happen when he could access more!

The effect was instantaneous and devastating.
BOOM!
Titano’s massive figure, which had weathered attacks from beings of incomprehensible power, began to tremble.

His arm, thick as an ancient tree trunk, started to buckle. The simple stick seemed to carry the weight of concepts themselves...truth, education, understanding, all compressed into three feet of white wood with traces of gold!

The giant’s knees began to bend, his entire frame being forced downward as if existence itself was pressing upon him. The crimson obsidian floor beneath them began to crack under the transferred pressure, reality struggling to accommodate weight that transcended physical measurement.

Before Titano’s body could be driven completely into the floor, Noah made a beckoning gesture. The Goad responded immediately, floating from the giant’s trembling palm back to its rightful owner’s hand with the casual ease of returning home.
Titano remained on one knee, his massive chest heaving with exertion, eyes wide with a mixture of shock and respect. Noah looked at him with understanding rather than mockery.

"Some weights," Noah said, "only a select few can bear. Not because of strength or will, but because of the nature of what they are. The Goad doesn’t test your muscles, Brother...it tests your capacity to carry the responsibility of forcing truth upon others. Oh, and you need a certain Tattoo for it!"
Titano nodded slowly, processing this lesson with the same care he applied to all of Noah’s teachings. Noah reached out to pat the giant’s shoulder with genuine affection.
"Don’t beat yourself up over it. Your strength lies elsewhere, and that’s perfectly fine."
The lovable titan’s expression brightened immediately at the reassurance, his simple nature not allowing disappointment to linger.
Noah felt the weight of the stick in his hands...not physical weight, instead, the weight of purpose, of potential consequences.
His gaze shifted, moving past Titano to settle on the two figures who had been observing from what they considered a safe distance.
Both Thessaly and Altheon instantly shuddered.

When Noah’s focus moved past Thessaly to lock onto Altheon specifically, the fairy-like being released a breath she didn’t realize she’d been holding. Relief flooded through her tiny form so intensely that she actually dropped several inches in altitude before catching herself.

Meanwhile, Altheon felt his entire existence begin to tremble. The sensation started in his core and radiated outward, every particle of his being recognizing that it was under scrutiny from something that could unmake it with casual indifference.
"What?" he managed to say, the word emerging as barely more than a hesitant whisper.
Noah’s eyes sharpened to points that could have cut through dimensional barriers. His voice, when it came, carried the weight of judgment already rendered!

"You did something a while ago that you may not even remember or consider consequential." Each word was delivered with precision that made them impossible to misunderstand. "I was going to kill you for it, but I will discipline you instead, so... come here."
HUUM!
The silence that followed was deafening.
Altheon’s luminous form actually paled, his ancient features cycling through confusion and growing dread. "What? I didn’t..."

His protests died as his gaze fell upon the simple stick that had just thoroughly thrashed five Inevitabilities. The fear that crawled up his spine was primal, instinctive, the kind that bypassed rational thought entirely!
Desperately, he looked toward Sigrid, seeking intervention from someone who might carry influence.

She met his gaze with calm indifference, her expression making it clear that this was not her concern. His attention shifted to Thessaly, but she had already turned away, her tiny form trembling with shame and fear, unwilling to involve herself in whatever justice was about to be dispensed.
She almost wanted to reassure Altheon that she could potentially bring him back incase he was killed...but she couldn’t bring herself to say anything!
Noah’s frown deepened at the delay. "Would you rather I kill you than discipline you?"

The question hung in the air. After a moment that stretched toward eternity, Altheon gritted his teeth and floated forward. Each movement felt like swimming through crystallized dread, his enhanced perception calculating thousands of escape possibilities while his wisdom told him none would succeed.
When he stopped before Noah, the Prime Living Origin looked like someone approaching their own funeral.
Noah raised the Goad with ceremonial precision. "This is for your education," he said, though he offered no explanation of what crime warranted this punishment.
The first strike came with deceptive gentleness.
PAH!
The sound rang through the paradoxical space, and Altheon’s scream followed immediately.
It wasn’t the physical impact...his body could withstand forces that would shatter Wheels of Existence. It was the Truth that accompanied it!
|You are a coward who attacks those weaker when you think there will be no consequences|
The second strike followed before he could process the first.
PAH!
|Your accumulated wisdom means nothing when you act on base impulses|

Altheon’s cries grew more desperate. This wasn’t pain that his Living Origin Authority could heal. This was fundamental truth being carved into his existence, each revelation more devastating than physical destruction could ever be!
PAH!
|You justify your actions with authority, but authority without integrity is merely sophisticated barbarism.|
The Prime Living Origin, who had existed for eons, who had witnessed the rise and fall of countless civilizations, was reduced to sobbing!

chapters.title: Chapter 4018: A Stick! VI
paragraphs: Red marks appeared across his luminous form...not wounds, but evidence of education forcibly imparted. They seemed to exist outside his body’s natural regeneration, as if the lessons they represented were too important to be healed away.
PAH!
|You will remember this moment every time you consider acting without honor.|
By the end, Altheon gazed at Noah and the stick with the kind of fear typically reserved for forces of nature!
He understood now, with terrible clarity, that this simple tool could do something far worse than kill him...it could make him understand himself!

Noah nodded with satisfaction, lowering the Goad. He didn’t mention that Altheon’s crime had been attempting to kill one of his bodies days ago. The lesson had been delivered; the specifics were irrelevant.
"Pick him up until he recovers," he said to Thessaly, his tone brooking no argument.

The Honored Living Existence nodded frantically, her wings fluttering as she approached Altheon’s trembling form. She stared at the red marks covering his body with horrified fascination. They defied every law of regeneration she understood. Would they even heal? Or would they remain as permanent reminders of education forcibly received?

With that matter settled, Noah moved to stand beside Sigrid, taking her hand with gentle certainty. Her fingers intertwined with his without hesitation, though her expression carried questions she wouldn’t voice in present company.
"Let’s see what else is in this place" he said, his stern demeanor softening into something warmer. "Afterwards, I need to bring you to my place. My home."
Behind them, Titano’s enthusiasm returned full force, apparently unaffected by witnessing Altheon’s discipline. "Will Titano get to visit as well???"
Noah glanced back with a genuine smile. "Of course, Brother. And I’ll make sure to prepare a feast."
The giant’s eyes lit up with joy that could have powered Wheels.

With renewed purpose, they delved deeper into the twisted passages of the Doorway to the Loom, leaving behind a thoroughly educated Prime Living Origin and a fairy who would think very carefully before crossing Noah!
In another Doorway entirely, past a bronze tear that had opened due to the resonance of ancient authorities, Alexander Asmodeus stepped into a realm that time had forgotten.

The Desiccated Sleeping Shore stretched before them like the graveyard of dreams. The sands, which should have been golden, were ash-gray, as if all color had been leached away by eons of abandonment. The sky above held no sun, no stars, only a uniform grayness that seemed to press down with the weight of forgetting.

Hundreds of dead trees dotted the landscape, their branches reaching toward nothing, their bark preserved in death like monuments to what had once been. Ancient structures rose from the sands...abodes and towers that looked as if they had been beautiful once, before time and desertion had worn them down to skeletal remains.

Royal Law Tristesse approached one of the structures with professional curiosity, reaching out to test its integrity. Her hand, wreathed in Law Authority that could reshape reality, met the worn stone. Nothing happened. She pressed harder, her power flaring. The structure didn’t even acknowledge her attempt!
"Indestructible," she murmured with genuine surprise. "Whatever force preserves this place transcends current understanding."

Alexander moved deeper into the Shore, drawn by instincts he didn’t fully understand. His Enneagram, the nine-pointed star on his chest, began to spin with increasing speed. As he neared certain areas, debris that looked like nothing more than dust and fragments suddenly animated, flying toward him as if magnetized.

A piece of what might have been pottery. A fragment of crystallized wood. Each item was absorbed directly into his Enneagram, disappearing into whatever space existed within that geometric impossibility.
The same phenomenon occurred with Seraphina, her own Enneagram drawing different fragments, as if each piece knew exactly where it belonged.

They continued deeper, past collapsed buildings that might have been homes, past dried fountains that might have once held Sacred Waters. The desolation was complete, yet somehow budding with possibility.
Then, as Alexander’s Enneagram absorbed what looked like the hand of an ancient clock, dust cascaded from above as a dirty gray cloth slid off a torn wall.
What was revealed made Seraphina scream, stumbling backward in fear!
A head.

Massive, bisected, yet somehow preserved in perfect, horrible detail. The eyes still burned with rage that had transcended death, frozen in eternal fury. The mouth gaped open in a scream that had lasted eons, teeth visible like monuments to violence.
It was an Early Creature!

This was all that remained of an Early Creature in its own Shore...a head that radiated such terrible presence that even in death, even bisected and abandoned, it made their hearts fill with dread that transcended rational fear.
Alexander maintained his composure through will alone, though sweat beaded on his forehead as he gazed upon this testament to ancient catastrophe.
Their Enneagrams blazed simultaneously, and prompts appeared.

|Synchronized Enneagram Activation Possible. While connected, the holders of the Enneagram fragments can induce a memory replay within the preserved consciousness of the Early Creature. This memory will reveal the locations of the Early Tool fragments of THE Living Law.|
|Connection Requirement: Physical and energetic synchronization between Enneagram holders.|
Alexander’s expression grew heavy as the implications settled. Seraphina’s eyes opened wide, understanding exactly what "connected" meant in this context.
She peeked over at Alexander to see his expression!
Alexander... couldn’t help but remember Noah’s words in Aeternitas Concordia. His gaze grew even more clouded as he looked at Seraphina, whose expression mixed embarrassment with something deeper.
Something...had to be done as too much was at stake!
In the Transcendent Spiritual Folds, existence took on properties that had more to do with thought than substance.

The Great Usurper floated without determined form, his consciousness spread across multiple probability states as he let the currents of Living Spiritual Authority carry him where they would. The sights were marvelous...thoughts given architecture, emotions crystallized into landscapes, concepts that had learned to dream.
He hummed contentedly, the sound reverberating through dimensions of pure consciousness.
With casual interest, he pulled up his Idle Gaming System interface, noting the golden glow on the [Transcendent Spiritual Folds Living Existential Dungeon] icon.
Time to collect his idle rewards!
Golden brilliance erupted around him as the system processed his accumulated gains.
|Idle Loot Obtained!|

[+10 Prime Living Spirit Shards (Collect 100 to summon a Prime Living Spirit Idle Soldier)], [+1 Honored Living Spirit Shard (Collect 100 to summon an Honored Living Spirit Idle King)], [+20 Living Existence Upgrade Crystals], [+5 Bottles of Liquified Consciousness], [+3 Memory Palace Blueprints], [+1 Seed of the Primordial Spirit Tree], [+1 Trillion Idle EXP]

The Great Usurper examined each reward with great interest, but it was the seed that truly captured his attention. He pulled it from his system space, the object materializing as something between light and thought.

[Seed of the Primordial Spirit Tree] :: A seed that predates the division between consciousness and substance. When planted in appropriate soil, will grow into a tree that produces Spirit Fruits. Each fruit grants permanent increase Living Existential Authority, 100,000,000 in Complexity and Purity, and entrance into a unique state of mind.
Planting Requirements: Soil blessed by an Early Creature, watered with Sacred Waters, tended by one who understands the nature of divided existence
Growth Time: 1,000 years (acceleratable through specific methods)
The Great Usurper appreciated the seed’s potential, but shook his head with wry amusement. He didn’t have what it took to plant such a thing. Who in existence did? Early Creature? What even was that?
He thought for a bit.
Then memory struck like lightning.
Osmont.
That ridiculously overpowered being who had once mentioned, almost as an afterthought, that when everything was over and done, he actually wanted to be a farmer.

The Great Usurper laughed, the sound rippling through spiritual dimensions. Had Osmont ever worked toward that dream? Could the man who seemed capable of anything actually be somewhere, tending to crops as a mere farmer?
Maybe he would be able to utilize this seed.
After all, what was more fitting than a farmer receiving seeds that could reshape existence itself?

chapters.title: Chapter 4019: Farmers of Existence! I
paragraphs: In the time when existence still questioned its own validity, when the boundaries between possible and impossible remained undrawn, there lived a Fold Dweller who possessed nothing of what would later be considered power.
No Living Existential Authority flowed through his veins. No Glyphs adorned his form. He was, by every measure that would come to matter, insignificant.
Yet he possessed eyes that saw.
Not metaphorically, not spiritually, but literally...eyes that perceived what should have been imperceptible, that noticed what preferred to remain unnoticed.
It was these eyes that allowed him to witness something that should have been impossible... THE Living Spirit, moving through the Earliest Folds like thought given purpose.

THE Living Spirit paused in its journey, its form...if form it could be called, rippling with surprise that transcended simple emotion. To be observed by a Fold Dweller, a being without even the smallest spark of authority...

"Due to your unique eyes that allow you to see," THE Living Spirit said, its voice carrying the weight of consciousness acknowledging consciousness, "I will answer any questions you have about existence."

The Fold Dweller gazed upon this manifestation of spiritual authority with reverence that bordered on worship. When he spoke, his question carried the desperate hope of every being that had ever felt inadequate in the face of infinity.

"In existence, how can one become more complex the easiest way?" His words tumbled forth with barely contained urgency. "If Fold Dwellers are not Living Existences and do not become one, any step towards complexity is arduous and long. How can they advance? How can they compare?"
THE Living Spirit regarded him with attention that seemed to pierce through to fundamental truths. When it responded, each word carried philosophical weight that would echo through epochs.
"Existence never decided that Living Existences or Early Creatures would be the fastest to progress in complexity or purity." The statement hung in the air like a revelation.
"Lifeforms themselves can decide that. If things feel hard, if progress feels slow... then one simply is not following the right path for their specific lifeform."
The Fold Dweller’s expression showed he remained unconvinced, his mortal mind struggling to grasp concepts that transcended mortality. "Then which methods can I use to become stronger faster?"

THE Living Spirit’s form shifted, as if considering how to translate infinite understanding into finite words. "You could be a farmer of existence itself...nurture wonders to grow, then consume those wonders for their accumulated complexity. You could devour the Everything of all others, taking their potential into yourself. Or..." it paused, the silence buzzing with possibility, "you can simply learn a Principle."
Confusion bloomed across the Fold Dweller’s features. "What is...a Principle?"

THE Living Spirit’s attention seemed to intensify, as if this question was both expected and profound. "If you knew that answer, you would never again worry about power. To truly understand a Principle, one must learn it from one of THE Living Existences. One must learn it from the Folds as they are right now." Its form rippled with something that might have been warning. "If ever the Principles are to be Lost or Forgotten... gaining any grasp on them will be an impossibility."
The weight of this revelation drove the Fold Dweller to his knees. His voice cracked with desperate hope as he pleaded, "Please, teach me. Show me the way to Principles, to power, to significance!"
THE Living Spirit observed his prostrated form with something that transcended sympathy yet fell short of mercy. "It is never so easy. Existence... is never so easy, nor so giving."
HUUM!
And with that pronouncement, THE Living Spirit vanished, leaving behind not even a whisper of its presence.

He rose from his knees with newfound determination burning in those unique eyes.

At that moment.

He tugged on the entanglement with the Great Usurper!

chapters.title: Chapter 4020: Farmers of Existence! II
paragraphs: The entanglement between existences stretched like a silver thread across impossible distances, and Noah pulled upon it with certainty.
Reality rippled around his form as something transcendent passed through the connection!

The Seed materialized in his palm with weight that transcended physical measurement. It pulsed with potential that made even the Early Veiled Shore pulse, the golden sands beneath his feet shifting in anticipation!
A message followed through the connection, the Great Usurper’s voice echoing out.

|I’ll continue paying the debt of the Seed of Existence you gave me, slowly, every now and then. I’ll send over farming-related stuff so you can work toward that dream of being a farmer. Who knows? Maybe you’ll actually achieve it.|

Noah smiled at the words, not questioning how Eckert had acquired a Seed with such profound origins. Existence was vast, and everyone had their opportunities. He didn’t go around telling Eckert or Alexander about becoming an Early Creature or possessing an Early Veiled Shore...of course others would have their own chances at transcendence, their own paths to power that defied conventional understanding.

He moved across the Shore with purpose, the Seed cradled in his hands like a newborn star. The cultivation plots stretched before him in neat rows, some already showing signs of the impossible herbs beginning to sprout. He selected an empty plot near the center, where the concentration of nutrients in the soil were vibrant!
Kneeling, he pressed the Seed into the golden sand with reverence that transcended simple planting. This was more than agriculture!
"Utilize the nutrients from currently devoured lifeforms," he commanded the Shore itself. "Accelerate its maturity."
The response was immediate.

|Seed of the Primordial Spirit Tree Planted. Acceleration Options Available. Natural Growth: 1,000 years. With Current Nutrient Infusion: 1 day. With 100 Drops of Early Creature Blood: 12 hours. With 1,000 Drops of Early Creature Blood: 1 hour. Select acceleration method|
Noah didn’t hesitate. Time was a resource, but blood...blood he could produce. The rapid explosion of complexity that would follow the tree’s maturation was worth any cost.

"One hour," he declared, watching as his skin split along carefully chosen lines. Deliberate openings through which his precious blood could flow. Each drop that fell onto the soil around the Seed was worth more than entire Wheelss, containing within it the compressed essence of an Early Creature’s existence!
The thousand drops fell like crimson rain, each one absorbed instantly by soil that had been waiting eons for such nourishment. The effect was immediate and magnificent.
HUUM!

The Seed cracked with a sound like reality accepting a new truth. A shoot emerged, pale as moonlight, growing with speed that made time itself seem uncertain. The farm-like atmosphere of the Shore intensified as the shoot became a sapling, the sapling stretched toward a sky that didn’t exist, its trunk thickening with each passing second.
Starlight seemed to shimmer along its bark...generated from within, as if the tree itself was a constellation that had chosen to take root.

Branches spread with precision, each one reaching toward different aspects of existence. Leaves unfurled that were simultaneously silver and gold, their surfaces inscribed with patterns that suggested thoughts becoming real.
Noah watched with satisfaction as his newest addition to the Shore established itself, when prompts suddenly cascaded before his vision!
|The Queen of Matter has successfully completed assigned task. Heidrun has been successfully tended and milked|
|Sacred Mead of Existence Obtained: 15,000 Drops. Efficiency Rating: Unprecedented.|
|Heidrun’s Comment: "Acceptable enthusiasm. Questionable technique. Overall satisfactory."|

His eyes blazed with interest as he turned to see the Queen of Matter approaching with a golden bucket that seemed too heavy for reality itself to properly support. She carried it with both hands, her entire body vibrating with pride at her accomplishment. The white-gold liquid within sloshed gently, each tiny wave containing enough power to elevate common beings to transcendence.
"Sir!" she exclaimed, her voice carrying the particular pitch of someone who had just achieved something they’d been told was impossible.

"I did it! Heidrun even said I was satisfactory! That’s basically a glowing recommendation from her!" She presented the bucket with ceremony that would have been excessive if not for what it contained.
"Please give me as many more jobs and tasks here so that I do not fall back to irrelevancy again!"

The desperation in that last statement was real...the Queen of Matter’s greatest fear had always been becoming a background character in her own existence. Noah reached out and ruffled her hair as he smiled lightly.
"You’re on the right path," he assured her. "Keep it up."

With a gesture, he drew the bucket into his spatial storage, the Sacred Mead joining his growing collection of impossible resources once more. "Let’s go finish the Abode first. There’s still work to be done."

The Shore buzzed with activity as construction resumed. Many plots of herbs would soon mature, the nine original trees would bear their first fruits, and now the tenth tree, the Primordial Spirit Tree...added its own unique presence to the agricultural miracle he was creating.
Stone by stone, block by block, the Abode took shape!
The construction was both mundane and transcendent...physical materials being assembled through manual labor, yet each piece carrying significance that transcended simple architecture.
As all of this occured...the Shore itself continued to move as if it were alive as the Aquarium in thr distance churned!
|Eminent Early Living Marine Lifeform Captured. Species: Void-Touched Leviathan Spawn. Successfully contained in Leviathan’s Eternum Cage.|

Noah glanced toward the Aquarium to witness the new arrival...a creature that seemed to exist in negative space, its form defined more by what wasn’t there than what was. It thrashed once against its containment before recognizing the futility and settling into sullen acceptance.
The Crimson-Eyed Depth Tyrant, his first capture, actually shifted away from the newcomer with visible wariness.
He returned his attention to the construction, where Emperor Penguin was waddling forward with the final building block...a keystone that would complete the entire structure!
The penguin’s expression radiated pride that seemed excessive for its small form, its flippers raised triumphantly as it placed the stone with ceremonial precision.

The moment the keystone settled into place, brilliant light erupted across the Early Veiled Shore. Not the harsh light of explosion, instead the warm radiance of something coming into perfect alignment with its purpose.
The Abode of the Early Creature was completed, and its details rose up before his eyes!
