chapters.title: Chapter 4021: Farmers of Existence! III
paragraphs: |Construction Complete: Abode of the Early Creature|
|Classification: Transcendent Dwelling|
|Spatial Parameters: External dimensions 100x100x100 meters. Internal dimensions equivalent to Minor Miniature Fold.|
|Primary Features:|

-Temporal Flux Chamber: Time flows independently from external reality. Stasis to acceleration possible but currently uncontrolled. Days or years may pass within while seconds pass outside, but never the other way around.
-Access Limitation: Early Creature plus 18 designated beings maximum simultaneous occupancy
- Pocket Dimensions: 99 separate spatial pockets, each with unique environmental properties
-Regenerative Architecture: Structure repairs itself using ambient existence
- Authority Suppression Field: All violence impossible within primary areas
-Meditation Amplification Zones: Complexity and Purity absorption increased by 300%
-Private Chambers: Specially attuned spaces that adjust to occupant preferences
It was glorious!

The Abode stood before them like something that had always existed but had only now chosen to manifest. Its exterior was carved from what appeared to be single piece of stone that had witnessed the birth and death of Folds. The surface wasn’t smooth but covered in intricate patterns that seemed to tell stories through images and through texture itself.

Archaic symbols that predated language spiraled up its walls, each one pulsing with faint light that synchronized with the breathing of the Shore itself. The entrance wasn’t a door but a swirling gateway of multicolored light, simultaneously inviting and warning that crossing its threshold meant entering something beyond normal existence.
Noah nodded with satisfaction as another prompt materialized.
|Participation Reward Activated. All beings who assisted in construction have earned the right to ascend any Sacred Totem within the Shore. Ringing the bell with personal Hymn grants Epiphany State.|
|Effect: 100,000% increase to Complexity and Purity absorption for 10 minutes. This opportunity is single-use per participant.|

The assembled helpers...Noah’s people who had labored to create this wonder, stared at the notification with expressions ranging from disbelief to overwhelming joy. Henry’s visage cracked a smile. Kazuhiko’s hand trembled on his sword hilt. Even Erikson, usually stoic, showed visible emotion.

Noah addressed them all, his voice carrying across the Shore with perfect clarity. "The Early Veiled Shore is vast and filled with opportunities. Tend to the plots and help with farming. Water the trees. Drink the Early Sacred Waters in moderation to not lose yourselves. Fight against Marine Lifeforms when you become powerful enough."

He paused, ensuring every word was understood. "Through this Shore, you can become unfathomably powerful in a short period of time. Outside of all this are the endless Folds of Existence with countless other lifeforms. Once you’re powerful enough, you can always venture out to experience what it means to face Fold Dwellers and Living Existences."

His people listened with bright eyes, understanding dawning that they had been given not just power, but purpose. They began to scatter across the Shore with newfound determination, some heading toward the Totems, others to the cultivation plots, each finding their own path to transcendence.

Noah took a moment to observe everything he had built. His gaze traveled to the distant seated figures of Ruination and the Infiniverse, both having crossed the hundred-million marker in their Complexity and Purity Quotients. They had held off on forming more Glyphs, waiting to form Kleos Glyphs like him. The potential they represented made his eyes shine with anticipation!
"Little Fish, can we go see inside?"

The small voice drew his attention downward. Barbatos had appeared beside him, her crimson eyes shining with excitement as she hugged his hand and gazed at the Abode. Her dark hair framed a face that managed to be both ancient and vibrant simultaneously.
Adelaide, Athena, Anna, and others approached from various directions, their expressions mixing curiosity with something else. Noah smiled warmly at the gathering!
"I’ll give you all a tour."
He looked toward where Moiraine sat in meditation, her form radiating the particular stillness of someone reconstructing their power. "You too, Moiraine. Come."
The procession that followed was almost ceremonial...Noah surrounded by these women who had become integral to his existence in ways that transcended simple companionship.
They approached the swirling gateway with mixed expressions of anticipation.
The moment they stepped through, reality reorganized itself around them.

They emerged into a stellar-lit hall that defied every assumption about interior space. The floor was marble shot through with starlight, extending for what appeared to be light-years in every direction. The ceiling...if it could be called that, was existence itself turned transparent, showing the dance of concepts and forces that most beings would never perceive.

Multiple ancient-locked archways floated throughout the space, each one carved from different impossible materials. Some were positioned on the floor, others hung in mid-air at angles that challenged three-dimensional thinking, and still others seemed to phase in and out of visibility.
Each doorway led to a different pocket dimension, a different reality with its own rules and wonders.
All of this existed inside a single Abode.
Barbatos’s eyes lit up with delight that could have powered stars. She tugged on Noah’s hand with surprising strength, pulling him toward an archway that gleamed with obsidian radiance.
"Little Fish, I want to see in here!"

As she pulled him forward, Noah’s body seamlessly divided...one version going with Barbatos while another remained with the group. The division was so smooth that reality didn’t even notice it had been cheated.

Adelaide shook her head with fond exasperation, her vibrant snow-blue hair catching the stellar light in ways that created small auroras around her head. She looked around, performing a quick headcount of all the women present, then fixed Noah with a calm smile.
"Make a few more bodies and give everyone the same treatment," she said, her tone perfectly pleasant yet taking no argument.
"You’ve been busily getting more complex and haven’t given us any time recently."
The words ended with sharp authority, and Noah nodded with a smile as he replied. "Yes, Ma’am."
HUUM!

Multiple versions of himself materialized without fanfare, each one moving to a different member of his harem. Gentle hands found waists, fingers intertwined with fingers, and each woman found herself being led toward a different doorway, a different pocket dimension where privacy and possibility intertwined.
The logistics of it should have been impossible...maintaining multiple fully conscious bodies, each providing genuine attention! But Noah had transcended such limitations long ago.
Finally, only Moiraine remained, looking at him with bright eyes that held depths of understanding.
"Sir...has quite an appetite," she observed, her tone carrying amusement rather than judgment.

Fight against Marine Lifeforms when you become powerful enough."

chapters.title: Chapter 4022: Farmers of Existence! IV
paragraphs: Noah nodded seriously. "Existence has many boons that everyone fights for. In the middle of all of it, if one has the chance to enjoy the simple things and doesn’t... they have the biggest losses. And I do not like losses when I have treasures all around me."
He extended his hand toward her. "Come. I need to see if Dual Cultivation still has stupendous results."
Her eyes blazed brighter as she took his hand without hesitation. "Yes, Sir."
Noah and Moiraine disappeared into another pocket dimension where time itself flowed according to different rules, where moments could stretch into eternities or compress into heartbeats!
Outside the Abode, another of Noah’s bodies remained seated on the golden sands, observing the Shore with satisfaction.
The Emperor Penguin’s indignant voice carried across the space as it complained to Kazuhiko and Erikson.
"I would have also liked a tour of the Abode we built..."
Kazuhiko, already holding Erikson’s slipper with practiced ease, delivered a light smack to the back of the penguin’s head. "No, no you would not, you flightless bird."
"Hey!" The Emperor Penguin’s authority flared white gold as it charged at Kazuhiko with tiny legs pumping furiously.
Noah smiled at these scenes of normalcy amidst transcendence.
Even as terrifying weavings of craziness unfolded outside.
Even as the Kleos Concordat would take place within a day as all Living Existences met.
The Early Veiled Shore remained its own isolated place with its glorious wonders that could make one forget about everything else!
As he had such thoughts.
Without warning, his seated form began to shine.
HUUM!

Brilliance erupted from his body, ancient and profound. His shirtless form revealed skin that had taken on an archaic quality, fair yet somehow containing depths that eyes couldn’t properly perceive. Taut muscles shifted beneath that skin with each breath, each movement revealing perfect control over a form that had transcended normal physicality.

The Kleos Glyph of the Creature’s First Lesson blazed upon his forehead, its ten-fold pattern rotating slowly as if contemplating truths. In his hand, the Goad rested with deceptive simplicity...just a stick, yet one that had educated Inevitabilities about their own existence.
But it was what was happening within that truly mattered. His Heart of an Early Creature pulsed with increasing intensity, sending waves of power through his entire being!
HUUUM!
And his Atlas...that internal map where all his Towers of Osmont grew like impossible trees, suddenly erupted with shocking radiance.
|Monumental Achievement: Early Atlas of the Folds - Complete|
|+500,000,000 Complexity Quotient. +500,000,000 Purity Quotient.|
WAA!

The surge of power was staggering. His body experienced waves of enhancement that would have destroyed lesser beings, each cell drinking in the advancement like desert sand accepting rain. This was why the Atlas had taken so long to complete...it wasn’t just mapping current existence, but something far more profound!
|Early Atlas of the Folds|
|Primary Function: Map and Pathway to the Earliest Folds|

|The Atlas has connected itself to the primordial core of what defines an Early Creature, then exceeded that foundation by incorporating your Quintessential and Tyrannical nature. It serves as a map, and as a bridge between what was, what is, and what might be.|
|Core Ability: Temporal Traversal|
- For limited duration, traverse into the Earliest Folds themselves
- Warning: Cannot control destination point
- Warning: Cannot remain indefinitely, extended stay results in permanent temporal displacement
-Each traversal establishes a Node on the Atlas for potential return
-Current Safe Duration: 1 hour
- Cooldown: 1 day
|Supplementary Functions:|
-Fold Memory: Can replay events from any visited location in the Earliest Folds
-Existential Compass: Always know your position relative to your origin point
-Temporal Anchor: The Towers of Osmont serve as lighthouses, each advancement extending safe duration
-Reality Recognition: Immune to temporal paradoxes during traversal
-Node Network: As Nodes accumulate, can begin to predict destination points.
|Growth Parameters|
-Atlas complexity increases through exploration
-Tower advancement extends traversal duration (Each stage = +unknown number of seconds)
-Heart completion reduces cooldown
-At full development: $@%% %#$%& in Earliest Folds becomes possible.
|Unique Synergy: The Tyrannical Navigator|
-Your nature as Tyrannical Emperor allows forcing favorable destinations
-Current Success Rate: 0.1%
-Increases with each successful traversal
|Unique Synergy: The Quintessential Mapper|
-Your nature as Quintessential Emperor allows recording of Earliest Fold resources
-Can identify and mark locations of Lost Forgotten Principles
-Current Detection Range: 1 light year around traversal point
Sheesh!
Noah felt the weight of this new capability settling into his existence!

The ability to visit the Earliest Folds even for mere seconds was unprecedented! That was where THE Creature had walked, where the THE Living Existences had been, where Principles existed before they became Lost or Forgotten.
The opportunities were staggering! The dangers were incomprehensible!
The Loot...ah!
Noah, seated on the golden sands of his Shore with multiple bodies experiencing transcendent wonders in pocket dimensions while others built and farmed and grew, smiled.
Because this was what it meant to be an Early Creature in truth....to be Him, Noah Osmont!
Not just power...but the ability to touch the very foundations of existence itself and do thr impossible.
Because what the fuck was even this capability?!
The Early Atlas of the Folds pulsed within him like a second heart, ready to guide him into the deep past where everything had begun.
Ready to help him understand what even Living Existences might have forgotten!
Noah observed the shocking functions of the Early Atlas of the Folds again and again, his enhanced perception parsing through the information. Each reading confirmed what seemed utterly impossible.
A one-day cooldown between uses, and a whole hour of exploration.
In such an hour, a terrifying number of things could be done. A terrifying number of things could be accomplished.

The silence stretched as Noah felt himself standing at a grand precipice of possibility and achievement. The weight of what he was about to attempt pressed against his consciousness like the attention of existence itself. He breathed out slowly, each exhalation carrying away doubt, leaving only determination.
"Use the Early Atlas of the Folds."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4023: Farmers of Existence! V
paragraphs: The words emerged with quiet certainty, and reality immediately responded.
|CRITICAL TRAVERSAL INITIATING|
|Extreme Caution Required|
|Failure Parameters:|
-If return does not occur within 1 hour: Complete destruction of traversing body and all associated weavings
-If death occurs during traversal: Risk of cascade failure affecting all bodies
-Certain deaths may result in complete existential extinction
|Proceed? This action cannot be undone|
Noah didn’t hesitate. His confirmation rang through his being with the certainty of someone who had already calculated the risks and found them acceptable!

His entire existence began to buzz with frequencies that shouldn’t exist. The sensation started in his core and radiated outward, each particle of his being vibrating in harmony with something ancient and profound. The Early Atlas within him blazed with light that existed before light had been defined.
Then, without warning...
WAP!

His body seated on the shores folded in on itself like reality accepting that it had been cheated. The space where he had been sitting showed no evidence of his presence, as if existence itself had forgotten he had been there!
|Transference to random point in the Earliest Folds has begun|
|Duration of traversal: Indeterminate. Destination: Unknown. Probability of survival: Calculating...|
|Calculation completed. Probability of survival...is best left unknown.|
Existence was unfathomably unique.
Across its infinite expanse, countless abilities had been formed, discarded, and utilized since the first moment something wondered if it should be rather than wasn’t.

Some were as small as conjuring fireballs...brief expressions of will that barely disturbed the fabric of reality. Others transcended comprehension entirely, achieving the impossible through sheer audacity of conception!
Among these impossibilities, perhaps none was more audacious than forming a map that connected to the Earliest Folds themselves.
To countless years and events in the far distant past, when the foundations of everything were still being laid, when THE Creature walked freely and THE Living Existences were young.

Noah felt his existence trembling as it was stretched across temporal distances that had no measurement. He was being pulled through time itself, toward a when that existed perpendicular to normal causality!
His being threatened to spread too thin, to dissolve into the spaces between moments.

The Rearing Stick materialized in his grip without conscious thought, its simple presence providing an anchor of stability. The Goad hummed with recognition, as if it remembered the path they were taking. Simultaneously, the Kleos Glyph on his forehead, the Creature’s First Lesson, blazed with light that helped hold his consciousness together.
His Towers of Osmont, made from his glorious True Sources, lit up the way for him to see!

Years and seconds passed simultaneously. He experienced the weight of eons in heartbeats, felt instants stretch into eternities. His perception fragmented and reformed countless times, each reconstruction slightly different from the last.
|Existential Integrity: 94%... 87%... 76%...|
|Stabilizing factors detected:|
-Goad recognition: +11% stability
-Kleos Glyph resonance: +30% stability
-Early Creature nature: +50% stability
|Final Integrity: 91%. Traversal viable. Your existence, though feeble by Earliest Fold standards, possesses sufficient confluence of factors for survival.|
HUUM!

After what seemed like forever and no time at all, Noah felt his existence warping and twisting through dimensions that had no names. Reality bent around him like water around a stone, then suddenly...
WAP!
He arrived.
BOOM!
He truly arrived!

The moment his feet touched whatever served as ground in this place, his existence erupted with sensation. Every cell in his body, every atom of his being, began drinking in something he had never known existed...a richness of authority that made everything he had experienced before seem like shadows of shadows.
|Location Reached: Unknown Point - The Earliest Folds. Temporal Coordinate: Unknown Years Before Present.|
|Environmental Analysis|
-Atmosphere contains Raw Early Existential Authority
-Passive absorption rate: 100,000 CQ/PQ per second
-Warning: Prolonged exposure may cause fundamental changes to existence
|Timer Started: 59:59 remaining|
Noah gasped as the very air filled his lungs with power. Not refined, not processed, but raw potential that existed before it had been divided into categories like Origin or Paradox!
This was the fundamental substance from which all authority would eventually derive.
And just being here...increased his Complexity and Purity by 100,000 per second!
Oh!
He looked around with eyes that struggled to process what they were seeing.

The landscape defied every assumption about what reality should look like. Countless green-gold reed plants floated vertically in space that might have been air or might have been thought. Each reed extended for light-years...he could somehow perceive their full length despite the impossibility of such vision. They shimmered with complexity so profound that looking at them directly caused his nascent understanding of existence to reorganize itself.

The sky was a swirling mixture of colors that hadn’t been invented yet, concepts that were still being debated. Mountains floated inverted in the distance, their peaks pointing toward depths that had no bottom. Rivers of what might have been time itself flowed upward, carrying fragments of events that would happen or had happened or were happening now.
Everything was more real than reality had any right to be!
Noah approached one of the floating reeds with careful reverence, his hand extending toward its surface. The moment his fingers made contact, information flooded his consciousness.

|Primordial Complexity Reed- One of the infinite reeds that grew when existence first wondered about growth. Bark contains compressed potential from before potential was defined. Those able to breach the bark will find sap containing 10,000,000 Complexity and Purity.

Noah’s astonishment was complete. A single reed contained what would take most beings eons to accumulate. And there were countless reeds stretching in every direction, a forest of impossible advancement just waiting to be harvested!

He pressed his hands against the bark, feeling its resistance. It was hard...conceptually. It resisted being opened the way reality resisted being changed. His enhanced strength meant nothing here. This required something more fundamental.

The Kleos Glyph on his forehead blazed with brilliant light as he called upon the Creature’s First Lesson. The authority of all ten Living Existence types flowed through him simultaneously, and finally...finally, the bark cracked.

Vibrant gold sap was revealed within, glowing with inner light that predated stars. Without hesitation, Noah cupped his hands and drank directly from the source. The explosion of sensation in his mouth transcended taste...it was like drinking liquified possibility itself.
|Primordial Complexity Reed Sap Consumed. Base Gain: +10,000,000 Complexity Quotient. Base Gain: +10,000,000 Purity Quotient. Unique Gain due to your unique nature bonus: +2,500,000 to each|

Mountains floated inverted in the distance, their peaks pointing toward depths that had no bottom.
Rivers of what might have been time itself flowed upward, carrying fragments of events that would happen or had happened or were happening now.
Everything was more real than reality had any right to be!
Noah approached one of the floating reeds with careful reverence, his hand extending toward its surface.
The moment his fingers made contact, information flooded his consciousness.
|Primordial Complexity Reed- One of the infinite reeds that grew when existence first wondered about growth.
Bark contains compressed potential from before potential was defined.
Those able to breach the bark will find sap containing 10,000,000 Complexity and Purity.
Noah’s astonishment was complete.
A single reed contained what would take most beings eons to accumulate.
And there were countless reeds stretching in every direction, a forest of impossible advancement just waiting to be harvested!
He pressed his hands against the bark, feeling its resistance.
It was hard...conceptually.
It resisted being opened the way reality resisted being changed.
His enhanced strength meant nothing here.
This required something more fundamental.
The Kleos Glyph on his forehead blazed with brilliant light as he called upon the Creature’s First Lesson.
The authority of all ten Living Existence types flowed through him simultaneously, and finally...finally, the bark cracked.
Vibrant gold sap was revealed within, glowing with inner light that predated stars.
Without hesitation, Noah cupped his hands and drank directly from the source.
The explosion of sensation in his mouth transcended taste...it was like drinking liquified possibility itself.
|Primordial Complexity Reed Sap Consumed.
Base Gain: +10,000,000 Complexity Quotient.
Base Gain: +10,000,000 Purity Quotient.
Unique Gain due to your unique nature bonus: +2,500,000 to each|

chapters.title: Chapter 4024: Farmers of Existence! VI
paragraphs: As Noah marveled at this wonder, feeling power coursing through him that would have taken normal beings multiple lifetimes to achieve...
BOOM!
A terrifying aura erupted behind him with force that made reality step back in acknowledgment. Noah spun to face the source, his enhanced perception immediately observing what stood before him.

The being was titanic in scale, humanoid in general shape but wrong in every specific. Its skin was bark-like but moved like flesh, inscribed with patterns that predated written Runes. Its eyes held depths of immensity!
Massive hands ended in fingers that could have carved mountains or cradled newborn thoughts with equal ease.

Most shocking was what it wasn’t...this was not a Living Existence. Noah’s enhanced perception confirmed it carried only the aura of a Fold Dweller with no Living Existential Authority, yet its power dwarfed any Duke he had encountered!
The being’s expression was grave as stones that had witnessed the death of Folds.
"Fool! What are you doing here alone when the mad Early Creature is still hunting around these parts?! Come on!"

Before Noah could respond, before he could process the implications of ’mad Early Creature’ or formulate questions, the titanic being’s hand closed around him with force that transcended physical or conceptual resistance!

The being’s grip contained authority that Noah couldn’t begin to counter because it was far too old! Authority accumulated not through advancement but through sheer survival in an era when survival itself was an achievement.

"I said COME ON!" the being roared, already moving with speed that compressed space around them. "The last fool who lingered near the Reeds got turned into a meal crushed between the teeth of an Early Creature!"
Noah found himself being carried like a child through a landscape that shifted and changed with each massive stride the being took. His timer showed [58:43] remaining.

The titanic being’s pace increased, its fear palpable despite its overwhelming power. Whatever Esrly Creature were running from, it was something that even natives of the Earliest Folds didn’t want to encounter!
Noah gripped the Goad tighter, feeling its weight shift in his hand as he thought of all thr possibilities- one of the major goals being...not to die here!
The Fold Dweller crossed through existence with strides that compressed reality around them, each step covering distances that had no proper measurement.
The sensation was like being dragged through water that was also fire that was also thought itself.
Seconds stretched and compressed simultaneously, and then...
They crossed a threshold.

The transition was immediate and absolute, like stepping from chaos into order, from possibility into definition. Noah felt barriers close behind them....barriers that were conceptual boundaries that declared this space separate from the madness beyond!

The titanic being released him with visible relief, its bark-flesh form sagging slightly as tension drained away. It breathed out...a sound like wind through forests that had never existed, and looked Noah up and down with eyes that held eons of assessment.
"You look a bit weaker than most," it observed, not unkindly but with the matter-of-fact tone of someone stating that water was wet. "Though I suppose that’s better than the last one I found..."
The being straightened, gesturing to the space around them with one massive hand. "I’ve brought you to the Folds of the Esteemed First Farmer, the One Who Gazed Upon THE Living Spirit."
The title rang through the space with weight that made reality pulse.
Prompts flashed before Noah right after!
|Location Identified: The Primordial Agricultural Sanctum. Owner- Viltharion the Principle Cultivator, The One Who Gazed Upon THE Living Spirit|
|Era: The Earliest Folds - Period of Initial Cultivation. Population: 731 Fold Dwellers. Warning: You are the weakest entity present by a factor of 1,000.|
|Time Remaining: 57:50|
Noah’s astonishment was complete as he took in his surroundings.

The reeds were still present, those light-year-long plants floating vertically through space, but here they had been organized. They grew in neat rows that suggested someone had imposed agricultural order on cosmic chaos.
Between them floated farming plots that defied comprehension...each one the size of an omniverse, perfect squares of cultivated existence that hummed with careful attention.

Stellar trees rose from these plots, their trunks composed of compressed starlight, their branches reaching into dimensions that hadn’t been named yet. Their leaves were concepts given form...each one containing a different aspect of what growth meant, what cultivation could become.

Hundreds of Fold Dwellers moved through this impossible farm with serious purpose. None possessed Living Existential Authority in the traditional sense, yet each one radiated power that would make current-era beings weep with inadequacy.

The weakest among them carried might equivalent to Honored Living Existences, their power accumulated by existing so long that existence itself had to acknowledge their significance as they were drenched in...Early Existential Authority!
Dozens more carried power that matched or exceeded Dukes.
The atmosphere was one of focused industry mixed with profound respect.

The Fold Dweller who had saved him shifted, its massive form creating small earthquakes with the movement. "I am Threnvar, Keeper of the Eighth Perimeter. You will stay in the secure areas until the threat of the mad Early Creature is taken care of."

Threnvar’s expression grew grimmer, if such a thing was possible on features carved from living bark. "The creature has been hunting for a while now. It seems to have developed a taste for complexity itself...not beings who possess it, but the abstract concept. Every time it feeds, something becomes simpler. Last week, it ate the concept of ’maybe’ from an entire region. Now everything there either is or isn’t, with no space between."

Threnvar looked at him again, its ancient eyes showing something that might have been pity. "With how weak you are, you should reinforce yourself immediately. Why don’t you have some Existential Dew Fruits?"

The being pointed with one massive finger toward a distant plot that blazed with white brilliance. "Go to the Seventh Contemplation Grove. Harvest as needed...but only what you can consume. The Farmer does not approve of waste."
Noah nodded seriously, offering a nod to the being who had saved him. "Thank you for your assistance."
"Don’t thank me yet," Threnvar rumbled. "If the mad one finds us here, we’re all equally doomed. Gratitude can wait for survival."

chapters.title: Chapter 4025: Do Nothing! I
paragraphs: Noah made his way toward the indicated plot, his movement careful and deliberate. He was acutely aware of being observed with the kind of attention given to children who had wandered into an adult workspace. The other Fold Dwellers didn’t stop their work, but he could feel their ancient gazes tracking his progress.
The Seventh Contemplation Grove rose before him like a monument to impossible agriculture.

The trees here were different from the stellar giants elsewhere...more refined, more purposeful. Their trunks were white as fresh paper, inscribed with patterns that might have been words if words had been invented yet.

Fruits hung from their branches like condensed thoughts. Each one was perfectly spherical, about the size of his fist, and contained within their translucent skin swirled galaxies of compressed potential.
Noah reached out to touch one, and information flooded his consciousness.

|Existential Dew Fruit|:: Cultivated with singular purpose by Viltharion the Principle Cultivator. Grown from seeds of contemplation after witnessing THE Living Spirit. Each fruit represents one meditation on the nature of Principles and how one could possibly grasp one. Consumption Effect: +5,000,000. Complexity Quotient Consumption Effect: +5,000,000 Purity Quotient
Special Effect: Increases perception and sensitivity to Principles by 10%*
Special Effect: May trigger epiphany regarding Principles
Note: These fruits are the result of a Fold Dweller who sought to plant Principles themselves after discussing existence with THE Living Spirit

Noah’s hand pulsed slightly as he plucked the fruit. It came away from the branch with a sound like a perfectly resolved musical note. The weight in his palm was negligible physically but profound conceptually...he was holding the crystallized meditation of someone who had spoken directly with THE Living Spirit!
He bit into it without hesitation.

The taste was indescribable as it was simple in a way that nothing in modern existence could achieve. It tasted like the moment before decision, like the space between heartbeats, like the pause before understanding dawns.
It was fucking glorious!
|Existential Dew Fruit Consumed|
|Complexity Quotient increased by 5,000,000. Purity Quotient increased by 5,000,000|
|Principle Perception increased by 10%| |You can now faintly sense the presence of Lost Forgotten Principles within 10 meters.|
|There are...0 Principles for sensed by your senses.|
HUUM!

The surge of advancement was smoother than what he had experienced from the reed sap...more refined, more purposeful. But it was the secondary effect that truly mattered. Noah could feel something shifting in his perception, as if a veil he hadn’t known existed was beginning to thin.
He looked at the tree before him with new understanding.
Another fruit found its way into his hand. Then another.
He began to eat as if he were a voracious wildling of an entity as each fruit...was 5 Million to Complexity and Purity!
|Timer: 55:48 remaining|
As Noah consumed his fourth fruit, feeling his complexity soar beyond anything he could have achieved in years of normal cultivation, a shadow fell across the grove.
The shadow that fell across the grove turned out to be something slightly new.
A curious Fold Dweller stood before him, her presence commanding attention through sheer physicality rather than any display of power.
She was burly, humanoid in general form but crowned with the head of a wolf.
Gray fur, streaked with silver that might have been age or might have been wisdom, covered her lupine features.
Her eyes, amber gold and ancient, regarded Noah with particular intensity.

"You are such a weak thing," she observed, her voice carrying a growl beneath words that somehow made them more genuine rather than threatening. "Yet you seem to be the least worried being here while others prepare for potential death."

It was true. All around them, Fold Dwellers who had existed since before time had proper measurement were taking defensive positions, their ancient faces showing fear. Yet Noah stood calmly, still holding his fourth fruit, juice running down his chin from where he’d bitten into it.
He swallowed the piece he’d been chewing, feeling the surge of complexity flow through him before responding. His voice emerged steady.

"Worrying," he said, meeting those amber eyes without flinching, "is the act of suffering twice. Once in imagination, once in reality...if the feared thing even comes to pass. It changes nothing except to steal from us the present moment, which is the only time we truly possess."
He took another bite of the fruit, the casual action emphasizing his point.

"I could spend these seconds fearing what might come, rehearsing deaths that may never arrive. Or I could use them to grow stronger, to experience what is rather than what might be. One should simply move forward while trying their best. The outcome will be what it is, but at least we’ll meet it having used our time rather than wasted it."
The wolf-woman’s eyes blazed brighter, her muzzle pulling back in what might have been a grin if wolves could truly grin. "Good mentality!"
The approval rang genuine. "I am Silvara, Guardian of the Contemplation Groves for eight hundred cycles."
She tilted her massive head, studying him with renewed interest. "And who might you be, young thing who speaks old truths?"
"Noah," he replied simply, seeing no reason for elaborate titles in this place.
"Noah." She tested the name, rolling it around like tasting new fruit. "Since you are a bit weak, I can help you out by sharing some of my Authority."
Her smile became decidedly devilish, showing teeth that could have torn through Folds .
"I likely have more than a thousand...actually, probably ten thousand times the amount of authority you possess. I will pass some to you through a ritual."
She moved closer, her massive form radiating warmth that felt like standing near a sun. "You don’t know the ritual, so I’ll take the lead. Just continue consuming the fruits."

Without waiting for agreement, Silvara began something that predated any wonder or technique Noah had encountered. She placed one massive pawed hand on his shoulder...and began to speak in runic language!
|Ancient Ritual Detected: The Gifting of Accumulated Days- Allows Fold Dwellers to transfer accumulated complexity and purity to others. Conversion Rate: 50% efficiency.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4026: Do Nothing! II
paragraphs: The air around them began to shimmer with patterns. Silvara’s form began to glow with inner light that had nothing to do with illumination and everything to do with the weight of existence acknowledging what she had accumulated.
Streams of that light began to flow from her into Noah, each strand carrying compressed years, condensed experiences, distilled existence itself!
|Receiving Authority Transfer. Source: Silvara - Guardian of the Contemplation Groves. Transfer Amount: 100,000,000 Authority Units expended.|
|Received: 50,000,000 Complexity Quotient. Received: 50,000,000 Purity Quotient.|
HUUM!

The sensation was overwhelming. Noah felt decades flowing into him, centuries of accumulated existence compressed into moments. His cells drank in the authority like desert sand accepting rain, each particle of his being growing denser with significance!
For Silvara, expending a hundred million units of her accumulated authority seemed to be nothing more than a casual expenditure.
She didn’t even pause in her ritual, the streams of light continuing to flow.
|Additional 300,000,000 Authority Units expended. Received: 150,000,000 Complexity Quotient. Received: 150,000,000 Purity Quotient.|
Noah’s astonishment grew as he felt himself transforming at a fundamental level!
|Additional 500,000,000 Authority Units expended. Received: 250,000,000 Complexity Quotient. Received: 250,000,000 Purity Quotient!|

When Silvara finally stopped and breathed out slightly, having casually expended nine hundred million units of authority as if giving away pocket change, Noah stared at her with undisguised astonishment.
In seconds, she had granted him advancement that would have taken others yeats to achieve through conventional means.

The wolf-woman laughed at his expression, the sound warm and genuine. "Why do you look like that? We Fold Dwellers have to take care of each other." Her expression grew more serious, amber eyes reflecting depths of experience.

"There are terrifying Early Creatures out there, horrific Inevitabilities, the prideful Living Existences who look down on us as if we’re insects, and more threats than can be counted. We only have each other, so- "
Her words cut off instantly.
BOOM!
From above, a bellow erupted that made existence itself recoil. It wasn’t a sound but the concept of command given voice: "EVERYONE DEFEND! IT’S HERE!"
The mad Early Creature...had arrived.
Noah barely caught a glimpse of it, his enhanced perception managing to process perhaps a fraction of what descended upon them.

It looked like what primitive humans might have imagined their ancestors to be...a tribal figure wrapped in hides that might have been skinned from concepts themselves. But its eyes... its eyes were crimson suns that burned with madness that transcended simple insanity.
Those eyes focused on the groves, and from them erupted beams of red light that covered everything.
Everything.
The attack was too fast for anything below Duke level to even perceive, let alone react to.
Even Noah, with all his enhanced capabilities, managed only to bring the Goad up in front of him...a futile gesture against something that transcended physical or even conceptual defense!
But Silvara moved.
Without hesitation, without thought, operating on instinct older than consciousness, she threw her massive form over Noah!
Her body became a shield, her very existence a barrier between him and the crimson light.

|A concept devouring attack has been detected. Attack Type: The Devouring of Life Itself. Effect: Complete cessation of all life-related concepts in affected area. Contact Result is death in all its meanings!|
WAA!
Noah was forced to watch, and could only watch...as fear bloomed in those ancient amber eyes of Silvara.
But beneath the fear was something else...determination. Acceptance. The knowledge that this was a choice worth making.
In her fear, she smiled towards Noah as her lips opened and voiced out.
"I’ve...used my time rather than wasted it. You are young, so you...should move forward while trying your best."
Noah’s weavings buzzed as this woman...repeated the words he just said to her!
BOOM!
The crimson light hit Silvara’s form, and immediately, horrifically, she began to drain.
It wasn’t death in any conventional sense. Her very existence began to fade, life itself being torn from her in streams visible to Noah’s enhanced perception.

Her fur went from gray to white to colorless. Her eyes, those warm amber depths, became flat and empty. Her body, which had radiated warmth moments before, became cold in ways that transcended temperature.

She curled tighter around him as she died, ensuring that not even a strand of the crimson light could reach him through gaps in her protection. Her last expression, frozen on lupine features that were becoming nothing more than a husk, was fear mixed with a smile!
Because even though she did all this, she still felt fear! She still had dreams!
Within seconds, the very life of Silvara was gone, leaving nothing but an empty shell that had once housed centuries of experience, wisdom, and warmth.
|Entity: Silvara - Guardian of the Contemplation Groves. Status: Complete Cessation of Existential Circulation.|
From far above, a roar of rage and sorrow erupted...a Fold Dweller of terrifying power engaging the Early Creature in combat that shook the very foundations of this domain.
The impacts of their collision sent shockwaves through dimensions, each blow containing enough force to unmake lesser Folds

The battle raged for five minutes that felt like hours as in this time, Noah stared at the sunken lifeless face of Silvara. He could do nothing else as a glimpse of that crimson light would destroy him!
Booms of complexity clashing against madness echoed through the space, making the air itself uncertain about whether it should exist. Then, suddenly, there was only sorrowful silence.
Noah’s expression was heavy as stone that had witnessed the death of mountains.

Throughout the entire battle, he had been looking at Silvara’s face....that fearful but smiling expression that would be carved into his memory. Someone who had known him for less than minutes had given everything to preserve his existence.
All because she was a Fold Dweller, and she believed him to be so as well!
A moment later, her body began to crumble.
Not decay...even decay required life processes.
This was simple dissolution, existence forgetting that she had ever been. The husk that had been Silvara became ash, then less than ash, revealing the devastation beyond.
|Environmental Warning- Area Devoid of Life Concept. Effect: Existence degradation at 1% per second. Time until complete dissolution is 100 seconds.|

sentences.text: The air around them began to shimmer with patterns.
Silvara’s form began to glow with inner light that had nothing to do with illumination and everything to do with the weight of existence acknowledging what she had accumulated.
Streams of that light began to flow from her into Noah, each strand carrying compressed years, condensed experiences, distilled existence itself!
|Receiving Authority Transfer.
Source: Silvara - Guardian of the Contemplation Groves.
Transfer Amount: 100,000,000 Authority Units expended.|
|Received: 50,000,000 Complexity Quotient.
Received: 50,000,000 Purity Quotient.|
HUUM!
The sensation was overwhelming.
Noah felt decades flowing into him, centuries of accumulated existence compressed into moments.
His cells drank in the authority like desert sand accepting rain, each particle of his being growing denser with significance!
For Silvara, expending a hundred million units of her accumulated authority seemed to be nothing more than a casual expenditure.
She didn’t even pause in her ritual, the streams of light continuing to flow.
|Additional 300,000,000 Authority Units expended.
Received: 150,000,000 Complexity Quotient.
Received: 150,000,000 Purity Quotient.|
Noah’s astonishment grew as he felt himself transforming at a fundamental level!
|Additional 500,000,000 Authority Units expended.
Received: 250,000,000 Complexity Quotient.
Received: 250,000,000 Purity Quotient!|

When Silvara finally stopped and breathed out slightly, having casually expended nine hundred million units of authority as if giving away pocket change, Noah stared at her with undisguised astonishment.
In seconds, she had granted him advancement that would have taken others yeats to achieve through conventional means.
The wolf-woman laughed at his expression, the sound warm and genuine.
"Why do you look like that?
We Fold Dwellers have to take care of each other." Her expression grew more serious, amber eyes reflecting depths of experience.
"There are terrifying Early Creatures out there, horrific Inevitabilities, the prideful Living Existences who look down on us as if we’re insects, and more threats than can be counted.
We only have each other, so- "
Her words cut off instantly.
BOOM!
From above, a bellow erupted that made existence itself recoil.
It wasn’t a sound but the concept of command given voice: "EVERYONE DEFEND!
IT’S HERE!"
The mad Early Creature...had arrived.
Noah barely caught a glimpse of it, his enhanced perception managing to process perhaps a fraction of what descended upon them.
It looked like what primitive humans might have imagined their ancestors to be...a tribal figure wrapped in hides that might have been skinned from concepts themselves.
But its eyes... its eyes were crimson suns that burned with madness that transcended simple insanity.
Those eyes focused on the groves, and from them erupted beams of red light that covered everything.
Everything.
The attack was too fast for anything below Duke level to even perceive, let alone react to.
Even Noah, with all his enhanced capabilities, managed only to bring the Goad up in front of him...a futile gesture against something that transcended physical or even conceptual defense!
But Silvara moved.
Without hesitation, without thought, operating on instinct older than consciousness, she threw her massive form over Noah!
Her body became a shield, her very existence a barrier between him and the crimson light.
|A concept devouring attack has been detected.
Attack Type: The Devouring of Life Itself.
Effect: Complete cessation of all life-related concepts in affected area.
Contact Result is death in all its meanings!|
WAA!
Noah was forced to watch, and could only watch...as fear bloomed in those ancient amber eyes of Silvara.
But beneath the fear was something else...determination.
Acceptance.
The knowledge that this was a choice worth making.
In her fear, she smiled towards Noah as her lips opened and voiced out.
"I’ve...used my time rather than wasted it.
You are young, so you...should move forward while trying your best."
Noah’s weavings buzzed as this woman...repeated the words he just said to her!
BOOM!
The crimson light hit Silvara’s form, and immediately, horrifically, she began to drain.
It wasn’t death in any conventional sense.
Her very existence began to fade, life itself being torn from her in streams visible to Noah’s enhanced perception.
Her fur went from gray to white to colorless.
Her eyes, those warm amber depths, became flat and empty.
Her body, which had radiated warmth moments before, became cold in ways that transcended temperature.
She curled tighter around him as she died, ensuring that not even a strand of the crimson light could reach him through gaps in her protection.
Her last expression, frozen on lupine features that were becoming nothing more than a husk, was fear mixed with a smile!
Because even though she did all this, she still felt fear!
She still had dreams!
Within seconds, the very life of Silvara was gone, leaving nothing but an empty shell that had once housed centuries of experience, wisdom, and warmth.
|Entity: Silvara - Guardian of the Contemplation Groves.
Status: Complete Cessation of Existential Circulation.|
From far above, a roar of rage and sorrow erupted...a Fold Dweller of terrifying power engaging the Early Creature in combat that shook the very foundations of this domain.
The impacts of their collision sent shockwaves through dimensions, each blow containing enough force to unmake lesser Folds
The battle raged for five minutes that felt like hours as in this time, Noah stared at the sunken lifeless face of Silvara.
He could do nothing else as a glimpse of that crimson light would destroy him!
Booms of complexity clashing against madness echoed through the space, making the air itself uncertain about whether it should exist.
Then, suddenly, there was only sorrowful silence.
Noah’s expression was heavy as stone that had witnessed the death of mountains.
Throughout the entire battle, he had been looking at Silvara’s face....that fearful but smiling expression that would be carved into his memory.
Someone who had known him for less than minutes had given everything to preserve his existence.
All because she was a Fold Dweller, and she believed him to be so as well!
A moment later, her body began to crumble.
Not decay...even decay required life processes.
This was simple dissolution, existence forgetting that she had ever been.
The husk that had been Silvara became ash, then less than ash, revealing the devastation beyond.
|Environmental Warning- Area Devoid of Life Concept.
Effect: Existence degradation at 1% per second.
Time until complete dissolution is 100 seconds.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4027: Do Nothing! III
paragraphs: The grove...that monument to impossible agriculture, was gone. In its place was nothing.
The trees hadn’t been destroyed; the concept of their growth had been devoured. The soil hadn’t been scorched; the idea of fertility had been consumed.
Noah looked up through the absence where beauty had been and witnessed something that transcended his understanding.
The First Farmer stood in the space above, holding a farming hoe that looked simple except for how reality bent around it in reverence. The tool dripped with something that might have been blood.

At his feet, or what served as feet for a being of his scale, lay the massive leg of an Early Creature, severed at the thigh. Crimson-gold droplets gushed from it like rivers, each drop containing enough authority to create or destroy Folds!
But it was the Farmer’s expression that struck Noah.
Viltharion, the One Who Gazed Upon THE Living Spirit, was crying!
Stellar tears rolled down features that had been carved by eons of patient work, each drop containing the condensed sorrow of watching everything he had built be destroyed in moments.
When he spoke, his voice carried the weight of grief transformed into rage!
"Why must it be like this?"
HUUUM!
The question rang through the devastated space, making even the absence of things pause to listen.

"We till the soil of existence. We plant. We nurture! We ask for nothing but the right to grow our crops in peace. Yet Early Creatures hunt us for sport or madness. Living Existences look down upon us as if we are insects unworthy of consideration. Inevitabilities unmake us for the crime of existing without paradox."
His grip on the hoe tightened, and reality cracked around his fingers.

"We have no Glyphs to protect us. No Authority beyond what time grants through simple endurance. We are the forgotten children of existence, neither transcendent enough to matter nor insignificant enough to be ignored!"
The tears continued to fall, but his voice grew stronger, angrier!

"But I will change things. I WILL change the position of Fold Dwellers, even if I have to hide them in the spaces between Folds themselves! Even if I have to dig beneath Existence to plant gardens where no Early Creature can reach! Even if I have to cultivate Principles in darkness until we become something that cannot be hunted!"
HUUM!
His roar shook the foundations of the domain as in his bellows and rage...he sensed life.
His gaze fell upon Noah...the sole survivor of the carnage.
The anger in those ancient eyes transformed into pity.

"Child," he said, his voice gentling despite the rage that still burned within, "you cannot remain here any longer. You will perish in seconds in a place devoid of the concept of life itself. I will send you...far from here."
He raised the hoe, and reality prepared to obey whatever command would follow.

"If I succeed in my goals, I will save you and all other Fold Dwellers. We will have our place in existence, our safety, our right to simply be." His expression grew complex, mixing determination with sorrow. "For now, take the latest result of my failures, and some fond memories..."
With these words, Viltharion waved his hand. Light erupted around Noah...encompassing, wrapping him in complexity so dense it formed a cocoon of pure authority.
The last thing Noah saw was the First Farmer standing amid devastation, tears still falling as he gazed at farmland that would never grow again.
Never again!
Then space folded, and Noah was elsewhere.
|Your existence has been wrapped by extremely complex authority for Emergency Evacuation across Fold Boundaries. Destination is random.|

|Item Received: Failed Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest- Viltharion’s attempt to cultivate a Principle that would allow infinite growth without depletion. Status: Incomplete - Missing crucial understanding. Can be completed with proper knowledge or materials.|
Prompts flashed amidst a storm of authority!

As Noah tumbled through spaces between spaces, the weight of what he had witnessed settled into his bones. He had sought advancement and found tragedy! He had gained power through sacrifice he never asked for!
And somewhere in the Earliest Folds, a Farmer continued to cry over fields that would never bloom again, planning revolution that would echo through the Folds!
It was enough for him to ask...why things were the way they were in the current Era.
Where...were the powerful Fold Dwellers?!
Where was the First Farmer?!

As his existence buzzed, he appeared in the new region with a sensation like being spat out by existence itself. His feet found purchase on ground that might have been stone or crystallized thought, and for a moment, he simply stood there, expression heavy as mountains that had witnessed too much.
Before he could process his surroundings, prompts continued to cascade across his vision.

|Additional Items Transferred by Viltharion, the First Farmer. Seed of the Tender’s Tree- One of the first successful seeds Viltharion cultivated after meeting THE Living Spirit. When planted and matured: Produces small humanoid lifeforms that exist solely to tend farming plots. Lifeforms possess no consciousness but perfect agricultural instinctm Each tree can produce 10 Tenders per cycle.|

|Seed of the Singular Prosperity Grass. A culmination of early experiments in concentrated growth. Produces a single blade of grass after 100 days. Consumption grants: +1,000,000,000 Complexity and +1,000,000,000 Purity Quotient.|
Noah gazed at the seeds materializing in his palm with an expression that mixed gratitude with something far more complex. The weight of them felt wrong... emotionally.
These weren’t just gifts; they were inheritance from someone who might never fulfill their own dreams.
He had made tremendous gains in the Earliest Folds so far in the midst of terrifying danger.
His complexity had soared, yet his existence felt sour, like fruit that had ripened in shadow rather than sunlight.
Silvara’s face burned in his mind...that final expression of fear mixed with determination, with that smile that said she regretted nothing.
She had known him for minutes at most, yet had given everything.
Everything.
What was her Everything worth?
The weight of that sacrifice pressed against his consciousness.

Threnvar, who had saved him, whom he hadn’t even seen die. Had the Keeper of the Eighth Perimeter fallen in those first seconds of crimson light? Or had he survived only to witness the devastation of everything he had sworn to protect?
The Mad Early Creature itself...that thing that moved while devouring entire concepts from areas, leaving behind nothing but absence!
Noah’s eyes burned with anger. It was the kind of rage that could fuel centuries of purpose!
But overshadowing even that was the image of the First Farmer, tears streaming down his ancient face as he stood over devastation with the severed leg of an Early Creature at his feet.
Viltharion had actually pushed away an Early Creature, had made it lose a limb...a feat that should have been impossible for a Fold Dweller.
All of them were unfathomably powerful by any reasonable measure, yet power hadn’t been enough.
It was never enough when the disparities were so vast.
How had Noah managed to survive when beings far greater had fallen?!

chapters.title: Chapter 4028: Do Nothing! IV
paragraphs: Through sacrifice. He had simply survived through sacrifice as it was not his power that saved him.
The visage of the Mad Early Creature flashed in his mind’s eye...those crimson suns that served as eyes, that tribal figure wrapped in conceptual hides.
If that thing still existed somewhere in the current era, when Noah became strong enough...
He would hunt it. Not for glory or advancement, but for the one who sacrificed!
But for now, he was far too feeble.
The gap between his current power and what would be needed was measured in epochs.

He grasped the Goad tighter, the Rearing Stick of the Early Creature providing a sense of safety that might have been illusory but was necessary nonetheless. The simple stick hummed with recognition of where they were, when they were.
Noah finally looked around properly, his body continuing to draw in the atmospheric authority of the Earliest Folds.
His complexity and purity increased with each breath, each heartbeat adding to his accumulated power. The environment revealed itself gradually, and what he saw made his Existence freeze.
"Fuck me..."
HUUM!
The curse escaped before he could stop it, the word hanging in air that had witnessed the birth of profanity itself.

He stood in an obsidian region that stretched beyond perception. The ground beneath his feet was black glass that reflected nothing, as if light itself was too afraid to touch it. Viscous rivers of something that might have been liquid paradox flowed in patterns that hurt to follow, their contents simultaneously existing and not existing.
But it was what he saw in the distance that truly stole his breath.
Inevitabilities.
Fucking Inevitabilities!
But not the writhing, tentacled monstrosities he had encountered before. These were different. Ancient. Original.
Some looked like massive slumbering bipedal beasts made of wriggling tentacles, but the tentacles were composed of contradictions given form.

Others appeared as massive humanoid creatures whose very existence challenged the concept of shape...they were human and not human, beast and not beast, existing in states that predated the separation between categories.
All of them... were slumbering. Their massive forms rose like mountains of impossibility, each breath they took in sleep causing reality to question itself.
Noah almost cursed the First Farmer. Why had his random teleportation sent him here of all places?

The moment he made any significant movement, the moment he disturbed their slumber, these Original Inevitabilities would locate him and he would experience a death that might unmake his very conception.
He had to-...!
"What a foul mouth you have. The little kids are currently in deep slumber, so you don’t have to worry, Outsider."
BOOM!
The voice that suddenly spoke behind him was terrifyingly sweet, like honey poured over sharpened steel.
Noah’s entire being seized as he hadn’t sensed anything!
His enhanced perception, his Early Creature nature, none of it had warned him of approach.
No prompts either from the Weaver of Existence, Atlas, or Shore!
He turned with careful control, each movement deliberate and non-threatening.
And behind him was...
A woman?
A woman!

The woman who stood there defied every assumption about what beauty could be. Her skin was fair in a way that suggested she had never known sunlight. Her hair was darkness itself given form, flowing in waves that had no end. But it was her dress that truly commanded attention...silky black fabric that didn’t just cover her form but extended across the entire obsidian region, as if she wore the landscape itself.
Noah’s existence buzzed with warnings. This was something that shouldn’t be observed directly, like staring into the concept of ending before endings had been defined.
His weavings moved toward the mental trigger that would cut short his traversal of the Earliest Folds. He could leave. Should leave. Immediately!
But before he could activate the return, he forced himself to speak with stern caution that barely masked his preparation to flee.
"Who... are you?"
A stupid question. And he knew it was stupid, but sometimes, one had to act stupid to survive a bit longer!
She smiled, and that simple expression contained depths that could drown civilizations.
"Of course....I am an Inevitability."
The words were delivered with the casual certainty of someone stating that water was wet, that fire burned, that existence existed.
Yet Noah instinctively moved backward, his body reacting before his Existence!
The woman watched his retreat with amusement that danced in eyes he now noticed were wrong.
Her pupils weren’t single points but layers...multiple folds of space-time collapsed into where eyes should be, showing depths that led to everywhere and nowhere simultaneously.

"It seems you fear me," she observed, her voice carrying playful reproach, "and also don’t, Outsider. You arrive in my home unannounced, and you act like I am the terrifying monstrosity? You are the intruder here."
Noah grasped his stick tighter, the Goad’s presence helping calm his racing thoughts as much as anything could in this situation.
"I apologize for trespassing," he managed, his voice steadier than he felt. "As for the fear..."
He paused, choosing his words with care that suggested he understood he was balanced on the edge of an blade.
"As far as I know, Inevitabilities are creatures that devour endlessly. Beings that seek Everything. So naturally, I feared."
The woman tilted her head with a tease that would have been charming if not for how reality tilted with her, maintaining her as the center of existence regardless of angle.
"But... I don’t want your Everything, though?"
She looked at the pulsing masses of slumbering Inevitabilities surrounding them, her expression growing fond in the way one might look at sleeping children.

"Well, I guess these little ones would want to devour you endlessly, but you seem to have a misunderstanding about Inevitabilities." Her attention returned to him, those layered-fold eyes containing invitation and threat in equal measure. "Do you have time for a story, Outsider?"
WAA!
Noah’s mind raced through calculations of risk and opportunity. Internally, he queried his Atlas, asking how quickly he would be returned to his current time if he decided to leave early.
|Early Traversal Return Speed: Instantaneous. Warning- When facing beings of sufficient power, even instants can be stretched into eons|
|Current entity threat level...Best not to think about it. Hope for the best|

chapters.title: Chapter 4029: Do Nothing! V
paragraphs: After a moment of deliberation that felt like hours, Noah looked at the terrifying woman with caution that bordered on resignation.
"I... should have some time."
Her smile grew dangerously as she nodded.
"Let me tell you about existence, Outsider. About the real existence, before definitions and categories and all the pretty boxes that later arrivals created."
She moved.
She did not walk, she simply existed in a slightly different position...closer to him, though maintaining distance that suggested respect for his obvious wariness.
"Imagine," she began, her voice taking on the cadence of ancient glory "lifeforms waking up day in and day out, harmoniously carrying out their way of existence."
She paused, letting the words settle.
"Their Way of Existence. Not chosen, not decided, simply what they were. It was natural. It was Existence. It was theirs."
Her expression grew complex, mixing nostalgia with something that might have been sorrow if Inevitabilities could truly feel such things.

"But then, at a certain point, other lifeforms appeared. The First Lifeforms...my kind, the Original Inevitabilities, simply sought to continue their Way of Existence. We consumed because that was our nature, we devoured because that was our function, we sought Everything because that was what we were."
The landscape around them seemed to respond to her words, the obsidian ground rippling with memories older than time.

"But the new lifeforms looked at us with horror. They said our Way of Existence was wrong. Horrid. Monstrous." Her voice carried no anger, only a kind of bewildered hurt. "These new lifeforms began hunting and killing the First Lifeforms as they imposed their Way of Existence. They had all these ideals for what Existence was. What Existence should be. What the Way of Existence for everyone should be."
She looked directly at Noah then, those layered eyes containing challenge and genuine curiosity.

"Tell me, Outsider. Are these New Lifeforms not terrible? Coming later, but deeming everything before them as wrong? Deciding that the Way of Existence of those who came before them was incorrect simply because... it didn’t match their preferences?"
Her smile grew dangerous as Noah remained utterly serious, his mind racing through the implications of her words.

"Inevitabilities," she continued, "simply have their Way of Existence. It is who we are, as fundamental as gravity pulling or light illuminating. Inevitabilities have been here before THE Creature. Before Early Creatures. Before Living Existences or Fold Dwellers."
She gestured to the slumbering giants around them.

"How arrogant they are. How great the ego and tyranny of these new lifeforms to look at the Way of Existence of Inevitabilities and deem it unnatural. Don’t they know how much chaos and disorder their Ways of Existence bring forth? They create rules then break them, establish order then rebel against it, define love then wage war over it."
Her expression grew genuinely sad then, an emotion that seemed wrong on features designed for inevitability rather than feeling.
"It is... disheartening."
Noah stood frozen from the weight of perspective being forcibly shifted.
He remained silent.
He looked at a terrifying Inevitability that he absolutely was not able to classify as his existence buzzed.
The timer on his traversal showed [42:18 remaining], but he wondered if he would leave this encounter intact, regardless of when he departed!
The woman...the Inevitability, waited for his response with patience that suggested she had all the time that had ever been or would ever be!

Noah considered the words of the terrifying Inevitability before him, his mind parsing through layers of meaning that challenged fundamental assumptions. After a moment of contemplation, he spoke with careful precision.
"You may be right. Inevitabilities have their Way of Existence."
He paused, then gestured toward the slumbering giants that surrounded them like mountains of contradiction.
"But what of my Way of Existence? If I were to meet any of these Inevitabilities right now..." He pointed directly at the nearest sleeping form, its tentacles writhing even in slumber.
"Their Way of Existence would be to devour me. But my Way of Existence is to very much remain alive. To prosper. To grow."
His voice grew firmer as he continued, finding solid ground in his argument.
"So Inevitabilities would directly conflict with my Way of Existence. Who gets to determine whose Way of Existence is more important? Who decides which nature takes precedence when they clash?"
He met those layered-fold eyes without flinching, though every instinct screamed at him to look away.
"I believe my own Way of Existence to be of paramount importance...at least to me. So what am I to do if faced with the Way of Existence of an Inevitability that sees me as something to be consumed?"
The woman’s smile deepened in response, carrying the weight of secrets that predated secrets.
"But," she said, her voice lilting with amusement, "the Way of Existence of Inevitabilities does not conflict with yours or any other lifeform’s."
HUUM!

Noah blinked, his enhanced perception trying to process what seemed like an obvious contradiction. He looked around at the massive forms of sleeping Inevitabilities, then back at her with barely concealed smile.
"Ma’am, what the hell are you talking about?"
Her smile grew dangerous. "Yes, Inevitabilities seek Everything, but... not really. I could even show you here, if you trust me."
Did he trust an Inevitability? The answer was absolutely, categorically, fundamentally not.
Yet even as every fiber of his being screamed rejection, the woman tapped one delicate finger against the obsidian ground.
The sound that resulted shouldn’t have been audible, yet it rang through the space like a bell that existed before sound.
One of the rumbling bodies stirred.
An Inevitability arose!
Ah!
The Inevitability that rose from slumber defied rational observation. Its form was contradiction incarnate...simultaneously massive and minuscule, ancient and newly born, terrible and beautiful.
Tentacles that might have been arms that might have been concepts writhed from a central mass that couldn’t decide if it was flesh or thought or the space between both.
But it was the eyes that commanded attention. Hundreds of them, thousands, each one containing a different definition of sight. They all turned toward Noah with the weight of inevitable attention.
The wild and terrifying aura that erupted from it exceeded any Duke he had encountered.
Noah knew with absolute certainty that he could not outrun this thing. Even the instant it would take to activate his return to the present wouldn’t be fast enough.
"Here," the woman said with the calm of someone conducting a lesson, "is an Inevitability whose Way of Existence is to devour Everything."
The creature began moving toward them...toward Noah with purpose that transcended simple hunger.

"When it sees you, it will come to devour. All I ask you to do... is nothing." Her words were delivered with the certainty of someone stating fundamental law. "Do not make a movement. Do not fight back."
HUUM!
